# Overview



This page introduces **Morph2Mol**, a foundation model that predicts single-cell spatial gene expression directly from H&E histology images. Here you will learn what problem the project solves, the core ideas behind its design, how the repository is organized, and where to go next in the documentation. This page stays at the conceptual level — hands-on commands and deep internals live in later pages.

## What Morph2Mol Does

Morph2Mol answers a concrete question in computational pathology: given a stained tissue image, what genes is each individual cell expressing? The system takes a whole-slide H&E image, finds every cell nucleus, extracts a small image crop around each cell, and produces a per-cell expression score across 18,580 model genes — without requiring any measured expression on the target slide ([README.md](/README.md#L1-L3), [README.md](/README.md#L44-L53)). The project is distributed as an installable Python package `morph2mol` (version 0.3.0, Python ≥ 3.10) built on PyTorch 2.6+, together with ready-to-run `predict/` and `train/` driver scripts ([pyproject.toml](/pyproject.toml#L6-L16), [requirements.txt](/requirements.txt#L1-L12)).

The central insight of the design is **retrieval-augmented prediction**. A pure image-to-expression model produces a *direct* score, but the system also keeps a *reference bank* of cells whose expression was actually measured (from platforms like Xenium or CosMx). At inference time, each target cell's image embedding retrieves the 50 most visually similar reference cell clusters, and their measured expression is blended with the direct prediction ([README.md](/README.md#L109), [predict/predict.py](/predict/predict.py#L177-L188)). This means spatial expression predictions are grounded in real measured data whenever a similar tissue has been profiled before.

## Key Capabilities at a Glance

| Capability | What it means | Where it lives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Automatic nuclei segmentation | Cellpose-SAM finds nuclei in the whole slide, handling slide-size images via overlapping windows | `predict/segment.py` |
| Direct expression prediction | Image → gene scores for 18,580 genes via a 25M-parameter model (`Morph2Mol-25M-scGPT`) | `predict/model.py`, `morph2mol/head.py` |
| Reference retrieval | Cosine search over a bank of ~100-cell clusters with measured expression | `morph2mol/retrieval.py` |
| Per-gene gated fusion | `X = beta*A + (1-beta)*R`, with weights fitted per organ and gene | `morph2mol/gate.py` |
| Streaming output | Results written incrementally to `.h5ad` so memory stays bounded | `predict/predict.py` |
| Release integrity | SHA-256 checksums verify checkpoints, gene space, bank, and fusion weights all match | `morph2mol/release.py` |
| Tissue-aware weights | Fusion weights for 15 organs in `narrow`/`wide` panel groups (20 organ/panel groups total) | `morph2mol/tissue.py`, `weights/` |

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L68-L88), [predict/predict.py](/predict/predict.py#L117-L122), [predict/segment.py](/predict/segment.py#L1-L28), [weights/README.md](/weights/README.md#L29-L31)

## How It Works: The Big Picture

The diagram below shows the full inference flow. Two branches run in parallel — the **direct branch** (a neural network predicting expression from images) and the **retrieval branch** (nearest-neighbor lookup into measured expression) — and their outputs are fused per gene. Before reading it, note the three model components you will meet repeatedly: the *frozen UNI2-h image encoder with trainable LoRA adapters*, the *SE(2) spatial decoder that attends over cell neighborhoods within 137 µm*, and the *negative-binomial expression head with scGPT-initialized gene embeddings*.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    A["H&E whole-slide image<br/>(SVS/TIFF/PNG/JPEG)"] --> B["Cellpose-SAM<br/>nuclei segmentation"]
    B --> C["Cell crops + masks<br/>(55 µm context)"]
    C --> D["UNI2-h ViT-huge encoder<br/>+ LoRA adapters"]
    D -->|"1536-d pooled features"| E["SE(2) spatial transformer<br/>6 layers · 256 dim · 137 µm radius"]
    E --> F["Negative-binomial head<br/>18,580 genes"]
    F --> G["Direct scores A<br/>= log1p(mu)"]
    D -->|"Stage-1 embedding"| H["Reference bank<br/>~100-cell clusters with<br/>measured expression"]
    H -->|"K=50 · tau=0.03<br/>cosine retrieval"| I["Retrieved scores R"]
    G --> J["Per-gene gated fusion<br/>X = beta·A + (1−beta)·R"]
    I --> J
    J --> K[("Output .h5ad<br/>X + layers A/R + spatial coords")]
```

The **direct branch** works as follows: each 55 µm cell crop is encoded by UNI2-h (a ViT-huge vision transformer, frozen), with small low-rank LoRA matrices injected into the attention layers of the last encoder blocks to adapt it to histology ([morph2mol/encoder.py](/morph2mol/encoder.py#L9-L21), [morph2mol/encoder.py](/morph2mol/encoder.py#L29-L40)). Cell-level features come from mask-weighted pooling over the encoder's patch tokens, so segmentation boundaries decide which image evidence belongs to which cell ([predict/segment.py](/predict/segment.py#L25-L27)). A six-layer spatial transformer then lets each target cell attend to up to 128 target + 64 context neighbors within 137 µm, using pairwise distances in microns through a learned Gaussian kernel ([morph2mol/se2.py](/morph2mol/se2.py#L7-L13), [README.md](/README.md#L57)). Finally, the negative-binomial head converts cell embeddings into per-gene mean rates `mu`, conditioned on absolute and relative cell area, and predictions are returned in `log1p(mu)` scale ([morph2mol/head.py](/morph2mol/head.py#L24-L40), [predict/model.py](/predict/model.py#L64-L68)).

The **retrieval branch** treats prediction as a lookup problem. The reference bank stores, for each ~100-cell cluster of previously measured cells, a 1536-dim image-embedding key (from Stage 1 training) plus the cluster's measured expression for the genes it covers ([morph2mol/retrieval.py](/morph2mol/retrieval.py#L120-L149)). Each target cell retrieves its 50 nearest clusters by exact fp16 cosine similarity, and cluster scores are combined with exponential weights at temperature 0.03 ([morph2mol/retrieval.py](/morph2mol/retrieval.py#L170-L200)). A per-gene **gate** then blends the two branches: `beta` weights were fitted offline on reference slides (never on the target), and genes without retrieval coverage fall back to the direct prediction ([morph2mol/gate.py](/morph2mol/gate.py#L83-L105), [README.md](/README.md#L109)).

Both branches are trained in two stages on paired H&E images and measured spatial expression. **Stage 1** aligns image features with scGPT RNA cell embeddings using a symmetric contrastive loss (temperature 0.07) — this is what makes image and expression spaces comparable for retrieval. **Stage 2** trains the spatial decoder and expression head with a negative-binomial objective, reusing the Stage 1 LoRA weights as initialization ([docs/training.md](/docs/training.md#L58-L97)). The reference bank and fusion weights are then built from the training corpus in separate steps ([docs/training.md](/docs/training.md#L99-L150)).

Sources: [morph2mol/encoder.py](/morph2mol/encoder.py#L9-L40), [morph2mol/se2.py](/morph2mol/se2.py#L7-L22), [morph2mol/head.py](/morph2mol/head.py#L24-L40), [morph2mol/retrieval.py](/morph2mol/retrieval.py#L120-L149), [morph2mol/gate.py](/morph2mol/gate.py#L83-L105), [predict/model.py](/predict/model.py#L13-L68), [docs/training.md](/docs/training.md#L58-L150)

## Repository Layout

The repository separates the **importable library** (`morph2mol/`) from the **command-line drivers** that call it (`predict/` for inference, `train/` for training). Tests and documentation sit at the top level, and the `weights/` directory ships gene symbol lists used to define the model's gene space.

```text
Morph2Mol/
├── morph2mol/          # Core library: model components, retrieval, gating, release
│   ├── encoder.py      #   UNI2-h builder + LoRA injection
│   ├── se2.py          #   SE(2) spatial transformer decoder
│   ├── head.py         #   Negative-binomial expression head
│   ├── retrieval.py    #   ReferenceBank: cluster retrieval engine
│   ├── gate.py         #   Per-gene fusion weight fitting + application
│   ├── release.py      #   Portable release loading + integrity checks
│   ├── scgpt_backend/  #   Vendored scGPT RNA embedding backend
│   └── training/       #   Stage 1 / Stage 2 training logic
├── predict/            # Inference CLI: segmentation, I/O, context, streaming output
├── train/              # Training drivers: prepare → phase1 → phase2 → bank → beta
├── configs/            # Example release configuration
├── docs/               # Training guide + input/output format specs
├── tests/              # Gene-table and prediction-compatibility tests
├── weights/            # Model gene symbol lists (genes.tsv, xenium_genes.tsv)
├── voice/              # Backward-compatible namespace alias
└── pyproject.toml      # Package metadata (morph2mol v0.3.0)
```

A useful detail for readers tracing older code or checkpoints: the package once shipped under a different name, and compatibility is preserved explicitly — the inference model class exposes `Voice25M = Morph2Mol` as an alias, and both `morph2mol-release-v1` and `voice25m-release-v1` schemas are accepted by the release loader ([predict/model.py](/predict/model.py#L71-L72), [morph2mol/release.py](/morph2mol/release.py#L11-L12)). The `morph2mol` package itself is importable without the driver scripts: everything from encoder construction to gated fusion is a library function you can call directly ([pyproject.toml](/pyproject.toml#L16-L19)).

## Verification and Reproducibility

Every prediction run is anchored to an auditable *release directory* containing `release.json`, the two stage checkpoints, the gene space, fusion weights, and the reference bank ([weights/README.md](/weights/README.md#L5-L27)). When a release is loaded, the system recomputes SHA-256 hashes of the stage checkpoints and gene space, cross-checks the bank's cache fingerprint against the gate metadata, and refuses to run if checkpoints, genes, bank, and fusion weights disagree ([morph2mol/release.py](/morph2mol/release.py#L21-L45)). These identities are also recorded in the output file's metadata (`stage1_sha256`, `stage2_sha256`, `gene_space_sha256`, `bank_fingerprint`), so any result can be traced back to the exact artifacts that produced it ([predict/predict.py](/predict/predict.py#L117-L122), [predict/predict.py](/predict/predict.py#L189-L197)).

Tissue handling follows the same "no silent assumptions" philosophy: organ names are user-supplied annotations in a `sample,tissue` CSV, matched case-insensitively, and related donor/block samples are transitively excluded from reference banks when fitting fusion weights — preventing a sample from "predicting itself" ([morph2mol/tissue.py](/morph2mol/tissue.py#L22-L56), [README.md](/README.md#L78)).

## What to Read Next

For a beginner-friendly progression through this catalog:

1. **[Quick Start](2-quick-start)** — install, download the model, and run your first prediction end to end.
2. **[Inference CLI Reference](3-inference-cli-reference)** — every `predict/predict.py` flag explained, from `--tissue` to memory controls.
3. **[Reading Prediction Outputs](4-reading-prediction-outputs)** — how to interpret the `.h5ad` fields (`X`, layers `A`/`R`, `var['beta']`, embeddings).
4. **[Architecture Overview](5-architecture-overview)** — the full component map before diving into individual modules.
5. Then follow the Deep Dive order: model components ([Image Encoder and LoRA Adapters](6-image-encoder-and-lora-adapters), [SE(2) Distance Attention Decoder](7-se-2-distance-attention-decoder), [Negative-Binomial Expression Head](8-negative-binomial-expression-head), [scGPT RNA Embedding Backend](9-scgpt-rna-embedding-backend)), retrieval-augmented prediction ([Reference Bank Construction](10-reference-bank-construction), [Cluster Retrieval Mechanics](11-cluster-retrieval-mechanics), [Gated Fusion Weights](12-gated-fusion-weights)), and finally training and inference engineering.

> [!TIP]
> The single most important sentence in this codebase's README for interpreting results: combined scores `X = beta*A + (1-beta)*R` describe *variation across cells within each gene* — they are not molecule counts ([README.md](/README.md#L109)).

> [!TIP]
> Segmentation quality directly bounds prediction quality: the per-cell feature is a mask-weighted average over encoder patches, so the boundary decides which image evidence is attributed to each cell. If you have your own cell boundaries (e.g., paired with a spatial assay), pass them via `--cells` instead of relying on automatic segmentation ([predict/segment.py](/predict/segment.py#L25-L27), [README.md](/README.md#L70)).


# Quick Start



This page takes you from a fresh clone of Morph2Mol to your first predicted single-cell expression matrix. Morph2Mol predicts spatial single-cell gene expression directly from H&E histology images: an image encoder reads cell-centered crops, a spatial decoder produces direct expression predictions, and a reference bank of cells with measured expression refines those predictions through retrieval and gated fusion. You need no measured expression and no precomputed image features for your target slide — only the image itself and the downloaded model release.

By the end of this page you will have: a working Python environment, a verified model release directory under `models/morph2mol`, a `results/prediction.h5ad` file readable with `anndata`, and enough CLI familiarity to adapt the workflow to your own slides.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L1-L3)

## What You Need Before Starting

| Requirement | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Python | **3.10 or later** (enforced by `requires-python` in `pyproject.toml`) |
| PyTorch | `torch>=2.6,<3`; install a CUDA build matching your GPU, or run CPU-only |
| GPU | CUDA is the default device; CPU works with `--device cpu --amp fp32` |
| Model access | Public Hugging Face repo `zchx/Morph2Mol` **plus** separately gated access to `MahmoodLab/UNI2-h` (the image-encoder backbone) |
| Slide formats | SVS, NDPI, MRXS via OpenSlide; PNG, JPEG, TIFF also supported |

The UNI2-h gating step is the one prerequisite beginners most often miss: the Morph2Mol download alone is not enough, because the encoder checkpoint `pytorch_model.bin` must be fetched from MahmoodLab's gated repository with an account that has been granted access. Apply for access before you start; approval is not instantaneous.

Sources: [pyproject.toml](/pyproject.toml#L6-L10), [requirements.txt](/requirements.txt#L1-L13), [README.md](/README.md#L13-L25), [weights/README.md](/weights/README.md#L1-L4)

## Step 1: Install the Environment

Clone the repository and install the pinned dependency set. The requirements file locks the inference stack: `torch>=2.6`, `timm==1.0.16`, `cellpose==4.2.1.1` (segmentation), `anndata>=0.10` (output format), `huggingface_hub` (model download), plus `numpy`, `pandas`, `scipy`, `Pillow`, `h5py`, `tifffile`, and OpenCV.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zchxhcz1/Morph2Mol.git
cd Morph2Mol
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

If you plan to use SVS, NDPI, or MRXS whole-slide images, also install the OpenSlide system library and `openslide-python`. Large slides should use an OpenSlide-readable format so the image is windowed rather than loaded whole into memory; plain PNG or JPEG works for smaller images. The package itself is declared in `pyproject.toml` as version 0.3.0 covering the `morph2mol`, `predict`, `train`, and `voice` packages.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L13-L25), [requirements.txt](/requirements.txt#L1-L13), [pyproject.toml](/pyproject.toml#L14-L17)

## Step 2: Download the Model Release

A **release** is a portable directory that bundles everything inference needs: checkpoints, gene information, fusion weights, and the reference bank. Authenticate once, then download both model parts into `models/morph2mol`:

```bash
hf auth login
python - <<'PYTHON'
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download, hf_hub_download

model_dir = "models/morph2mol"
snapshot_download("zchx/Morph2Mol", local_dir=model_dir)
hf_hub_download("MahmoodLab/UNI2-h", "pytorch_model.bin", local_dir=f"{model_dir}/uni2h")
PYTHON
```

Keep the release directory intact and together — the loader cross-checks its contents against each other, as described below.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L27-L44), [weights/README.md](/weights/README.md#L1-L4)

## Inside the Release Directory

The complete directory consumed by `--release` looks like this:

```text
models/morph2mol/
  release.json          # manifest: relative paths + checksums (schema morph2mol-release-v1)
  stage1.pt             # Stage 1 retrieval/alignment checkpoint
  stage2.pt             # Stage 2 expression checkpoint
  gene_space.npz        # model gene space (18,580 genes)
  xenium_genes.tsv      # ordered Xenium panel gene list
  beta.json             # combined fusion weights, all organ/panel groups
  beta.meta.json        # fusion-weight metadata
  beta/                 # per-group gene-weight tables (e.g. lung/narrow.json)
  uni2h/pytorch_model.bin   # UNI2-h encoder weights (downloaded separately)
  bank/                 # reference bank: summaries per reference object
```

| Artifact | Role at inference |
| --- | --- |
| `stage1.pt`, `stage2.pt` | The two model checkpoints whose SHA-256 hashes are recorded in `release.json` |
| `gene_space.npz` | Defines the model gene head your `--genes` selection must draw from |
| `beta.json` + `beta/` | Fusion weights; the root file is used automatically, per-group tables under `beta/ORGAN/WIDTH.json` |
| `bank/` | Reference cells with measured expression used for retrieval-augmented refinement |

The example config `configs/release.example.json` shows the same contract: keys `uni2h`, `stage1`, `stage2`, `gene_space`, `xenium_genes`, `bank`, and `gate` under schema `morph2mol-release-v1`. When prediction starts, the `Release` loader checks that every required artifact exists, verifies recorded SHA-256 checksums, and confirms that the bank, fusion weights, and checkpoints all reference the same model identity — if any of these fail you get a fast, explicit error rather than silent wrong predictions. A deeper treatment belongs to [Release Integrity Verification](21-release-integrity-verification).

> [!TIP]
> Never mix files between release directories. The loader cross-checks `checkpoint_sha256`, `gene_space_sha256`, and `cache_fingerprint` across the bank, the gate, and the checkpoints; a single mismatched file fails the whole release load with `Model checkpoints, genes, reference bank and fusion weights do not match`.

Sources: [weights/README.md](/weights/README.md#L5-L31), [configs/release.example.json](/configs/release.example.json#L1-L11), [morph2mol/release.py](/morph2mol/release.py#L8-L45)

## Step 3: Run Your First Prediction

One command produces a complete prediction. It segments nuclei, extracts cell-centered crops, predicts expression, retrieves reference expression, fuses both sources, and streams the result to disk — also saving the segmentation beside the output:

```bash
python predict/predict.py \
  --image /path/to/slide.svs \
  --release models/morph2mol \
  --out results/prediction.h5ad
```

The pipeline your first command triggers:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Input slide<br/>SVS / TIFF / PNG / JPEG"] --> B{"Physical resolution<br/>in metadata?"}
    B -- "yes" --> D
    B -- "no" --> C["Supply --mpp<br/>microns per pixel"] --> D
    D["Nuclei segmentation<br/>Cellpose-SAM cpsam"] --> E["cells.npz<br/>nuclei polygons + centroids"]
    E --> F["55-um mask-weighted<br/>cell crops"]
    F --> G["Image encoder<br/>UNI2-h backbone"]
    G --> H["Direct prediction A<br/>log1p scale"]
    G --> I["Stage-1 embedding<br/>reference retrieval K=50"]
    H --> J["Gated fusion<br/>X = beta*A + (1-beta)*R"]
    I --> J
    J --> K["prediction.h5ad<br/>streamed via .partial, renamed on completion"]
    D -.-> L["cells.npz kept<br/>beside the output"]
```

Three first-run behaviors are worth knowing in advance. First, if the image carries no physical-resolution metadata, the command exits with an explicit error telling you to pass `--mpp`; a typical scanned-slide value is `0.25`, but you must use your own image's true resolution. Second, the segmentation step runs as a subprocess invoking `predict/segment.py`, and **on the very first run Cellpose-SAM weights are downloaded automatically** from `mouseland/cellpose-sam` via Hugging Face Hub — a network connection is needed even if your model download is complete. Third, the resulting `cells.npz` is written next to your output file; re-running on the same output path without `--overwrite` protects both files from accidental clobbering.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L46-L73), [predict/predict.py](/predict/predict.py#L13-L68), [predict/segment.py](/predict/segment.py#L48-L58)

## Key Options for Your First Runs

The full flag surface is documented in [Inference CLI Reference](3-inference-cli-reference). These are the options a beginner needs on day one:

| Flag | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--image` / `--prepared` | one is required | Input slide (auto-segmented) or a pre-prepared directory of cell crops and boundaries |
| `--release` | required | Path to your model release directory (`models/morph2mol`) |
| `--out` | required | Output `.h5ad` path |
| `--mpp` | from metadata | Microns per pixel; **required** when slide metadata lacks resolution |
| `--genes` | `all` | `all` (18,580 model genes), `xenium`, or a text file of gene symbols, one per line |
| `--tissue` | global weights | Organ or organ/width fusion group, e.g. `lung` or `lung/wide` |
| `--device` / `--amp` | `cuda` / `bf16` | CPU inference: `--device cpu --amp fp32` |
| `--enc-chunk` / `--query-batch` | `64` / `256` | Lower both to reduce transient GPU memory |
| `--workers` | `4` | CPU workers loading cell crops |
| `--overwrite` | off | Allow reusing an existing output or partial path |

Fusion-weight groups cover 15 reference organs (bone, brain, breast, cervix, colon, heart, kidney, liver, lung, lymph_node, ovary, pancreas, prostate, skin, tonsil) across 20 organ/panel combinations. `narrow` groups fit fewer than 1,000 measured model genes; `wide` at least 1,000. Omitting `--tissue` applies global weights — a safe default for a first run.

Sources: [predict/predict.py](/predict/predict.py#L13-L38), [README.md](/README.md#L74-L89)

## Inspect the Result

Read the output with `anndata`; the file contains per-cell predictions over your requested genes:

```python
import anndata as ad
prediction = ad.read_h5ad("results/prediction.h5ad")
```

| Field | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `X` | Combined scores: `beta * A + (1 - beta) * R` |
| `layers['A']` | Direct image-based predictions in `log1p(mu)` scale |
| `layers['R']` | Reference-derived scores; `NaN` where reference coverage is unavailable |
| `var['beta']` / `var['covered']` | Per-gene fusion weight and reference coverage |
| `obsm['spatial']` | Cell centroids as x,y coordinates in source-image pixels |

One interpretation rule matters from the start: combined scores describe **variation across cells within each gene** — they are per-gene scores, not molecule counts. Genes without reference coverage or fitted weights fall back to the direct prediction. Full field semantics belong to [Reading Prediction Outputs](4-reading-prediction-outputs).

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L91-L115), [predict/predict.py](/predict/predict.py#L108-L121)

## Troubleshooting the First Run

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Image has no physical resolution metadata. Supply --mpp` | Slide lacks resolution tags | Re-run with your true microns-per-pixel, e.g. `--mpp 0.25` |
| `Missing release artifact …` | Incomplete download (usually UNI2-h or bank) | Re-run the Step 2 download; check `models/morph2mol` against the directory tree above |
| `Release checksum mismatch: …` | Corrupted or partially transferred checkpoint | Delete and re-download the affected file |
| `Model checkpoints, genes, reference bank and fusion weights do not match` | Files mixed from different releases | Keep one release directory intact; re-download as a unit |
| `FileExistsError: Output/partial exists` | Previous run wrote to the same path | Choose a new `--out` or pass `--overwrite` |
| CUDA out of memory | Large slide, big batch defaults | `--enc-chunk 32 --query-batch 64` (or lower); CPU fallback: `--device cpu --amp fp32` |
| `cellpose is required by predict/segment.py` | Segmentation dependency missing | `pip install cellpose>=4.0` (the requirements file pins `cellpose==4.2.1.1`) |

Sources: [predict/predict.py](/predict/predict.py#L41-L50), [morph2mol/release.py](/morph2mol/release.py#L13-L45), [predict/segment.py](/predict/segment.py#L41-L58), [requirements.txt](/requirements.txt#L10-L10)

> [!TIP]
> Watch for `*.partial` files. Output matrices are streamed to a `.partial` HDF5 file and atomically renamed to the final `.h5ad` only after every cell has been written exactly once — a leftover `.partial` means an interrupted run, not a usable result.

## Where to Go Next

You have now completed the minimum loop: install → download → predict → inspect. Recommended progression from here:

- [Inference CLI Reference](3-inference-cli-reference) — every flag, including `--prepared`, `--cells`, and reference-exclusion options, before scaling to production slides
- [Reading Prediction Outputs](4-reading-prediction-outputs) — complete output schema, embedding fields, and interpretation guidance
- [Architecture Overview](5-architecture-overview) — how the encoder, SE(2) decoder, retrieval bank, and gate fit together
- [Release Integrity Verification](21-release-integrity-verification) — what the release loader checks and why, useful when sharing releases across machines
- Training your own model requires paired H&E images and measured spatial expression; start with [Training Data Contracts](13-training-data-contracts) and the repository guide [docs/training.md](/docs/training.md#L1-L1)


# Inference CLI Reference



This page is the complete operator's manual for Morph2Mol's single inference command, `predict/predict.py`. It documents every command-line argument, the validation rules the tool enforces, the files it reads and writes, and the progress messages you will see in the terminal. You do not need to understand the model internals to use this page — it is written for running predictions from an H&E image to a finished `.h5ad` file. For a hands-on walkthrough with a real slide, start with [Quick Start](2-quick-start); for interpreting the result matrix afterward, continue to [Reading Prediction Outputs](4-reading-prediction-outputs).

Sources: [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L1-L9), [README.md](README.md#L44-L53)

## Running the command

Morph2Mol is a Python package without a console-script entry point, so the CLI is invoked directly as a script from the repository root:

```bash
python predict/predict.py --image /path/to/slide.svs --release models/morph2mol --out results/prediction.h5ad
```

The project requires Python 3.10 or later, and the dependencies come from `requirements.txt` (`pip install -r requirements.txt`). If your slide is in SVS, NDPI, or MRXS format, you additionally need the OpenSlide system library and `openslide-python`; PNG, JPEG, and TIFF images work without it. Because the script resolves its own parent directory at import time, it can be launched from any working directory, but relative paths in `--image`, `--release`, and `--out` are resolved against wherever you run it — keeping the repo root as your working directory avoids surprises.

Sources: [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L5-L16), [README.md](README.md#L15-L23), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L8)

## What one invocation does

A single call to `predict.py` chains the whole inference pipeline: automatic nuclei segmentation (unless you supply boundaries), cell-centered crop extraction, image encoding, spatial decoding, reference-bank retrieval, gated fusion, and streaming disk output. The command needs no measured expression and no precomputed features for the target slide — everything is derived from the image plus the downloaded model release.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["python predict/predict.py"] --> B{"Input mode?"}
    B -->|"--image without --cells"| C["segment.py subprocess<br/>Cellpose-SAM writes cells.npz"]
    B -->|"--cells or --prepared"| D["Load cell boundaries"]
    C --> D
    D --> E["Geometry: 55 um crops,<br/>um positions, area stats"]
    E --> F["Load release:<br/>checkpoints, genes, bank, gate"]
    F --> G["Encode stage-2 features<br/>UNI2-h + LoRA, chunked"]
    G --> H["SE(2) decode<br/>A = log1p(mu) direct scores"]
    H --> I["Stream rows to .partial h5"]
    I --> J["Retrieve top-50 from bank<br/>gated fusion: X, R"]
    J --> K["Rename .partial to --out<br/>complete = true"]
```

The pipeline runs in two passes over the same open output file: first a per-block loop encodes images and writes the direct prediction layer `A` (printing `[A] blocks k/total`), then the model and slide handles are released from memory and a second loop performs retrieval and fusion in batches, writing the `R` and fused `X` matrices. The two-phase memory release — deleting the model, closing the slide reader, and emptying the CUDA cache — is why a single process can predict large slides without holding both the network and the reference bank resident at once.

Sources: [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L52-L71), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L126-L174), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L175-L201), [README.md](README.md#L55-L66)

## Required arguments

Two arguments are always mandatory, plus exactly one input source. The source flags `--image` and `--prepared` form a mutually exclusive required group: argparse rejects the command if neither — or both — are given.

| Argument | Required | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--image PATH` or `--prepared DIR` | One of the two | Input slide (WSI/TIFF/PNG/JPEG) or prepared slide directory |
| `--release DIR` | Yes | Portable model directory containing `release.json`, checkpoints, gene space, fusion weights, and the reference bank |
| `--out PATH` | Yes | Destination `.h5ad`; matrices are streamed to disk as they are computed |

The `--release` directory is the model folder downloaded from Hugging Face. It must contain `release.json` plus the artifacts it references (`stage1.pt`, `stage2.pt`, `gene_space.npz`, the UNI2-h checkpoint, `beta.json`, and `bank/`); the loader resolves every relative path from `release.json` and fails fast with a named artifact if one is missing. Keeping all files together is essential — the loader additionally cross-checks checksums between checkpoints, gene space, bank, and fusion weights before any GPU work starts.

Sources: [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L13-L19), [weights/README.md](weights/README.md#L5-L29), [morph2mol/release.py](morph2mol/release.py#L10-L26)

## Choosing the input source

The CLI accepts three input styles, and the `open_slide` dispatcher picks the reader purely from which flags you passed: `--prepared` alone wins, otherwise `--image` plus `--cells` must both be present.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Q["What do you have?"] --> A["An H&E slide file"]
    Q --> B["A prepared slide directory"]
    A --> A1{"Own segmentation?"}
    A1 -->|"No"| A2["--image SLIDE"]
    A1 -->|"Yes"| A3["--image SLIDE --cells MY.npz"]
    B --> B1["--prepared DIR"]
```

| Flag | Input consumed | Segmentation | Typical use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--image slide.svs` | Whole-slide image | Automatic (Cellpose-SAM subprocess) | Fresh slides, quickest start |
| `--image slide.svs --cells seg.npz` | Image + boundary file | Skipped | You have masks from your own pipeline |
| `--prepared slide_dir/` | Pre-cut crops + `patch_cell_boundaries.npz` + `manifest.csv.gz` | Already done | Training/benchmark layout, repeated runs |

Passing `--cells` together with `--prepared` is rejected at argument-parsing time with `--cells applies only to --image`, because a prepared directory already carries its own boundaries. When you supply your own `cells.npz` for a whole-slide image, it must follow the segmentation file contract: `y_pixel` and `x_pixel` centroid arrays, an `indptr` offset array into `vertex_x`/`vertex_y` polygon vertices, and optionally `cell_id` and `mpp`. Coordinates live in full-resolution source-image pixels, and cell identifiers must be unique — the loader raises `Cell identifiers must be unique` otherwise.

Sources: [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L13-L16), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L43-L44), [predict/inputs.py](predict/inputs.py#L116-L122), [predict/segment.py](predict/segment.py#L17-L23), [predict/inputs.py](predict/inputs.py#L14-L33), [predict/inputs.py](predict/inputs.py#L67-L91)

## Physical resolution: `--mpp`

Morph2Mol reasons in micrometers, not pixels: every cell gets a crop covering the fixed **55 µm** training field of view, so the tool must know your slide's microns-per-pixel (mpp) value. When omitted, the CLI reads `--mpp` from slide metadata in this order: first your explicit flag, then the OpenSlide properties (`openslide.mpp-x`, `aperio.MPP`, or `tiff.XResolution`), then the `mpp` key stored inside a `cells.npz`. If none of these yield a positive finite value, the run stops with `Image has no physical resolution metadata. Supply --mpp (um/pixel)` — plain PNG/JPEG files never carry this metadata, so they always need the flag.

```bash
python predict/predict.py --image /path/to/image.png --mpp 0.25 \
  --release models/morph2mol --out results/prediction.h5ad
```

Two guardrails protect you from nonsense values: argparse-time validation rejects any `--mpp` outside the range `0 < mpp < 100`, and the geometry helper independently rejects non-positive or non-finite resolutions. The mpp you supply directly controls the crop size in source pixels (`55 µm ÷ mpp`), so a wrong value silently misplaces the field of view — double-check scanner specifications before overriding metadata.

Sources: [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L17), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L39-L40), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L52-L59), [predict/slide_io.py](predict/slide_io.py#L64-L74), [predict/inputs.py](predict/inputs.py#L25-L29), [predict/geometry.py](predict/geometry.py#L6-L16), [README.md](README.md#L61-L66)

## Gene panel selection: `--genes`

The `--genes` flag controls how many of the model's output genes are materialized in the `.h5ad`. It accepts exactly three kinds of values:

| Value | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `all` (default) | Predict all 18,580 model genes |
| `xenium` | Restrict to the Xenium panel listed in the release (`xenium_genes.tsv`); fails if the release does not ship one |
| `path/to/genes.txt` | Predict an ordered list of gene symbols, one per line, read from your file |

Custom lists are validated strictly: the requested symbols must be nonempty, unique, and all present in the model's gene head — otherwise the run aborts with `Requested genes must be nonempty, unique, and present in the model gene head`. Row order in the output `var` table preserves your file's order, and each retained gene is mapped to its index in the model head internally. Narrower panels shrink both VRAM traffic and output file size proportionally to the gene count.

Sources: [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L21), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L94-L105), [README.md](README.md#L68-L74), [weights/README.md](weights/README.md#L29)

## Organ-tuned fusion: `--tissue`

`--tissue` selects which set of fusion weights blends the direct prediction with retrieved reference expression. The value is either an organ name (`lung`) or an explicit organ/width group (`lung/wide`); omitting it or passing an unrecognized name falls back to global weights fitted across the entire reference set. Width keywords carry a precise meaning: `narrow` groups were fitted on references with fewer than 1,000 measured model genes, `wide` groups on references with at least 1,000. Supplying an organ alone lets the tool pick the width automatically from how many genes you requested, while an explicit group pins that choice.

The released model ships weights for all 15 reference organs — bone, brain, breast, cervix, colon, heart, kidney, liver, lung, lymph_node, ovary, pancreas, prostate, skin, and tonsil — packaged in a combined `beta.json` that prediction loads automatically. The gate loader validates that the requested gene set is compatible with the selected gate before inference begins, so panel/gate mismatches surface immediately rather than as garbage scores. The mechanics of how β weights are computed and applied are covered in [Gated Fusion Weights](12-gated-fusion-weights).

Sources: [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L20), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L109-L112), [README.md](README.md#L84-L88)

## Hardware and performance flags

CUDA is the default device and bf16 the default autocast precision. Autocast only engages on CUDA — on CPU the flag is inert, which is why the README prescribes the explicit pairing `--device cpu --amp fp32` for CPU inference. Memory pressure is tuned through two independent knobs: `--enc-chunk` slices each block's images into encoder sub-batches, and `--query-batch` sizes the retrieval/fusion batches in the second pass.

| Flag | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--device` | `cuda` | Compute device; use `cpu` when no GPU is available |
| `--amp` | `bf16` | Autocast dtype on CUDA: `bf16`, `fp16`, or `fp32` (disable mixed precision) |
| `--enc-chunk` | `64` | Images per encoder forward chunk; lower to cut transient GPU memory |
| `--query-batch` | `256` | Cells per retrieval + fusion batch; lower for memory-constrained GPUs |
| `--workers` | `4` | CPU DataLoader workers that load cell crops; `0` disables multiprocessing |
| `--save-embeddings` | off | Additionally persist stage-2 and SE(2) embeddings to `obsm` |

Validation rejects non-positive `--enc-chunk`/`--query-batch` or a negative `--workers` before any model is loaded, so typo-level mistakes fail in milliseconds. When combined with `--device cpu`, the segmentation subprocess is also launched with its `--cpu` flag, keeping the whole pipeline on CPU rather than silently falling back mid-way.

Sources: [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L22-L27), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L41-L42), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L68-L69), [predict/model.py](predict/model.py#L56-L57), [README.md](README.md#L77), [README.md](README.md#L80)

## Segmentation flags

When `--image` is given without `--cells`, the CLI launches `predict/segment.py` as a subprocess with the resolved mpp and your chosen window parameters, writing the result beside the output as `<out-stem>.cells.npz`. Three flags tune this step from the parent command:

| Flag | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--segment-window` | `2048` | Window side in slide pixels; the slide is processed window by window |
| `--segment-overlap` | `128` | Context margin around each window so nuclei on seams are segmented completely |
| `--segment-model` | official `cpsam` | Path to local Cellpose-SAM weights instead of the auto-downloaded checkpoint |

The first segmentation run downloads the official `cpsam` checkpoint from the `mouseland/cellpose-sam` Hugging Face repository; point `--segment-model` at a local file to work offline or with fine-tuned weights. You can also run `predict/segment.py` standalone with `--image`, `--out`, and `--mpp` to produce a reusable segmentation file and inspect it before committing to a full prediction. The segmentation algorithm's windowing rule and quality considerations are detailed in [Nuclei Segmentation with Cellpose-SAM](18-nuclei-segmentation-with-cellpose-sam).

> [!TIP]
> After segmentation, segment.py prints the median nucleus diameter in pixels and micrometers. Healthy H&E nuclei land around 6–12 µm — if your printout is far from that range, your `--mpp` or color channel assumption is wrong, and it is cheaper to fix now than after a full prediction.

Sources: [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L28-L30), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L60-L70), [predict/segment.py](predict/segment.py#L54-L58), [predict/segment.py](predict/segment.py#L99-L115), [predict/segment.py](predict/segment.py#L187-L191), [README.md](README.md#L55)

## Identity, privacy, and reference exclusion

Retrieval can accidentally return cells from the very slide you are predicting (or from related samples), which leaks the answer and inflates apparent quality. The CLI prevents this by default: the target's `--sample-id` is always excluded from the reference bank, and `--exclude` removes additional donor/block identifiers given as space-separated names. If `--sample-id` is omitted, it defaults to the basename of your `--image` or `--prepared` input, which is how the training/benchmark layout stays leak-free without extra flags.

The identifiers you pass are matched against the bank's object names, and the actually-excluded subset is recorded in the output metadata (`excluded_objects`) alongside the retrieval settings (`K=50` neighbors, `tau=0.03`, cluster target size 100) and the bank fingerprint — giving you an auditable record of exactly which references influenced the run. Retrieval accuracy itself — clustering, similarity search, and coverage — is explained in [Cluster Retrieval Mechanics](11-cluster-retrieval-mechanics).

Sources: [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L31-L32), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L107-L108), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L178-L179), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L189-L191), [README.md](README.md#L78)

## Output path control and safe reruns

The CLI treats your output path transactionally. All matrices are written to a hidden sibling file named `<out>.partial` first; only after the completion flag is set does the tool atomically rename it to the final `--out` path with `os.replace`. This means a crashed or killed run can never leave a half-written file pretending to be valid at `--out`.

The flip side is rerun protection: if either the final output **or** a leftover `.partial` exists and you have not passed `--overwrite`, the command raises `FileExistsError` immediately. The same guard applies to the auto-generated `cells.npz` — if a previous segmentation file sits next to your output, you must either point `--cells` at it explicitly (to reuse the segmentation) or pick a new output path. The design intent is that resuming from an existing artifact is always an explicit, visible choice rather than a silent overwrite.

> [!TIP]
> If a run died mid-way, a stale `<out>.partial` will block your rerun with `Output/partial exists`. Delete it, or pass `--overwrite` — but remember `--overwrite` also triggers re-segmentation if the `cells.npz` is absent, so keep the segmentation file when you only want to re-run the model stages.

Sources: [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L19), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L33), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L45-L49), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L60-L62), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L198-L201)

## Files the command writes

| Path / field | Trigger | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<out>.partial` → `--out` | Always | Final `.h5ad` (layers `A`, `R`, matrix `X`, `obsm['spatial']`, provenance in `uns['morph2mol']`) |
| `<out-stem>.cells.npz` | Automatic segmentation | Centroids, polygon vertices, cell IDs, mpp — reusable via `--cells` |
| `obsm['X_morph2mol_stage2']`, `obsm['X_morph2mol_se2']` | `--save-embeddings` | Stage-2 and SE(2) embeddings as float16 |
| `obsm['X_morph2mol_phase1']` | Kept only with `--save-embeddings` | Stage-1 retrieval embedding; computed always for retrieval but deleted at the end unless you ask to keep it |

Inside the `.h5ad`, `obs` carries per-cell `x_pixel`/`y_pixel` (source-image pixels) and `x_um`/`y_um` (micrometers), while `var` records which `global_gene_id` each output row maps to, the applied `beta` fusion weight, and per-gene `covered` flags. The provenance block in `uns['morph2mol']` stores the model name, checkpoint SHA-256 hashes, mpp, tissue choice, gate source, and scale conventions — so any prediction file can be traced back to the exact release that produced it. Field-by-field interpretation continues in [Reading Prediction Outputs](4-reading-prediction-outputs).

Sources: [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L60), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L114-L122), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L136-L141), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L192-L197), [README.md](README.md#L92-L109)

## Progress lines and what they mean

The CLI prints flush-through progress so long runs stay observable; every line is prefixed with a bracketed stage tag.

| Message | Stage | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[slide] ... mpp=... -> window scale ...` | Segmentation | Slide dimensions, reader backend, and rescale factor for Cellpose |
| `[plan] Nx x Ny = M windows ...` | Segmentation | Total segmentation windows over the slide |
| `window k/total N nuclei (t s)` | Segmentation | Running window count and nuclei found so far |
| `[predict] N cells; G genes; B target/context blocks` | Prediction start | Confirms cell count, panel size, and spatial blocking plan |
| `[A] blocks k/B` | Direct pass | Encode + decode progress; printed every 20 blocks |
| `[retrieval + fusion] e/N cells` | Fusion pass | Cells fused with reference expression so far |
| `[done] out.h5ad` | Finish | Partial file was atomically renamed; prediction is complete and valid |

The target/context block count reported at start reflects the spatial blocking protocol — up to 128 target cells and 64 context neighbors within 137 µm per block, with every cell output exactly once. Blocking internals live in [Spatial Context Blocking](19-spatial-context-blocking) and the exactly-once write contract in [Streaming Output and Fault Tolerance](20-streaming-output-and-fault-tolerance).

Sources: [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L123), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L165-L166), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L188), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L201), [predict/segment.py](predict/segment.py#L124-L133), [predict/segment.py](predict/segment.py#L188-L191), [README.md](README.md#L57)

## Validation errors and how to fix them

The CLI fails fast with explicit messages before or during inference. Each row below pairs a real error string from the code with its cause and remedy.

| Error message | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--mpp must be positive microns per pixel` | mpp outside `(0, 100)` | Pass a realistic scanner resolution, e.g. `0.25` |
| `Batch sizes must be positive and workers nonnegative` | Zero/negative `--enc-chunk`, `--query-batch`, or `--workers` | Use positive batch sizes, workers ≥ 0 |
| `--cells applies only to --image` | Combined `--prepared` with `--cells` | Drop `--cells`; prepared dirs carry their own boundaries |
| `Output/partial exists: ...` | Previous run's file or leftover `.partial` | New `--out` path, or `--overwrite` |
| `Image has no physical resolution metadata. Supply --mpp` | PNG/JPEG or metadata-free slide | Pass `--mpp` explicitly |
| `... exists. Pass it explicitly with --cells ...` | Auto-segmentation file already beside output | Reuse via `--cells`, change `--out`, or `--overwrite` |
| `No cells in input` | Empty or failed segmentation | Check `--channel`/`--mpp`; inspect the standalone segment run |
| `Cell identifiers must be unique` | Duplicate IDs in supplied `cells.npz` | Regenerate the segmentation file with unique `cell_id`s |
| `Missing release artifact <key>: ...` | File referenced by `release.json` absent | Restore the complete model directory |
| `Release checksum mismatch: <key>` | Artifact does not match its recorded hash | Re-download the corrupted file |
| `Model checkpoints, genes, reference bank and fusion weights do not match` | Bank/gate built from a different release | Use a consistently exported release set |
| `Release does not provide xenium_genes` | `--genes xenium` on a release without the panel | Use `--genes all` or a custom gene file |
| `Requested genes must be nonempty, unique, and present in the model gene head` | Bad custom gene list | Deduplicate and spell-check against the model gene symbols |
| `Nonfinite direct prediction` | Numerical fault (often extreme inputs/precision) | Try `--amp fp32`, verify slide is real H&E at expected mpp |
| `Prediction must write each target cell exactly once` | Internal write-coverage invariant violated | Report the input; this should never trigger in normal use |

Most of these checks run before any GPU work: argument validation first, then release integrity verification (schema, artifact presence, cross-artifact checksums between stage-1/stage-2, gene space, bank, and gate). Release verification mechanics are covered in [Release Integrity Verification](21-release-integrity-verification).

Sources: [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L39-L48), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L57-L62), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L87-L90), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L97-L104), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L152-L153), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L167-L168), [morph2mol/release.py](morph2mol/release.py#L10-L45), [predict/slide_io.py](predict/slide_io.py#L50-L60)

## Where to go next

With the CLI mastered, the natural reading path is: generate a first prediction following [Quick Start](2-quick-start), then learn to load and interpret the output tensors in [Reading Prediction Outputs](4-reading-prediction-outputs). When you are ready to go deeper, the segmentation options you just met are dissected in [Nuclei Segmentation with Cellpose-SAM](18-nuclei-segmentation-with-cellpose-sam), the blocking behavior behind the `target/context blocks` counter in [Spatial Context Blocking](19-spatial-context-blocking), the fusion weights behind `--tissue` in [Gated Fusion Weights](12-gated-fusion-weights), and the pre-flight checks behind `--release` in [Release Integrity Verification](21-release-integrity-verification). The repo-level input format specification — image geometry, the prepared-slide layout, and `cells.npz` contract — lives in [docs/formats.md](docs/formats.md).


# Reading Prediction Outputs



This page explains everything Morph2Mol writes to disk when a prediction finishes. After reading it you will be able to load a result file, identify every field inside it, interpret the three score matrices correctly, and verify that a run completed cleanly. The output is a single AnnData `.h5ad` file — the standard single-cell Python container — so the same file works with scanpy, anndata, and any HDF5 tool.

## Loading the Result File

A prediction run invoked with `--out results/prediction.h5ad` produces exactly one primary artifact. Loading it requires only the `anndata` package that ships with Morph2Mol's dependencies:

```python
import anndata as ad
prediction = ad.read_h5ad("results/prediction.h5ad")
```

The returned `AnnData` object is a table of cells (rows in `obs`) by genes (columns in `var`), with extra matrices attached alongside. Every cell from your slide appears exactly once as a row — the pipeline processes cells in spatial blocks of up to 128 targets with halo context cells, but only target predictions are saved, and each cell is written precisely once.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L94-L114), [docs/formats.md](docs/formats.md#L52-L59), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L113-L116)

## Anatomy of the Output File

The diagram below maps the complete field layout as written by the prediction pipeline. Matrices marked *optional* only exist when the corresponding CLI flag was used.

```mermaid
graph TD
    ROOT["prediction.h5ad<br/>AnnData / HDF5"] --> X["X<br/>[cells × genes] float32<br/>fused expression scores"]
    ROOT --> OBS["obs — cell table"]
    ROOT --> VAR["var — gene table"]
    ROOT --> LAYERS["layers"]
    ROOT --> OBSM["obsm — cell embeddings"]
    ROOT --> UNS["uns['morph2mol']<br/>provenance metadata"]
    OBS --> O1["cell_id (index)"]
    OBS --> O2["y_pixel, x_pixel"]
    OBS --> O3["y_um, x_um"]
    VAR --> V1["global_gene_id"]
    VAR --> V2["beta"]
    VAR --> V3["covered"]
    LAYERS --> L1["A — direct<br/>log1p(mu), float32"]
    LAYERS --> L2["R — reference<br/>z-scores, NaN = uncovered"]
    OBSM --> M1["spatial — x,y in source pixels"]
    OBSM --> M2["X_morph2mol_phase1 · 1536-d float16"]
    OBSM --> M3["X_morph2mol_stage2 · 1536-d float16"]
    OBSM --> M4["X_morph2mol_se2 · d_model-d float16"]
```

Predictions and reference scores are stored as `float32`; stored embeddings are compressed to `float16`. Large matrices are written incrementally into chunked, LZF-compressed HDF5 datasets, so output size scales with cell count × requested genes rather than requiring the whole result in memory at once.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L101-L111), [docs/formats.md](docs/formats.md#L52-L54), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L126-L141)

## Three Score Matrices and What Each One Means

The file holds up to three related matrices, and choosing the right one is the most common beginner question:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Q["Which matrix should I analyze?"] -->|"primary result:<br/>cell-to-cell variation per gene"| X["X"]
    Q -->|"raw decoder output<br/>in log1p(mu)"| A["layers['A']"]
    Q -->|"retrieved reference signal<br/>or coverage audit"| R["layers['R']"]
    R -->|"a NaN column"| FB["var['covered'] is False →<br/>X falls back to A for that gene"]
```

**`layers['A']`** — the direct predictions, in `log1p(mu)` scale, produced by the Negative-Binomial expression decoder from image features alone. **`layers['R']`** — expression scores retrieved from the reference bank of cells with *measured* expression, standardized as a per-reference population z-score of `log1p(counts)`. A gene may contain `NaN` here, which means the reference bank has no measured coverage for that gene. **`X`** — the final combined score:

```text
X = beta * A + (1 - beta) * R
```

where `beta` is a per-gene fusion weight in `[0, 1]` fitted offline from reference data — no target expression is read at inference time. Genes with no reference coverage (or no fitted weight) automatically use the direct prediction, because the fusion code forces `beta = 1.0` wherever `R` is missing. This fallback lives in `apply_gate`, which also blocks non-finite weights from silently blanking a gene's column.

> [!TIP]
> The `NaN` values in `layers['R']` are intentional, not an error: `ReferenceBank.configure` marks a gene as covered only if it appears in at least one reference-bank panel, and uncovered queries return an all-`NaN` block. Always pair `R` with `var['covered']` when auditing coverage.

An important interpretation rule: combined scores describe **variation across cells within each gene** — they are not molecule counts, and columns are not comparable to each other as absolute abundance. The exact scale description is self-documented inside the file in `uns['morph2mol']['X_scale']`, alongside `A_scale` and `R_scale`.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L113-L114), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L121-L122), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L183-L188), [morph2mol/gate.py](morph2mol/gate.py#L88-L105), [morph2mol/retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L168-L177)

## Cell Coordinates: Pixels vs Microns

Spatial positions are stored twice, and they use different conventions:

| Field | Units | Coordinate order | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `obsm['spatial']` | source-image pixels | **x, y** | Scanpy-compatible centroids (`spatial_order: "x,y in source pixels"`) |
| `obs['x_pixel']`, `obs['y_pixel']` | source-image pixels | per-column | Same centroids, individual columns |
| `obs['x_um']`, `obs['y_um']` | microns | per-column | Physical positions derived from `mpp`, usable for cross-slide comparisons |

The `obsm['spatial']` matrix follows the x-major convention that plotting tools like scanpy's spatial viewers expect, while the micron columns are derived using the microns-per-pixel value recorded in the metadata. If you supply `--mpp`, that exact value is what the micron columns are based on.

Sources: [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L114-L116), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L194), [docs/formats.md](docs/formats.md#L52-L53)

## Gene Metadata: `beta` and `covered`

The `var` table identifies each output gene and records how its final score was produced. `var_names` are the gene symbols you requested (all 18,580 model genes by default, or a narrower panel via `--genes xenium` or a custom list), and `global_gene_id` maps each symbol to its index in the full model gene head.

| Column | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `global_gene_id` | int64 | Position of the gene in the model's 18,580-gene output head |
| `beta` | float32 | Applied fusion weight in `[0, 1]`; `1.0` means pure direct prediction |
| `covered` | bool | Whether the reference bank provides measured expression for this gene |

A `beta` close to 1 means the image decoder dominated that gene's score; a `beta` close to 0 means retrieved reference expression dominated. `covered == False` always coincides with `beta == 1.0` in that column's fusion, because the transferred weight cannot apply where `R` is absent.

Sources: [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L113-L113), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L192-L193), [README.md](README.md#L106-L107), [morph2mol/gate.py](morph2mol/gate.py#L97-L105)

## Provenance Metadata in `uns`

Every result file carries a `uns['morph2mol']` dictionary that makes the run self-describing and reproducible. It records the model identity, SHA-256 hashes of the loaded checkpoints, the spatial blocking configuration, and the fusion settings.

| Key | Example / meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `model` | `"Morph2Mol-25M-scGPT"` |
| `stage1_sha256`, `stage2_sha256`, `gene_space_sha256` | Checkpoint integrity hashes for reproducibility audits |
| `mpp`, `crop_um` | Source resolution used; fixed 55 µm cell crop |
| `spatial_context` | Blocking plan: `mode='target_context'`, `max_target_cells`, `max_context_cells`, `context_radius_um`, seed, and `output_policy='targets_once_only'` |
| `gate_source`, `tissue` | Which fusion-weight group was applied (e.g. `lung/wide`, or `direct` if global) |
| `source` | Input kind (auto-segmented image, supplied cells, or prepared slide) |
| `K`, `tau`, `cluster_target_size` | Retrieval settings: 50 neighbors, temperature 0.03, 100-cell clusters |
| `bank_fingerprint`, `excluded_objects` | Which reference bank was used and which donors/blocks were excluded |
| `A_scale`, `R_scale`, `X_scale` | Self-documenting scale descriptions for each matrix |

> [!TIP]
> To verify you are comparing results produced under identical conditions, check `uns['morph2mol']['spatial_context']` and the three `*_sha256` fields: the partition is deterministic for a given sample ID and seed, and matching hashes guarantee the same model weights were used.

Sources: [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L117-L122), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L189-L191), [predict/spatial_context.py](predict/spatial_context.py#L42-L47)

## Completion Guarantees and `.partial` Files

Prediction matrices are streamed to disk block by block into a temporary `<output>.partial` file. Only after every cell has been written, the reference retrieval and fusion pass finishes, and the final metadata is committed, does the writer set the HDF5 root attribute `complete = True` and atomically rename the file with `os.replace`. This means a file appearing under your `--out` path is always a finished result.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S["run starts"] --> P["write to<br/>prediction.h5ad.partial<br/>complete=False"]
    P --> C{"all blocks written<br/>+ retrieval fused?"}
    C -->|"yes"| F["complete=True<br/>os.replace → prediction.h5ad"]
    C -->|"interrupted"| H["only .partial remains<br/>restart with --overwrite or new path"]
```

Two practical consequences for reading outputs. First, if a run is interrupted, only the `.partial` file survives — the real output will not exist, and rerunning without `--overwrite` will raise `FileExistsError` until you remove the leftovers or choose a new path. Second, because each cell is committed exactly once (enforced both per block by `commit_target_rows` and globally by a final `written == 1` check), you never need to de-duplicate rows after loading.

Sources: [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L126-L127), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L144-L168), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L195-L201), [docs/formats.md](docs/formats.md#L57-L59), [predict/spatial_context.py](predict/spatial_context.py#L64-L78)

## Optional Embeddings

By default the file keeps only what is needed downstream: the phase-1 retrieval embeddings are computed during the run but deleted from the file after retrieval completes, unless you passed `--save-embeddings`. With that flag, three additional `obsm` matrices are kept:

| Key | Shape / dtype | Produced by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `obsm['X_morph2mol_phase1']` | [N, 1536] float16 | Stage-1 contrastive encoder — the features used for reference retrieval |
| `obsm['X_morph2mol_stage2']` | [N, 1536] float16 | Stage-2 image encoder output |
| `obsm['X_morph2mol_se2']` | [N, d_model] float16 | SE(2) spatial decoder embeddings |

These are useful for downstream analyses such as clustering cells by morphology, computing retrieval diagnostics, or debugging fusion behavior. They are stored in float16 to keep file size manageable; cast to float32 before doing arithmetic that needs the precision.

Sources: [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L137-L141), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L157-L164), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L195-L196), [README.md](README.md#L109-L111)

## Reading Old Files and Troubleshooting

The `morph2mol.prediction_io` module provides two small helpers that read results produced by earlier releases: `prediction_metadata` accepts either the current `uns['morph2mol']` key or the legacy `uns['voice25m']`, and `phase1_features` accepts either `obsm['X_morph2mol_phase1']` or the legacy `obsm['X_voice_phase1']`.

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FileExistsError: Output/partial exists` | Previous run finished or was interrupted at that path | Remove the old files, pass `--overwrite`, or choose a new `--out` |
| `.partial` file present, no `.h5ad` | Run was interrupted before completion | Restart the run; the partial file is never a valid result |
| `NaN` values in `layers['R']` | Reference bank has no measured coverage for that gene | Expected — `X` used the direct branch; check `var['covered']` |
| Scores look nothing like counts | Combined scores are per-gene relative measures, not molecule counts | Compare across cells within a gene; see `X_scale` in `uns['morph2mol']` |
| Unsure whether a file is complete | Atomic rename guarantees named outputs are complete | Optionally verify `complete == True` by opening the file with `h5py` directly |

Sources: [morph2mol/prediction_io.py](morph2mol/prediction_io.py#L1-L13), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L47-L49), [docs/formats.md](docs/formats.md#L57-L59)

## Where to Go Next

- To understand how these fields are produced end-to-end, continue to [Architecture Overview](5-architecture-overview).
- For the command-line flags that control what lands in the file (such as `--save-embeddings` and `--genes`), see [Inference CLI Reference](3-inference-cli-reference).
- To learn how the per-gene `beta` weights are fitted, read [Gated Fusion Weights](12-gated-fusion-weights).
- For the mechanics behind `layers['R']`, see [Cluster Retrieval Mechanics](11-cluster-retrieval-mechanics).
- If you need to audit the model files a prediction depends on, check [Release Integrity Verification](21-release-integrity-verification).
- For the engineering details of the streaming write path, see [Streaming Output and Fault Tolerance](20-streaming-output-and-fault-tolerance).

# Architecture Overview



Morph2Mol is a foundation model that predicts single-cell spatial gene expression directly from H&E histology images. Its architecture combines three cooperating mechanisms: a masked-pooling image encoder producing per-cell morphological features, a distance-aware spatial decoder that lets neighboring cells exchange information, and a retrieval branch that borrows measured expression profiles from a reference bank. This page maps the repository onto that design — the component boundaries, the fixed training recipe behind the released 25M checkpoint, and the integrity checks that tie inference artifacts together — so you know exactly where each concern lives before diving into the deep-dive pages.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L1-L5), [pyproject.toml](/pyproject.toml#L6-L19)

## System Composition and Package Layout

The repository is organized as three package roots with a strict dependency direction: `train/` and `predict/` are thin entry-point layers, while `morph2mol/` holds all reusable machinery. Inference code imports training-produced artifacts but never training drivers — `predict/model.py` explicitly states it contains "the released 25M architecture, without importing training drivers," and `morph2mol/release.py` is documented as requiring "no training corpus at inference." This one-way flow is what makes the released model portable.

| Package root | Responsibility | Key modules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `morph2mol/` | Shared model, training, retrieval, and packaging library | `encoder.py`, `se2.py`, `head.py`, `retrieval.py`, `gate.py`, `recipe.py`, `release.py`, `training/` |
| `train/` | CLI entry points for the two fixed training stages and corpus preparation | `train_phase1.py`, `train_phase2.py`, `prepare.py`, `embed_scgpt.py`, `export_release.py` |
| `predict/` | End-to-end inference: segmentation, slide I/O, spatial blocking, orchestration | `segment.py`, `spatial_context.py`, `model.py`, `predict.py` |

Sources: [pyproject.toml](/pyproject.toml#L14-L16), [predict/model.py](/predict/model.py#L1-L3), [morph2mol/release.py](/morph2mol/release.py#L1-L3)

## The Dual-Branch Prediction Architecture

Every predicted cell flows through two parallel branches whose outputs are fused per gene. The **direct branch** learns to synthesize expression from morphology alone (encoder → spatial decoder → negative-binomial head), producing a score for all 18,580 model genes. The **retrieval branch** embeds each cell into a shared Phase-1 contrastive space, finds similar reference communities in a precomputed bank, and returns their averaged measured expression. A per-gene fusion weight β, fitted offline on reference slides, blends them: `X = β·A + (1−β)·R`. The prerequisite to reading the diagram below: solid arrows carry data during inference; dashed arrows are offline preparation steps that happened before the release was packaged.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph OFFLINE["Offline preparation (dashed)"]
        SC[("scGPT cell + gene embeddings")] --> S1
        CORPUS[("Paired H&E + spatial transcriptomics corpus")] --> S1
        S1["Stage 1<br/>contrastive alignment"] --> S2["Stage 2<br/>NB expression training"]
        S1 --> BANK["Reference bank<br/>(clustered communities)"]
        S1 --> GATE["Fusion weights beta<br/>(41-point grid fit)"]
    end
    subgraph ONLINE["Inference (solid)"]
        IMG["H&E slide"] --> SEG["Cellpose-SAM<br/>nuclei segmentation"]
        SEG --> CROP["Cell crops +<br/>mask pooling"]
        CROP --> ENC["UNI2-h + LoRA<br/>encoder"]
        ENC -->|"stage2 LoRA h [1536]"| DEC["SE(2) spatial<br/>decoder d=256"]
        ENC -->|"phase1 LoRA H1"| RET["Bank retrieval<br/>K=50, tau=0.03"]
        DEC --> HEAD["NB expression head<br/>log1p(mu) = A"]
        HEAD --> FUSE["Per-gene fusion<br/>beta*A + (1-beta)*R"]
        RET -->|"R"| FUSE
        FUSE --> OUT[("Streaming<br/>.h5ad output")]
    end
    S2 -.checkpoints.-> ENC
    S2 -.weights.-> DEC
    S2 -.weights.-> HEAD
    BANK -.summaries.-> RET
    GATE -.beta.json.-> FUSE
```

Sources: [predict/predict.py](/predict/predict.py#L162-L181), [README.md](/README.md#L86-L96)

## Direct Branch: From Pixels to Expression

The direct branch is a three-stage composition with fixed dimensions throughout. The **image encoder** is UNI2-h, a ViT-Huge/14 with 1536-dimensional embeddings, 24 blocks, SwiGLU MLPs, and 8 register tokens, built through `timm` with strict state-dict loading and every parameter frozen ([encoder.py](/morph2mol/encoder.py#L35-L41)). Training touches it only through **LoRA adapters** — rank-16 low-rank factors with alpha 32 injected into the query/key/value and projection matrices of the last 12 blocks ([encoder.py](/morph2mol/encoder.py#L13-L26)). Per-cell features come from mask-weighted pooling: the encoder's 256 patch tokens (a 16×16 grid after stripping the 9 prefix tokens) are multiplied by a mask-weight map and summed into a single 1536-dim vector, so each cell's feature is an average over exactly its own image evidence ([encoder.py](/morph2mol/encoder.py#L27-L33)).

The **spatial decoder** then lets cells within a neighborhood exchange information. A `GaussianModule` converts pairwise inter-cell distances in microns — clipped at the 137 µm context radius — into 128 Gaussian basis features projected to 64-dim pair embeddings ([se2.py](/morph2mol/se2.py#L12-L14), [_se2_arch.py](/morph2mol/_se2_arch.py#L7-L22)). Six identical `SE2Layer` blocks (3 before and 3 after a mid-point, d_model=256, 8 heads) refine both cell features and pair features; each layer converts pair states into an additive attention bias, so geometry directly shapes who attends to whom ([se2.py](/morph2mol/se2.py#L8-L20), [_se2_arch.py](/morph2mol/_se2_arch.py#L24-L58)).

The **expression head** maps decoder states to gene expression under a negative-binomial observation model. `DirectHead` keeps a learnable gene-row matrix `W` (initialized from scGPT gene embeddings during training), concatenates the 256-dim cell state with two cell-area covariates, passes them through a small MLP, and computes `mu` via softplus; a global area exponent scales rates by cell size ([head.py](/morph2mol/head.py#L27-L44)). Areas themselves are computed by the shoelace formula from nucleus boundary polygons, with degenerate polygons replaced by the slide median rather than zero ([head.py](/morph2mol/head.py#L7-L25)). Training minimizes the analytic negative-binomial log-likelihood ([head.py](/morph2mol/head.py#L45-L46)).

| Component | Input → Output | Fixed dimensions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UNI2-h encoder | `[B,3,224,224]` crops + masks → `[B,1536]` | 24 blocks, embed 1536, LoRA r=16 on last 12 |
| SE(2) decoder | `[N,1536]` + `pos µm` → `[N,256]` | d_model 256, d_pair 64, 6 layers, 8 heads, 137 µm |
| NB head | `[N,256]` + areas + gene ids → `[N,G]` | MLP 258→1024→D, per-gene θ, area exponent |

Sources: [morph2mol/encoder.py](/morph2mol/encoder.py#L13-L41), [morph2mol/se2.py](/morph2mol/se2.py#L8-L22), [morph2mol/head.py](/morph2mol/head.py#L27-L46)

## Retrieval Branch: Reference Bank and Gated Fusion

The retrieval branch operates on a **reference bank**: one directory per reference object (donor/tissue block), each holding community summaries produced by clustering cell features within that slide. During bank construction, an exhaustive float32 K-means-style assignment (with optional Faiss GPU acceleration, no ANN approximation) groups cells into communities of target size 100, and each community is summarized into an fp16 mean key (1536-dim Phase-1 embedding) plus a float32 mean expression vector ([bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L18-L54)). At load time, `ReferenceBank` verifies the bank's schema, cache fingerprint, completion marker, per-artifact SHA-256 hashes, and panel integrity before pooling every community's expression into a single preallocated device tensor — deliberately bounding host and device memory ([retrieval.py](/morph2mol/retrieval.py#L76-L131)).

Retrieval itself is exact, not approximate: query features are L2-normalized in fp16 and scored by full cosine against every community, top-50 neighbors per bank object are merged per coverage group, and ties at the cutoff threshold receive fractional weights at temperature τ = 0.03 ([retrieval.py](/morph2mol/retrieval.py#L143-L200)). Coverage is explicit — a query gene participates only in groups whose reference objects measured it, and genes covered by no object surface as NaN, which downstream logic treats as "no retrieval" ([retrieval.py](/morph2mol/retrieval.py#L62-L67)).

Fusion weights close the loop. `fit_beta` sweeps a 41-point grid of β per gene, selecting the value that maximizes the Pearson correlation of the blended score against measured expression on reference slides; a grid is chosen over a closed form because the objective is smooth but not concave in β ([gate.py](/morph2mol/gate.py#L6-L8), [gate.py](/morph2mol/gate.py#L48-L75)). At inference, `apply_gate` is deliberately label-blind: it looks up the transferred β per gene and fuses, forcing β = 1 (direct-only) wherever retrieval coverage is missing so NaN can never silently blank a gene column ([gate.py](/morph2mol/gate.py#L77-L105)).

> [!TIP]
> The direct branch and the retrieval branch read the **same encoder** with different LoRA weights. `Morph2Mol.encode(which=...)` hot-swaps adapter tensors between the Phase-1 (stage-1 contrastive) and stage-2 parameterizations; stage-2 checkpoints save only the trainable subset, and frozen adapters are restored from the stage-1 checkpoint ([predict/model.py](/predict/model.py#L49-L63)). This is why both stage-1 and stage-2 artifacts must ship in every release.

Sources: [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L18-L54), [morph2mol/retrieval.py](/morph2mol/retrieval.py#L76-L200), [morph2mol/gate.py](/morph2mol/gate.py#L6-L105)

## Training Pipeline: A Fixed Two-Stage Recipe

Training follows a strictly ordered, hard-coded recipe. **Stage 1** aligns image and RNA representations with a symmetric InfoNCE loss between the LoRA-adapted image tower and a projection tower over 512-dimensional scGPT cell embeddings; it runs three full-coverage epochs with random right-angle rotations and reflections applied jointly to crops and masks, and uses gradient caching so the 2,048-cell effective batch fits through the frozen ViT in chunks ([training/stage1.py](/morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L1-L110), [docs/training.md](/docs/training.md#L60-L77)). **Stage 2** then trains expression prediction end-to-end: `ExpressionModel` wires encoder → `Linear(1536,256)` → `SpatialTransformer` → `DirectHead`, with the first 20% of steps keeping LoRA frozen, negative-binomial plus auxiliary losses, and gradient checkpointing for the SE(2) stack ([training/stage2.py](/morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L77-L90), [morph2mol/recipe.py](/morph2mol/recipe.py#L23-L39)).

Nothing about these settings is negotiable at the module level. `recipe.py` raises a `TypeError` if any caller tries to override a fixed value, and `check_stage2_settings` refuses to load a checkpoint whose args deviate from the Morph2Mol-25M recipe — architectural constants (128 target cells, 64 context cells, 137 µm radius, seed 1) are shared verbatim by training, calibration, and inference code ([morph2mol/recipe.py](/morph2mol/recipe.py#L4-L40), [predict/spatial_context.py](/predict/spatial_context.py#L71-L81)). Downstream artifacts inherit this discipline: entry-point scripts (`train/_entry.py`) accept only path, hardware, and resume arguments, and even chunk sizes must divide the effective batch exactly ([train/_entry.py](/train/_entry.py#L7-L24)).

| | Stage 1 — alignment | Stage 2 — expression |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Objective | Symmetric InfoNCE (τ = 0.07) | NB log-likelihood + aux/MSE terms |
| Trainable | LoRA adapters + projection towers | Linear in-proj, SE(2) decoder, NB head, LoRA (after 20% freeze) |
| Batch / schedule | 2,048/rank, 3 epochs, warmup 150 | Full-coverage blocks, 3 epochs, grad-ckpt on |
| Output | `stage1_final.pt` (LoRA + towers) | `stage2` checkpoint (identity-linked to stage 1) |
| Feeds into | Retrieval keys (phase1 LoRA), bank, gate fitting | Direct branch A, `log1p(mu)` |

Sources: [morph2mol/training/stage1.py](/morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L17-L110), [morph2mol/training/stage2.py](/morph2morph/training/stage2.py#L77-L90), [morph2mol/recipe.py](/morph2mol/recipe.py#L11-L40), [docs/training.md](/docs/training.md#L60-L78)

## Inference Pipeline: Deterministic, Streaming, Self-Verifying

`predict/predict.py` chains the whole system in one process. It first shells out to `segment.py`, which runs Cellpose-SAM on overlapping windows and keeps each nucleus only in the window whose interior contains its centroid — a rule guaranteeing every cell is segmented exactly once ([predict/predict.py](/predict/predict.py#L66-L78), [predict/segment.py](/predict/segment.py#L1-L18)). Cells are then partitioned into blocks of at most 128 targets plus up to 64 halo context cells within 137 µm; the partition is seeded deterministically from the sample name (`zlib.crc32`), reusing the training-time partition functions so inference blocking matches calibration blocking bit-for-bit ([predict/spatial_context.py](/predict/spatial_context.py#L15-L52)). Within each block, all cells attend to each other in the SE(2) decoder, but `commit_target_rows` scatters only the owned target prefix into the output, with a hard assertion that no cell is written twice ([predict/spatial_context.py](/predict/spatial_context.py#L54-L68)).

Output handling is streaming and atomic: the writer creates chunked, compressed HDF5 datasets up front and fills rows block by block, then deletes the model and GPU cache before the second retrieval pass runs in `query_batch` slices; only when every row is verified written does `os.replace` rename the `.partial` file to the final `.h5ad` ([predict/predict.py](/predict/predict.py#L108-L206)). Provenance travels with the data — the `uns` block records checkpoint SHA-256s, retrieval parameters (K=50, τ=0.03), gate source, the spatial-context protocol, and the scales of each stored layer ([predict/predict.py](/predict/predict.py#L98-L106)).

> [!TIP]
> The spatial blocking protocol is itself a verified artifact. `Release` cross-checks that the fusion-weight metadata's `spatial_context` matches `prediction_protocol()`, and that bank, gate, stage-1, stage-2, and gene-space hashes are mutually consistent — so a gate fitted under a different blocking scheme is structurally impossible to pair with this checkpoint ([morph2mol/release.py](/morph2mol/release.py#L33-L46), [predict/spatial_context.py](/predict/spatial_context.py#L71-L91)).

Sources: [predict/predict.py](/predict/predict.py#L62-L206), [predict/segment.py](/predict/segment.py#L1-L47), [predict/spatial_context.py](/predict/spatial_context.py#L15-L91)

## Integrity Chain

The release directory is the architectural seam between training and inference, and it is treated as a chain of custody rather than a folder of files. `Release` validates the `morph2mol-release-v1` schema, resolves the six artifact paths (UNI2-h weights, stage-1, stage-2, gene space, bank, gate), and re-hashes stage-1/stage-2/gene-space against declared SHA-256s ([morph2mol/release.py](/morph2mol/release.py#L6-L22)).
