| `manifest.json` | Object list, protocol IDs, artifact paths | Builder's sole input contract |

Sources: [train/prepare_bank.py](/train/prepare_bank.py#L67-L73), [morph2mol/bank_io.py](/morph2mol/bank_io.py#L10-L14)

## Stage 2: Clustering and Summarization with `bank_builder.py`

`predict/build_bank.py` is an eight-line shim that imports and runs `bank_builder.main` [predict/build_bank.py](/predict/build_bank.py#L1-L8). The builder accepts `--manifest`, `--output`, `--device`, `--backend` (`auto`/`faiss`/`torch`), and `--expected-objects` [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L222-L230). Before any computation, it disables TF32 matmuls to keep float arithmetic bit-stable across runs [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L76-L81), and validates the manifest: object count must match expectation, stay within 1–256 (a bound tied to uint8 source IDs), and contain no duplicates [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L85-L87).

### The identity dict and cache fingerprint

Reproducibility is engineered through an **identity dictionary** captured before any clustering: schema, checkpoint and gene-space SHA-256s, both protocol IDs, the manifest hash, and every fixed hyperparameter — `target_size=100`, `PCA_dimensions=64`, `max_PCA_rows=100000`, `kmeans_iterations=10`, `per_object_seed='object_index'`, `retrieval_K=50`, `tau=0.03`, backend, torch version, and device [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L93-L101). The Faiss version is pinned into the identity when that backend is used [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L102-L105). Per-object **source signatures** (path, size, mtime of `E`/`Y`/`panel`, plus the feature-meta SHA) are folded in after re-validating each object's split and feature metadata [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L106-L112). The SHA-256 of this canonicalized dict becomes the **`cache_fingerprint`** [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L113).

> [!TIP]
> The fingerprint is the bank's reproducibility contract: any change to inputs, hyperparameters, library versions, or protocol IDs changes the hash, which invalidates every cached summary and forces a rebuild into a fresh directory. Conversely, an unchanged fingerprint lets an interrupted build resume — completed objects are detected and reused verbatim.

Sources: [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L93-L113), [morph2mol/bank_io.py](/morph2mol/bank_io.py#L30-L31)

### Write exclusivity and idempotent restarts

The output directory is guarded by a kernel-level `flock` on `.build.lock`, which releases automatically even for killed processes — the code notes this avoids stale PID locks entirely [morph2mol/bank_io.py](/morph2mol/bank_io.py#L42-L55). Under the lock, if `model.json` already exists, its content must exactly equal the freshly computed model (identity + fingerprint) or the build refuses with *"Bank input/configuration changed; choose a new output directory"*; otherwise the model is written once and becomes the directory's identity record [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L115-L122).

Sources: [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L115-L122), [morph2mol/bank_io.py](/morph2mol/bank_io.py#L42-L55)

### Deterministic PCA projection

Per object, features are validated first: `E` must be `[N, 1536]`, `Y` must be `[N, len(panel)]`, the panel must be unique and in-range, at least 64 cells must exist (the PCA-64 minimum), and the row count must match the manifest's declared `n_cells` [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L132-L141). PCA then proceeds deterministically: a random subsample of `min(N, 100000)` rows is drawn with a generator seeded by the object index, standardized via `original_keys` (L2-normalized Phase-1 features), and reduced to 64 components with `torch.pca_lowrank`; the mean, components, and sampled row indices are all persisted (`PCA_mean.npy`, `PCA_components.npy`, `PCA_training_rows.npy`) so the projection is fully reconstructible [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L142-L150). All N cells are then projected to the 64-D space in 32768-row chunks [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L152-L155).

Sources: [morph2morph/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L142-L155), [docs/training.md](/docs/training.md#L117)

### k-means with exact full-population assignment

Cluster count targets ~100 cells per community: `nclusters = max(1, n // 100)`, initialized by a seeded `randperm` over projected cells [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L156-L158). Ten Lloyd iterations follow, with two interchangeable assignment backends:

| Property | `torch` backend | `faiss` backend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Assignment | Chunked exhaustive float32 L2, no ANN, no subsampling [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L30-L45) | `GpuIndexFlatL2` in float32 (`useFloat16=False`), searched in 8192-row blocks [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L167-L176) |
| Tie-breaking | First centre wins exact ties [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L43) | Faiss internal ordering |
| GPU resources | None needed | 256 MiB temp memory, null-stream sharing with Torch for safe tensor interop [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L160-L165) |
| Selection | Default with `--backend auto` fallback [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L15-L27) | Requires CUDA + GPU Faiss; explicit `faiss` selection fails hard otherwise [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L24-L26) |

Centroids update only over non-empty clusters each iteration [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L179-L185). Notably, the code keeps the *tenth* assignment rather than performing an eleventh search after the final centroid update — an explicit, documented choice [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L187). Labels are then canonicalized with `unique(..., return_inverse=True)`, which simultaneously compacts away empty clusters [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L188-L189). The training guide confirms these parameters: PCA-64 on up to 100,000 cells per slide, 10 iterations, `max(1, floor(N/100))` initial clusters, empty clusters removed, ≥64 cells required, and either backend selectable [docs/training.md](/docs/training.md#L117).

Sources: [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L156-L189), [docs/training.md](/docs/training.md#L117)

### Cluster summarization: keys, values, counts

The `summarize` routine aggregates everything into three artifacts via chunked `index_add_` accumulation [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L48-L62):

- **`keys`** — each cell's Phase-1 feature is L2-normalized to float16 (`original_keys` enforces finite `[N,1536]` input [morph2mol/retrieval.py](/morph2mol/retrieval.py#L64-L68)), averaged within its cluster, and re-normalized. The result is a float16 `[C, 1536]` matrix of cluster centroids on the unit hypersphere [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L55-L59).
- **`values`** — cluster-mean standardized expression across the panel genes, float32, computed from the float16 `Y` upcast per chunk [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L56-L60).
- **`counts`** — cluster cell counts as int64 [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L50-L62).

Non-finite guards fire on both input chunks and final summaries [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L57-L61). All five artifacts plus the three PCA files are saved per object [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L191-L196), and a conservation check asserts no cells were lost (`counts.sum() == n`) [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L197).

> [!TIP]
> Cluster keys are not raw feature centroids — they are normalize → average → re-normalize compositions. Because mean-of-unit-vectors then renormalization stays on the unit sphere, retrieval can later use exact float16 cosine similarity against these keys with zero approximation loss, which is why the bank records `retrieval_K=50` and `tau=0.03` as part of its identity rather than leaving them to inference code.

Sources: [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L48-L62), [morph2mol/retrieval.py](/morph2mol/retrieval.py#L64-L68), [docs/training.md](/docs/training.md#L119)

## On-Disk Layout of a Constructed Bank

A completed bank is a plain directory of NumPy artifacts plus two JSON records. Everything the consumer needs is declared in `bank_io.py`: the schema string `morph2mol-reference-bank`, both protocol IDs, and the eight-member `ARTIFACTS` tuple [morph2mol/bank_io.py](/morph2mol/bank_io.py#L10-L14).

```text
bank/
├── model.json                  # identity dict + cache_fingerprint
├── bank_complete.json          # totals: n_objects, n_cells, n_communities
├── .build.lock                 # kernel flock for write exclusivity
└── summaries/
    ├── object_00/
    │   ├── keys.npy            # [C,1536]  float16  unit-sphere cluster centroids
    │   ├── values.npy          # [C, panel] float32 cluster-mean expression
    │   ├── panel.npy           # global gene indices of measured panel
    │   ├── counts.npy          # [C] int64 cells per cluster
    │   ├── labels.npy          # [N] int32 per-cell cluster assignment
    │   ├── PCA_mean.npy        # projection mean
    │   ├── PCA_components.npy  # 64 components
    │   ├── PCA_training_rows.npy  # sampled rows used to fit PCA
    │   └── complete.json       # metadata + per-artifact SHA-256
    └── object_01/ ...
```

After the per-object loop, `bank_complete.json` records the fingerprint alongside aggregate totals — object count, total cells, and total communities [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L217-L219). This marker is what later turns a partially built directory into an unusable one: loaders demand it before accepting anything [morph2mol/retrieval.py](/morph2mol/retrieval.py#L89-L90).

Sources: [morph2mol/bank_io.py](/morph2mol/bank_io.py#L10-L14), [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L191-L219)

## The Integrity and Reproducibility Chain

Every artifact is protected by a layered verification system that spans construction, caching, and consumption:

1. **Per-object completion records.** After saving, the builder re-hashes each input signature and compares against the pre-build snapshot, failing with *"Input changed during build"* if any file mutated mid-run [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L198-L200). It then writes `complete.json` containing object metadata and the SHA-256 of every artifact [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L201-L209).
2. **Resume validation.** On re-run, a completed object is accepted only if its `complete.json` matches the current fingerprint, object name, and all stored artifact hashes [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L65-L72).
3. **Feature provenance.** `validate_feature` cross-checks the checkpoint hash and protocol ID, requires dimensionality 1536, and demands `output_field == 'phase1'` — explicitly rejecting Stage-2 embeddings being smuggled in as retrieval keys [morph2mol/bank_io.py](/morph2mol/bank_io.py#L58-L65).
4. **Consumer-side verification.** `ReferenceBank.__init__` re-verifies the schema, recomputes the fingerprint from the model JSON, checks `target_size == 100` and the completion marker, requires `retrieval_K == 50` and `tau == TAU`, validates per-object metadata and artifact hashes (optionally skippable via `verify_hashes=False`), and enforces the 1–256 object bound [morph2mol/retrieval.py](/morph2mol/retrieval.py#L77-L112).
5. **Release binding.** A final release cross-checks the bank's `checkpoint_sha256` against the packaged Stage-1 hash and `gene_space_sha256` against the gene space, so a bank can never be silently paired with mismatched checkpoints or genes [morph2mol/release.py](/morph2mol/release.py#L27-L41).

| Check | Enforced at | Failure mode |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Manifest objects are training-split samples | `prepare_bank.py` | `ValueError` [train/prepare_bank.py](/train/prepare_bank.py#L29-L30) |
| Cached predictions match release Stage-1 hash | `prepare_bank.py` | Rejected cache [train/prepare_bank.py](/train/prepare_bank.py#L52-L53) |
| E/Y/panel shapes, panel range, ≥64 cells | `bank_builder.build` | `ValueError` [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L132-L141) |
| Inputs unchanged during build | Per-object finalize | Build abort [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L198-L200) |
| Artifact SHA-256 vs `complete.json` | Resume + load | Corrupt-artifact error [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L65-L72), [morph2mol/retrieval.py](/morph2mol/retrieval.py#L104-L107) |
| Bank ↔ release checkpoint/gene hashes | `Release` construction | Mismatch error [morph2mol/release.py](/morph2mol/release.py#L27-L41) |

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph build["bank_builder.py"]
        ID[identity dict<br/>hashes + hyperparameters] --> FP[cache_fingerprint]
        FP --> MJ[model.json]
        MJ --> OBJ[per-object clustering]
        OBJ --> SIG[verify source signatures] --> CJ[complete.json<br/>+ artifact SHA-256s]
        CJ --> BC[bank_complete.json]
    end
    subgraph consume["retrieval.py ReferenceBank"]
        LOAD[load model.json] --> REFP[recompute fingerprint]
        REFP --> CHK[hash every artifact]
        CHK --> READY[usable bank]
    end
    BC -.->|fingerprint match required| LOAD
    READY -.->|checkpoint + gene-space hashes| REL[Release binding<br/>release.py]
```

Sources: [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L65-L72), [morph2mol/bank_builder.py](/morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L198-L219), [morph2mol/bank_io.py](/morph2mol/bank_io.py#L58-L65), [morph2mol/retrieval.py](/morph2mol/retrieval.py#L77-L112), [morph2mol/release.py](/morph2mol/release.py#L27-L41)

## How the Bank Is Consumed (Handoff)

At load time, `ReferenceBank` streams each object's `keys.npy` to the device as float16 tensors, validates `values.npy` shape/dtype against its panel, and copies the whole expression pool into one preallocated device tensor to bound memory — no second full pool during concatenation [morph2mol/retrieval.py](/morph2mol/retrieval.py#L120-L146). The `exclude` parameter drops specific objects at load (used when fitting fusion weights must exclude a query's own reference), and the uint8 source IDs it assigns are the reason for the 256-object ceiling [morph2mol/retrieval.py](/morph2mol/retrieval.py#L97-L112). What happens next — 50-neighbor selection per coverage group, tie-shared exponential weights at temperature 0.03, and fusion into direct predictions — is the domain of [Cluster Retrieval Mechanics](11-cluster-retrieval-mechanics) and [Gated Fusion Weights](12-gated-fusion-weights). Packaging the finished bank into a distributable release is covered by [Model Export and Release Packaging](17-model-export-and-release-packaging).

Sources: [morph2mol/retrieval.py](/morph2mol/retrieval.py#L97-L146), [docs/training.md](/docs/training.md#L119-L120)

## Key Takeaways

Bank construction in Morph2Mol is deliberately **conservative and self-verifying**: exhaustive (non-approximate) PCA and k-means on full populations, deterministic per-object seeding, population-level expression standardization with explicit floors, and hash-chained artifacts from creation through consumption. The `cache_fingerprint` turns the entire pipeline into a pure function of its declared inputs — identical inputs always yield an identical, resumable bank; any drift yields an immediately detectable mismatch rather than silent corruption. This is the foundation that makes retrieval-augmented prediction trustworthy: when you call [Cluster Retrieval Mechanics](11-cluster-retrieval-mechanics), you are querying summaries whose provenance can be re-verified in milliseconds from `complete.json` alone.


# Cluster Retrieval Mechanics



This page explains how Morph2Mol converts direct morphological predictions into retrieval-augmented ones. The engine lives in a single class — `ReferenceBank` — which indexes reference slides as *clusters* of ~100 cells, matches each target cell against cluster keys with exact fp16 cosine search, resolves cross-bank coverage groups, distributes tie weight fractionally at the k-th neighbor boundary, and aggregates standardized expression values from a flat GPU pool. The design goals are verifiable exactness (no ANN approximations), deterministic tie handling, and a strict NaN-based coverage contract consumed downstream by the gated fusion stage.

## Why Retrieval Indexes Clusters, Not Cells

The reference bank does not store per-cell entries. During bank construction, cells within each reference slide are k-means clustered into communities of `target_size=100` cells, and each community is summarized into two artifacts: a **cluster key** (the re-normalized mean of member cells' normalized Phase-1 features, cast to fp16) and a **cluster value** (the mean standardized log1p expression across the bank panel) [bank_builder.py](morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L48-L62). At inference time the relationship is deliberately asymmetric: the *query* is a single cell's raw Phase-1 feature vector, while the *index* consists of cluster keys. A target cell thus borrows expression from its 50 most morphologically similar reference communities.

This asymmetry is a noise-robustness trade-off rather than a pure compression choice:

| Dimension | Cluster-level index (chosen) | Cell-level index |
|---|---|---|
| Unit of retrieval | ~100-cell k-means community | Individual annotated cell |
| Key stability | Mean over members damps segmentation/registration noise | Sensitive to single-cell artifacts |
| Expression semantics | Smoothed population z-score per panel gene | Noisy per-cell measurements |
| Storage | #communities × #panel genes | #cells × #panel genes |
| Top-50 granularity | 50 communities ≈ up to ~5,000 cells of evidence | 50 individual cells |

Note that these *feature-space clusters* are unrelated to the *spatial target/context blocks* (≤128 cells) used for inference batching — the latter belong to [Spatial Context Blocking](19-spatial-context-blocking) and are configured independently at `TARGET_CELLS = 128` [recipe.py](morph2mol/recipe.py#L5), [predict/spatial_context.py](predict/spatial_context.py#L15-L26).

The bank itself carries the invariant `require(self.model['target_size'] == 100)` — a release built with any other community size is rejected outright [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L87).

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph Reference Bank (per object/slide)
        K1[Cluster keys<br/>fp16 1536-d, normalized] 
        V1[Cluster values<br/>z-scored log1p, bank panel]
        P1[Object panel<br/>gene id subset]
    end
    Q[Target cell<br/>raw Phase-1 1536-d] -->|L2-normalize, fp16| QN
    QN -->|exact cosine per object| K1
    K1 --> TB[Per-bank top-50]
    P1 --> CG{Coverage groups<br/>banks sharing a gene}
    TB --> CG
    CG --> TW[Tie-aware weights<br/>tau = 0.03]
    TW --> AGG[Weighted gather<br/>from flat value pool]
    V1 --> AGG
    AGG --> R[R matrix<br/>NaN = no coverage]
    R --> G[apply_gate fusion]
```

Sources: [bank_builder.py](morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L48-L62), [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L87), [recipe.py](morph2mol/recipe.py#L5)

## Bank Invariants Checked Before Any Query

`ReferenceBank.__init__` treats the bank directory as untrusted input. Before a single similarity score is computed, it verifies a chain of invariants that bind the bank to the exact model, gene space, and build configuration [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L77-L112):

| Check | Assertion | Failure meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Schema | `morph2mol-reference-bank` (or legacy alias) | Directory is not a bank |
| Fingerprint | SHA-256 of `model.json` identity equals `cache_fingerprint` [bank_io.py](morph2mol/bank_io.py#L30-L31) | Metadata edited after build |
| Cluster size | `target_size == 100` | Bank built with different clustering |
| Completion marker | `bank_complete.json` count matches `expected_objects` and fingerprint [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L89-L94) | Interrupted build |
| Retrieval contract | `retrieval_K == 50` and `tau == 0.03` | Bank/Search hyperparameters drift |
| Per-object metadata | `complete.json` object id and fingerprint | Stale or swapped object cache |
| Artifact integrity | All `ARTIFACTS` present; SHA-256 match when `verify_hashes=True` [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L104-L107) | Corrupt or missing `.npy` |
| Panel sanity | Unique gene ids within `[0, n_genes)` [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L108-L109) | Malformed panel |
| Object count | 1–256 objects | Hard limit from uint8 source ids [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L111) |

Loading is equally deliberate about memory. Every object's `values.npy` is opened as a read-only memmap, and a **single preallocated GPU pool** of float32 receives the flattened values exactly once — avoiding a second full expression pool during concatenation. Cluster keys are moved to device as fp16 `[N, 1536]`, and three index tensors are built: `row_start` (per-community address in the pool), `source` (uint8 object id per community), and `offsets` (global community id base per object) [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L120-L149). The artifacts themselves follow the protocol declared in [bank_io.py](morph2mol/bank_io.py#L10-L14): features use `masked_cell_features`, values use `standardized_log_expression`.

Sources: [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L77-L149), [bank_io.py](morph2mol/bank_io.py#L10-L31)

## Panel Adaptation: Coverage Groups and Column Maps

A target panel (e.g. `--genes xenium`) rarely matches any reference object's panel exactly, and different references may measure different gene subsets. `configure(panel)` precomputes the entire adaptation in one pass [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L151-L168):

1. **Coverage groups** — `groups_for` partitions query panel positions by *which* banks contain each gene: the group key is the tuple of bank indices whose panel includes the gene [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L70-L75). A gene present in objects 0 and 2 only forms its own group and will be retrieved against exactly those two indexes.
2. **Column map** — a `[n_banks, n_panel_genes]` int32 matrix mapping a (bank, global panel position) pair to that bank's local panel column, or `-1` when the bank does not measure the gene.
3. **Gene→group map and coverage mask** — `group_for_gene` assigns each panel position its group id (or `-1` for genes no reference measures), and `covered` is the boolean mask of supported genes.

The consequence is a precise definition of *retrieval coverage*: a gene is retrievable if and only if at least one excluded-filtered reference object measures it. Genes outside this set are never zero-filled — their output column stays NaN, and gene chunks during aggregation skip them entirely [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L222-L228). This NaN is not an error state; it is the deliberate handshake signal that the fusion stage consumes (see the final section).

Sources: [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L70-L75), [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L151-L168)

## Exact Cosine Search at Temperature 0.03

`retrieve(H, k=50)` begins by validating the query tensor with `original_keys`: it must be finite raw Phase-1 features of shape `[N, 1536]`, which are L2-normalized and cast to fp16 on device [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L64-L68). This is the *same* normalization used when bank cluster keys were built (cluster keys are normalized means of these normalized member features), so queries and keys occupy one identical metric space.

The search itself is exhaustive and documented as such — the source carries the comment *"Documented exact fp16 cosine, no PCA256/ANN candidate omissions"* [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L180-L188). Two exactness measures back this claim:

- **TF32 is disabled** for both matmul and cuDNN (`torch.backends.*.allow_tf32 = False`) so reduced-precision kernels cannot silently perturb scores [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L80-L81).
- **No index compression**: each object's keys are scored in full (`Q @ E.T`), queries processed in chunks of 256, and per-bank `topk(min(50, bank size))` retained with community ids offset into the global id space.

Neighbors are then resolved **per coverage group**, not per bank. For each group, the candidate lists of all member banks are concatenated; `effective_k = min(50, total candidates)` scores are selected, and the k-th score `theta` becomes a threshold [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L189-L200).

> [!TIP]
> The softmax denominator is computed *only* over the selected top-k scores, yet the numerator assigns fractional mass to *every* tied neighbor — potentially more ties than fit in top-k. This works because `fractional = (effective_k - n_gt) / n_eq` conserves tie mass exactly: `n_eq × fractional = effective_k − n_gt`, which equals the number of ties inside the top-k. Deleting the fractional trick in favor of naive weighting would break the sum-to-one invariant whenever the k-th score is tied.

Weight computation then proceeds [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L201-L213):

```python
theta = selected[:, -1:]                     # k-th score (the tie boundary)
mx    = selected[:, :1]                      # top-1 score (softmax stabilizer)
fractional = (effective_k - n_gt) / n_eq     # shared share per tied neighbor
denominator = exp((selected - mx)/TAU).sum() # over top-k only
mass = 1 if v > theta else fractional if v == theta else 0
w = exp((v - mx)/TAU) * mass / denominator
```

With `TAU = 0.03` [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L14), the weighting is sharply peaked: a neighbor 0.1 cosine below the query maximum receives roughly `exp(-3.3) ≈ 3.6%` of the top-1's weight, so retrieved expression is dominated by the handful of morphologically nearest communities.

Determinism is protected by a **retry protocol**. The retained candidate window is `k + tie_padding` wide (default 64), but the number of scores ≥ `theta` is counted over the *full* group candidate set. If any query/group needs more room than the window provides, `retrieve` recursively re-invokes itself with `tie_padding = required - k` so every threshold tie participates, then truncates the stacked result to the global `required` width [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L214-L221). A hard assertion verifies each weight row sums to 1 within `2e-5` before any aggregation happens.

Sources: [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L64-L68), [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L170-L221)

## Weighted Expression Aggregation from the Flat Pool

The final stage converts weight distributions into retrieved expression. Output is initialized to NaN for the whole `[N, G]` matrix, then filled gene-chunk-wise in blocks of 128 columns, skipping positions whose `group_for_gene` is `-1` [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L222-L239).

For each supported gene chunk, the gather pipeline is:

1. **Select neighbor cells** — `cells[q0:q1, groups, :]` picks, per query and per gene group, the retained community ids (a query gene supported by two banks reads the union of both banks' top-50 lists).
2. **Resolve object and column** — `source[chosen]` yields each neighbor's object id; `colmap[source, position]` maps it to that object's local expression column.
3. **Address the pool** — `row_start[chosen] + col` computes flat addresses directly into the single preallocated value pool.
4. **Weighted sum** — `output = Σ (w × expression)` over the neighbor axis.

> [!TIP]
> Query chunks during the gather are sized by a budget formula — `qstep = clamp(16_000_000 / (positions × required), 1, 256)` — keeping each transient gather under ~64 MiB of float32. Because community ids, source ids, and pool addresses are all precomputed tensors, no Python-level loop over neighbors or objects exists on the hot path.

`retrieve` returns the float32 NumPy matrix plus a statistics dictionary that inference code embeds into output metadata [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L240-L242):

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `max_retained_threshold_ties` | Widest tie set actually needed (drives the window width after retry) |
| `coverage_groups` | Number of distinct bank-subset groups for the query panel |
| `covered_genes` | Count of retrievable genes in the panel |

Sources: [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L222-L242)

## Integration in the Inference Pipeline

The CLI orchestrates retrieval in a narrow, memory-conscious window of the prediction run. After the full direct-pass matrix `A` is written and the vision model is deleted (freeing VRAM), retrieval begins [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L169-L188):

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Load Release with retrieval=True] --> B[bank = ReferenceBank paths bank, exclude set]
    B --> C["excluded = --exclude donors ∪ sample_id<br/>(self-reference exclusion)"]
    C --> D[bank.configure panel]
    D --> E[covered = bank.covered → var.covered column]
    E --> F["Per 256-cell batch:<br/>R = bank.retrieve H1, k=50"]
    F --> G["fused, beta = apply_gate A, R, panel, beta_map"]
    G --> H[Write R layer and fused X]
    H --> I{More batches?}
    I -->|yes| F
    I -->|no| J[Record K=50, tau=0.03,<br/>cluster_target_size=100, bank fingerprint,<br/>excluded objects into uns metadata]
```

Three aspects deserve attention. First, **self-reference exclusion**: the query slide's own `sample_id` (or `--sample-id`) is merged with any explicit `--exclude` donors before bank construction, so a slide can never retrieve from communities containing its own cells — the guard against leakage when predicting a reference slide itself [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L177-L182). Second, **query features are the raw Phase-1 embeddings** (`X_morph2mol_phase1`), encoded per target cell during the direct pass and persisted fp16 precisely so retrieval can replay them in batches of `--query-batch 256` [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L137-L164). Third, the run records the complete retrieval contract — `K=50`, `tau=0.03`, `cluster_target_size=100`, the bank fingerprint, and the resolved exclusion list — into `.uns['morph2mol']`, together with scale declarations: `R_scale` is *"per-reference population z score of log1p(counts)"* and `X_scale` is *"per-gene scores, not counts"* [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L189-L192).

A `--reference` calibration mode disables retrieval entirely (`Release(..., retrieval=not reference)`), writing only direct predictions as ground truth for fusion-weight fitting — that calibration workflow belongs to [Gated Fusion Weights](12-gated-fusion-weights) [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L50-L51), [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L109-L112).

Sources: [predict/predict.py](predict/predict.py#L137-L192)

## The NaN Contract: Where Retrieval Hands Off to Fusion

Retrieval's last responsibility is a clean interface with gating. `apply_gate` treats `R` as masked input: `covered = np.isfinite(R).all(0)` per gene, and any gene that arrives NaN — or whose transferred beta is non-finite — is forced to `beta = 1.0`, meaning the direct branch alone survives fusion [gate.py](morph2mol/gate.py#L96-L104). The code comments are explicit that letting a NaN propagate would silently blank the gene's entire column, which is why retrieval never zero-fills and the gate never trusts absent coverage.

Integrity also spans module boundaries at release load time. `Release` cross-checks that the bank's `checkpoint_sha256` and `gene_space_sha256` match the release's verified Stage-1 checkpoint and gene space, that the gate metadata carries the bank's `cache_fingerprint`, and that the gate's fitted `K`/`tau` equal the bank's `retrieval_K`/`tau` — a mismatch in any of these aborts before inference [release.py](morph2mol/release.py#L27-L45). In other words, a release cannot ship fusion weights fitted against a differently-configured retrieval contract. The artifact-side checksums (SHA-256 per `.npy`, enforced on every bank load) are covered operationally in [Release Integrity Verification](21-release-integrity-verification), and the full construction pipeline that produces these clusters is documented in [Reference Bank Construction](10-reference-bank-construction).

Sources: [gate.py](morph2mol/gate.py#L83-L104), [release.py](morph2mol/release.py#L27-L45)

## Where to Go Next

- [Reference Bank Construction](10-reference-bank-construction) — how communities, keys, values, and panels are built and fingerprinted upstream of this page's mechanics.
- [Gated Fusion Weights](12-gated-fusion-weights) — how the beta grid is fitted on calibration slides and how `apply_gate` consumes the NaN-coverage contract.
- [Spatial Context Blocking](19-spatial-context-blocking) — the *spatial* (not feature-space) blocking that batches cell crops during prediction.
- [Reading Prediction Outputs](4-reading-prediction-outputs) — where the `R` layer, `covered`/`beta` columns, and `.uns` retrieval metadata land in the `.h5ad` output.

# Gated Fusion Weights



Morph2Mol never asks you to trust a single predictor. Every target cell receives two expression estimates per gene: a **direct branch** `A` produced by the trained negative-binomial head, and a **retrieved branch** `R` assembled from matched reference communities in the expression bank. The *gated fusion* layer decides, **per gene**, how much weight each branch contributes to the final `X` matrix. This page explains the fusion contract, how the gate weights are fitted on measured reference slides, how stratum-specific weights are selected at inference, and how the whole chain stays provably consistent across a release. Deep implementation detail of the retrieval call itself is covered in [Cluster Retrieval Mechanics](11-cluster-retrieval-mechanics); here `R` is treated as an input.

## The Two-Branch Fusion Contract

The fusion is a scalar convex blend, applied independently for every gene `g` and every cell:

```
X[:, g] = beta[g] · A[:, g] + (1 − beta[g]) · R[:, g]
```

The convention matters: **`beta = 1` means "direct model only"**, and `beta = 0` means "retrieval only". The two branches are not on the same scale and do not have the same coverage, which is precisely why a per-gene gate exists rather than a global mixing constant:

| Property | Branch `A` (direct) | Branch `R` (retrieved) |
|---|---|---|
| Producer | Stage-2 encoder + NB expression head | `ReferenceBank.retrieve` over community summaries |
| Scale | `log1p(mu)` | per-reference population z-score of `log1p(counts)` |
| Coverage | every panel gene, always finite | only genes present in at least one reference panel; `NaN` elsewhere |
| Failure mode | runtime error on nonfinite output | silent absence (encoded as `NaN`) |

Both scales are declared verbatim in the prediction metadata (`A_scale`, `R_scale`, `X_scale`), and the gate file itself carries a `branches` block documenting the same triple — the fusion never hides what it is combining.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Direct["Branch A - direct model"]
        IMG["H&amp;E crop"] --> ENC["stage-2 encoder"] --> HEAD["NB head"] --> A["A = log1p(mu)"]
    end
    subgraph Retrieved["Branch R - retrieval"]
        H1["phase-1 features H1"] --> RK["cluster retrieval, K=50"] --> R["R = weighted community z"]
    end
    BETA["beta[g] per gene, from beta.json"] --> FUSE
    A --> FUSE["X = beta·A + (1-beta)·R"]
    R --> FUSE
    FUSE --> OUT["X matrix + var/beta + var/covered"]
```

Sources: [predict.py](predict/predict.py#L117-L122), [gate.py](morph2mol/gate.py#L83-L104), [fit_beta.py](train/fit_beta.py#L86-L89)

## Fitting Beta by Grid-Searched Correlation

The gate weight for each gene is fitted on **reference slides whose measured expression you are allowed to read**. The objective is deliberately simple: choose the `beta` in `[0, 1]` that maximizes the Pearson correlation between the blended prediction and the measured log1p counts, per gene. Because a correlation of a blend is smooth but **not concave** in `beta`, the implementation rejects a closed-form solution in favor of a fixed 41-point grid (`GRID = linspace(0, 1, 41)`), which is both robust and cheap at this size.

The fitting kernel in `_fit_gene_chunk` follows a precise recipe. All three arrays are column-centred first (`_centred`), the |Y| norm is precomputed once, and then each grid point evaluates `per_gene_pcc_blend`, a vectorized Pearson computation over all genes simultaneously. Two eligibility rules gate which genes are fitted at all (`_fit_eligible`): the retrieved column must be finite for every cell, and the measured labels must actually vary (constant genes carry no correlation signal). Genes that fail — most importantly genes with no retrieval coverage — are pinned to `beta = 1.0`, i.e., the direct branch stands alone.

> [!TIP]
> Ties on the correlation grid are broken toward the **larger** beta (`(p == best) &amp; (b > beta)` in the grid loop). When two blend ratios correlate identically with the measured labels, the system prefers the direct model — a quiet anti-retrieval bias that avoids handing genes to the retrieval branch without measurable benefit.

To bound temporary memory on whole-slide fits, `fit_beta` processes genes in chunks of 128, allocating only the output vectors up front and copying each chunk of `A`, `R`, `Y` before the centring pass. The returned pair is `(beta [G], pcc_at_beta [G])` — the achieved correlation is kept alongside the weight so downstream aggregation and diagnostics can inspect fit quality per gene.

| Design decision | Implementation | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| 41-point grid, not calculus | `GRID` sweep in `_fit_gene_chunk` | correlation-of-blend objective is smooth but not concave in beta |
| Gene chunking at 128 | column slicing inside `fit_beta` | bounds peak temporary memory per slide |
| Eligibility filter | `_fit_eligible` | variance-free or never-covered genes cannot be fitted meaningfully |
| Coverage fallback | `beta[~covered] = 1.0` | genes without retrieval must not be dragged by zero-filled `R` |

Sources: [gate.py](morph2mol/gate.py#L5-L18), [gate.py](morph2mol/gate.py#L33-L63), [gate.py](morph2mol/gate.py#L66-L80)

## From Reference Slides to a Gate File

The `train/fit_beta.py` entry point orchestrates the fitting campaign and enforces the hygiene that makes the transferred weights trustworthy. Before any statistics are computed, it verifies that the bank's `checkpoint_sha256` and `gene_space_sha256` match the release, and that every requested fitting reference belongs to the **approved `gate_fit_references` split** of the training contract — gate fitting is a privilege of held-out, contract-approved slides, not an ad-hoc operation.

Each reference then goes through a leakage-controlled calibration loop:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S0["load release, gene space, bank model.json"] --> S1["verify stage1/gene_space identity vs bank"]
    S1 --> S2["contract check: refs subset of gate_fit_references"]
    S2 --> S3["per reference: seeded subsample of max_cells (default 20000)"]
    S3 --> S4["A = direct.h5ad layers/A, hashes checked"]
    S4 --> S5["Y = measured log1p counts from dataset"]
    S5 --> S6["exclude self + shared donor/block origin groups"]
    S6 --> S7["R = bank.retrieve(H1, 50)"]
    S7 --> S8["fit_beta: 41-point grid per gene"]
    S8 --> S9{"tissue known?"}
    S9 -- yes --> S10["group under tissue/wide or tissue/narrow"]
    S9 -- no --> S11["contributes to global only"]
    S10 --> S12["mean-aggregate into strata + global"]
    S11 --> S12
    S12 --> S13["write beta.json + beta.meta.json"]
```

Three details in this loop deserve attention. First, the labels `Y` are **measured log1p counts read from the dataset**, not the z-scored values the bank stores — the code comments this distinction explicitly, since silently fitting against bank `Y.npy` would optimize against the wrong scale. Second, retrieval during fitting is **leave-one-out**: `reference_exclusions` removes the sample itself *and transitively expands* any shared `donor_or_block_id` groups from the bank, so a slide is never scored against communities that include its own donor or block. Third, the direct predictions are validated to belong to the exact release checkpoints before use.

The per-reference fits are then aggregated by plain averaging of each gene's beta into a hierarchy: tissue-and-panel-width **strata** (keys like `lung/wide`) and a `global` pool. The resulting `beta.json` is a self-describing artifact whose schema the selection rules at inference time depend on:

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `version` | `"per_gene"` — gene-wise weights, not a scalar |
| `fallback` | `"same_tissue"` — stratum fallback policy |
| `tissue_casefold` | tissue names matched case-insensitively |
| `panel_cut` | gene-count threshold (1000) separating `wide` from `narrow` panels |
| `min_refs` | minimum number of references for a stratum to be eligible |
| `strata_order` | deterministic tie-break order over `tissue/width` keys |
| `strata` | `{tissue/width: {n_refs, beta}}` maps |
| `global` | `{n_refs, beta}` over all fitting references |
| `fit_signature.genes` | SHA-256 of the ordered gene list the betas were fitted against |
| `branches` | documentation of the `A`, `R`, and fusion scales |

Alongside `beta.json`, a `beta.meta.json` records the provenance needed later: the gate's own SHA-256, both checkpoint hashes, the gene-space hash, the bank `cache_fingerprint`, the retrieval settings (`K=50, tau=0.03`), the reference list with its exclusions, the calibration subsample size and seed, and the spatial-context prediction protocol.

Sources: [fit_beta.py](train/fit_beta.py#L28-L38), [fit_beta.py](train/fit_beta.py#L43-L79), [tissue.py](morph2mol/tissue.py#L43-L56), [fit_beta.py](train/fit_beta.py#L81-L99)

## Stratum Selection Rules at Inference

When a target slide arrives, the fusion weight vector is not recomputed — it is **selected** from the shipped hierarchy by `select_gate` in `gate_rules.py`. The selection dimension is a two-part key: the tissue (user-supplied via `--tissue`) and the panel width, derived automatically as `wide` when the requested gene count is at least `panel_cut` (1000) and `narrow` otherwise.

The algorithm in `select_gate_source` is a small state machine with strict validation. Only strata with `n_refs >= min_refs` are eligible. Stratum keys are parsed as `tissue/width`, and any key whose width component is not exactly `narrow` or `wide` is rejected outright. If `tissue_casefold` is set, both stratum names and the target tissue are passed through `tissue_key` (strip + casefold) before comparison, and **case-equivalent strata in the same file are treated as a refit-required error** rather than silently resolved. The target tissue itself may carry an explicit width override (`lung/wide`), which is validated and split before lookup. Resolution then proceeds by exact match on `tissue/width`, followed by the first same-tissue entry in `strata_order`, and finally the `global` pool — which is also the outcome for an unknown or omitted tissue, matching the CLI help ("omitted or unknown uses global weights").

One further guard runs before any of this: `validate_gate_genes` hashes the target's ordered gene list and compares it to `fit_signature.genes`. Because betas are stored against **integer global gene IDs**, applying them under a different gene head ordering would be a silent misalignment; the hash check turns that into a hard "refit the gate" error.

| Target request | Resolution outcome |
|---|---|
| `lung`, 4000 genes, `lung/wide` eligible | exact stratum `lung/wide` |
| `lung/wide`, 300 genes | explicit width override wins → `lung/wide` |
| `Lung`, casefold enabled | matches strata under casefolded tissue |
| `lung`, but `lung/narrow` only, width `narrow` | `lung/narrow` via `strata_order` |
| `brain`, no `brain` stratum | `global` |
| stratum with `n_refs < min_refs` | not eligible; falls through the chain |

Sources: [gate_rules.py](morph2mol/gate_rules.py#L7-L13), [gate_rules.py](morph2mol/gate_rules.py#L16-L43), [gate_rules.py](morph2mol/gate_rules.py#L46-L49), [tissue.py](morph2mol/tissue.py#L7-L8), [predict.py](predict/predict.py#L20-L20)

## Applying the Gate on a Target Slide

Fusion at inference is isolated in `apply_gate` with an explicit contract: **nothing here reads the target's labels**. The function receives the direct predictions `A`, the retrieved matrix `R` (with `NaN` marking uncovered genes), the panel of global gene IDs, and the selected `beta_by_gene` map. It assembles the per-gene beta vector by lookup with `default = 1.0`, then applies three defensive normalizations that jointly guarantee the blend degrades gracefully to the direct branch.

The ordering of these guards is load-bearing. Betas that are missing from the map, or arrive as `NaN`, become `1.0` — the inline comment explains why: a nonfinite beta let through would silently blank that gene's entire column. Next, beta values outside `[0, 1]` raise immediately, since a transferred file should never contain out-of-range weights. Finally, **wherever `R` is not fully finite, beta is forced to `1.0` before the `nan_to_num` sanitization**, so the zero-filled retrieval values can never contaminate the blend — for uncovered genes the fused output is exactly `A`.

> [!TIP]
> The `NaN` handling is an ordering constraint, not just validation: `R`'s blanks are converted to `0.0` *after* the covered-mask forces `beta = 1.0`. If the conversion ran first, an uncovered gene blended at `beta &lt; 1` would be dragged toward zero by the zero-filled retrieval values instead of cleanly falling back to the direct branch.

In `predict/predict.py`, fusion is the final phase of the streaming pipeline. The model pass runs first over spatial-context blocks, writing `layers/A` and the phase-1 features; the model and its GPU memory are then explicitly released before the retrieval bank is opened with the target itself and any `--exclude` objects removed. For each query batch, `bank.retrieve` produces `R`, `apply_gate` fuses it into `X`, and both are streamed to disk. The gate leaves an auditable trace in the output file:

| Output artifact | Content |
|---|---|
| `X` (top-level matrix) | fused predictions, declared as `beta*A+(1-beta)*R; per-gene scores, not counts` |
| `layers/A` | direct branch, kept for inspection |
| `layers/R` | raw retrieved branch, kept for inspection |
| `var['beta']` | the beta actually applied per output gene (all ones in `--reference` mode) |
| `var['covered']` | which genes had any retrieval coverage |
| `uns['morph2mol'].gate_source` | the resolved stratum key, e.g. `lung/wide` or `global` |

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant P as predict.py
    participant GR as gate_rules
    participant M as Morph2Mol model
    participant B as ReferenceBank
    participant G as gate.apply_gate
    P->>GR: validate_gate_genes(release.gate, genes)
    P->>GR: select_gate(release.gate, --tissue, n_genes)
    GR-->>P: source stratum + beta_map
    loop spatial context blocks
        P->>M: encode + decode(panel)
        M-->>P: A, z
        P->>P: stream layers/A, H1
    end
    P->>B: ReferenceBank(bank, exclude target)
    loop query batches
        P->>B: retrieve(H1, 50)
        B-->>P: R (NaN = uncovered)
        P->>G: apply_gate(A, R, panel, beta_map)
        G-->>P: fused X, beta used
        P->>P: stream layers/R, X
    end
    P->>P: var/beta, var/covered, uns gate_source
```

Sources: [gate.py](morph2mol/gate.py#L83-L104), [predict.py](predict/predict.py#L108-L112), [predict.py](predict/predict.py#L175-L193)

## Provenance and Integrity of a Shipped Gate

A gate file is only meaningful for one exact combination of checkpoints, gene space, and bank. The release loader turns that statement into mechanical verification: on construction with retrieval enabled, `Release` reads `beta.json` and `beta.meta.json` and cross-checks seven identities before any prediction is allowed. Any mismatch aborts with "Model checkpoints, genes, reference bank and fusion weights do not match" — including the subtle case where the gate was fitted under different retrieval settings (`K`, `tau`) than the shipped bank uses.

| Integrity check | Gate-side value | Compared against |
|---|---|---|
| gate file hash | `gate_meta['gate_sha256']` | SHA-256 of shipped `beta.json` |
| alignment checkpoint | `gate_meta['checkpoint_sha256']` | release `stage1` hash |
| expression checkpoint | `gate_meta['stage2_checkpoint_sha256']` | release `stage2` hash |
| gene space | `gate_meta['gene_space_sha256']` | release `gene_space` hash |
| bank identity | `gate_meta['cache_fingerprint']` | bank `cache_fingerprint` |
| retrieval settings | `gate_meta['K']`, `gate_meta['tau']` | bank `retrieval_K`, `tau` |
| gene head ordering | `fit_signature.genes` | SHA-256 of target gene list at predict time |

Packaging enforces the pairing at export time too: `export_release.py` refuses to ship a bank without a gate or vice versa ("Supply both --bank and --beta"), copies both `beta.json` and its `.meta.json` into the release, and registers the gate path in `release.json`. The result is a release in which fusion weights cannot drift away from the model, the bank, or the gene head — and a per-slide, per-gene audit trail in every prediction output.

Sources: [release.py](morph2mol/release.py#L27-L45), [export_release.py](train/export_release.py#L50-L55), [predict.py](predict/predict.py#L117-L122)

## Where to Go Next

The gate is the last hop of the retrieval-augmented path. To understand where `R` comes from — cluster keys, temperature-weighted community blending, and coverage semantics — read [Cluster Retrieval Mechanics](11-cluster-retrieval-mechanics), and see how those per-slide artifacts are produced in [Reference Bank Construction](10-reference-bank-construction). The `A` branch's training story, including the gene head the `fit_signature` protects, is covered in [Stage 2 Expression Training](15-stage-2-expression-training) and packaged end-to-end in [Model Export and Release Packaging](17-model-export-and-release-packaging). For how to interpret `var['beta']` and `var['covered']` in a real prediction file, see [Reading Prediction Outputs](4-reading-prediction-outputs).

# Training Data Contracts



Training in Morph2Mol runs over expensive distributed jobs on large corpora, so the pipeline treats its input data as a formal contract rather than a loose convention. This page explains the *contract layer*: the corpus layout, the split topology, the per-slide and per-cell file guarantees, the gene-space rules, and the identity artifacts that bind checkpoints, caches, and resumes to exactly the data they were built from. The authoritative implementation is `morph2mol/training_contract.py`, a dependency-free module of pure validation functions that every training entry point imports before touching data. Training mechanics themselves — what the loss optimizes or how batches are scheduled — are covered in [Stage 1 Contrastive Alignment](14-stage-1-contrastive-alignment) and [Stage 2 Expression Training](15-stage-2-expression-training); this page stays strictly on the *data rules* those stages enforce.

## The Contract Kernel and Its Enforcement Layers

The design separates **contract definition** (what valid data looks like) from **contract enforcement** (where it is checked). The kernel module contains no PyTorch or training logic — only `Path`, `hashlib`, and `json` — which makes it importable from preparation scripts, both training stages, and the resume layer without coupling any of them. Each stage re-derives the contract from disk at startup rather than trusting a stored copy, and checkpoints that claim to be trained on a corpus embed the full contract dict verbatim for later comparison.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Corpus["Corpus on disk — ground truth"]
        MAN["MANIFEST.csv"]
        SP["splits/*.txt — 6 files"]
        OBJ["training_set/{xenium,cosmx}/TISSUE/SAMPLE/..."]
        META["metadata/shared_origin_groups.csv"]
    end
    subgraph Kernel["morph2mol/training_contract.py"]
        DC["dataset_contract()"]
        CM["check_members()"]
        SS["stage1_steps()"]
        CH["check_checkpoint()"]
        GH["gene_hash()"]
        CI["checkpoint_identity()"]
        LL["load_lora_checked()"]
    end
    subgraph Consumers["Pipeline entry points"]
        PREP["train/prepare.py"]
        S1["Stage 1 entry"]
        S2["Stage 2 entry"]
        RES["training_resume.py"]
    end
    MAN --> DC
    SP --> DC
    DC --> PREP
    DC --> S1
    DC --> S2
    S1 --> CM
    S2 --> CM
    SS --> S1
    CH --> S2
    GH --> S2
    CI --> S2
    LL --> S2
    DC --> RES
```

Sources: [training_contract.py](morph2mol/training_contract.py#L1-L78), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L136-L137), [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L113-L114), [prepare.py](train/prepare.py#L18-L21)

## Corpus Layout and Split Topology

A valid corpus is a directory with a `MANIFEST.csv` at its root, one subdirectory per split (`training_set/{xenium,cosmx}/TISSUE/SAMPLE` and `cross_slide_test_set/...`), a `splits/` folder of six text files, and an optional `metadata/shared_origin_groups.csv` for donor/block grouping. Each split file holds one globally unique sample name per line; blank lines are skipped and `#` lines are treated as comments. Reading a split file that contains a duplicate name is an immediate error — identity is enforced at the text level before any set logic runs.

```text
corpus/
  MANIFEST.csv
  training_set/{xenium,cosmx}/TISSUE/SAMPLE/...
  cross_slide_test_set/{xenium,cosmx}/TISSUE/SAMPLE/...
  splits/
    training_set.txt
    inslide_test_set.txt
    cross_slide_test_set.txt
    stage2_global_training.txt
    retrieval_references.txt
    gate_fit_references.txt
  metadata/shared_origin_groups.csv
```

Sources: [docs/training.md](docs/training.md#L17-L30), [training_contract.py](morph2mol/training_contract.py#L7-L11)

The six split files are not independent lists — they are bound by a set algebra that `dataset_contract()` evaluates on every run. Four invariants must hold simultaneously, and a violation of any one aborts startup with a single `Invalid Stage1/Stage2/test split` error:

| Invariant | Set expression | Why it exists |
| --- | --- | --- |
| In-slide holdout nesting | `inslide_test_set ⊆ training_set` | Held-out cells live *inside* training slides, so their slides must appear in the training split |
| Cross-slide disjointness | `training_set ∩ cross_slide_test_set = ∅` | Cross-slide generalization requires fully unseen slides |
| Stage-2 derivation | `stage2_global_training = training_set − inslide_test_set` | Expression training excludes in-slide test cells; the set is *exact*, not approximate |
| Reference-set equality | `retrieval_references = gate_fit_references = stage2_global_training` | Both downstream reference sets must match Stage-2 training and exclude all test objects |

Beyond the ID lists, `dataset_contract()` hashes the raw bytes of `MANIFEST.csv` into `manifest_sha256`, and resolves the dataset root to an absolute path. The returned dict — six ID lists, the resolved root, and the manifest hash — becomes the canonical `contract` object threaded through every later check. Because Stage 1 writes this dict verbatim into checkpoints as `run_contract`, any later comparison of `run_contract` against a freshly derived contract transitively pins the sample sets *and* the manifest bytes.

> [!TIP]
> The four invariants are **interdependent equations**, not independent rules: adding one sample to `inslide_test_set.txt` silently reshapes `stage2_global_training`, `retrieval_references`, and `gate_fit_references` in the same run. Enforcement happens at training start, not at corpus preparation time — so validate your splits with `dataset_contract()` before committing to an expensive multi-day run.

Sources: [training_contract.py](morph2mol/training_contract.py#L14-L28), [docs/training.md](docs/training.md#L32-L34)

```mermaid
graph LR
    TR["training_set<br/>(image–RNA alignment)"] -- "superset" --> IT["inslide_test_set<br/>(held-out cells within training slides)"]
    TR -- "training − inslide" ==> S2["stage2_global_training<br/>(expression training)"]
    S2 == "exact equality" ==> RR["retrieval_references"]
    S2 == "exact equality" ==> GR["gate_fit_references"]
    CT["cross_slide_test_set"] -. "disjoint from training_set" .- TR
```

## Object Identity: Resolving a Sample Name

Sample names in split files are logical identifiers; the corpus resolves them to directories through `object_directory()` in `morph2mol/tissue.py`. Resolution globs the pattern `*/*/*/{sample}` under the corpus root — that is `{split_root}/{platform}/{tissue}/{sample}` — and rejects anything under a directory containing `rawdata`. Two uniqueness conditions must hold: the resolved absolute paths must collapse to exactly one, and the tissue-level parent directory name (compared case-insensitively) must be unique across all matches. When a sample physically exists under both `training_set/` and another split root, the `training_set/` copy is preferred.

> [!TIP]
> The `training_set` preference combined with the *cross-root* ambiguity check means sample names must be globally unique across the entire corpus — not just within one split file. A name reused under different platforms or tissue directories fails with `ambiguous corpus objects`, because path resolution cannot disambiguate which slide a split line refers to.

The same module defines two auxiliary contracts used downstream. `read_tissue_map()` validates the organ-annotation CSV: it must contain `sample` and `tissue` columns, samples must be non-empty and unique, and organ names must match `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*` after casefolding. `reference_exclusions()` reads `metadata/shared_origin_groups.csv` (rows of `field=donor_or_block_id`, semicolon-separated `samples`) and computes the *transitive closure* of excluded samples starting from a query reference — so if blocks A and B share a donor, fitting fusion weights for A also excludes B, and anything else grouped with B.

Sources: [tissue.py](morph2mol/tissue.py#L11-L19), [tissue.py](morph2mol/tissue.py#L22-L37), [tissue.py](morph2mol/tissue.py#L43-L56)

## The Prepared-Slide File Contract

Every sample directory in the corpus must follow the prepared-slide format. Three of these files are load-bearing for training: `dataset.json` pins geometry, `manifest.csv.gz` maps expression rows to crop paths, and `expression.npz` + `genes.tsv` define the count matrix and its gene order. `train/prepare.py` re-validates the geometry contract per object: `patch_size` must be exactly `224` (pixels) and `patch_size_um` exactly `55` (µm), fixing `um_per_px` at 55/224 throughout the pipeline.

| File | Required contract | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dataset.json` | `patch_size = 224`, `patch_size_um = 55`, plus `um_per_pixel_source` | `prepare.py`, Stage 2 `LiveStore` |
| `manifest.csv.gz` | CSV with `expr_row`, `patch_path` columns; paths relative to the slide directory | `cells_of()`, `load_slide_npz()` |
| `patch_cell_boundaries.npz` | `expr_rows` [N], `indptr` [N+1], `vertex_x_patch`/`vertex_y_patch`, `y_pixel`/`x_pixel`, scalar `output_size` | `cells_of()`, `load_slide_npz()` |
| `expression.npz` | SciPy CSR raw counts, rows matching expression-row space | `training_slides()`, `LiveStore` |
| `genes.tsv` | Tab-separated, header + gene symbols in first column | `prepare.py`, `LiveStore` |

Protein, control, and non-gene channels must be filtered out *before* corpus preparation — the contract layer trusts that what remains in `genes.tsv` are RNA gene symbols. The optional `cells.npz` fields documented for prediction inputs (centroids, polygons, optional `mpp`) are the upstream source format; training consumes only the prepared derivatives above.

Sources: [docs/formats.md](docs/formats.md#L17-L39), [prepare.py](train/prepare.py#L27-L33), [docs/training.md](docs/training.md#L32-L34)

## Cell-Level Input Guarantees

Two functions translate the per-slide files into training-ready cell records, and both guarantee the same three invariants: every expression row has exactly one crop path, every cell has a normalized 16×16 mask, and cell ordering follows boundary-row order. `load_slide_npz()` (Stage 1) and `cells_of()` (Stage 2) rasterize each polygon into a 224×224 binary image via `output_size`, then area-pool it into a 16×16 float mask by block averaging — which requires `output_size` to be divisible by 16. Polygons with fewer than three vertices rasterize to empty; rather than dropping the cell, the mask falls back to a single central token (`w[8,8] = 1.0`), then the whole mask is divided by its sum so it is always a probability distribution.

The crop-path lookup itself is a contract: `manifest.csv.gz` is deduplicated on `expr_row` and indexed, and any boundary row whose `expr_row` lacks a manifest entry would raise a `KeyError` at data-build time — the "every boundary row must have a crop" rule is enforced implicitly by construction. In Stage 2, `LiveStore` additionally converts `y_pixel`/`x_pixel` centroids to microns using the slide's own `um_per_pixel_source` from `dataset.json`, so spatial distances in the decoder are physically meaningful regardless of the scanner's native resolution.

Sources: [contrastive.py](morph2mol/training/contrastive.py#L50-L64), [cell_inputs.py](morph2mol/training/cell_inputs.py#L5-L26), [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L40-L41)

## Gene Space: The Global Gene Contract

The gene axis has its own contract chain. `train/prepare.py` consumes a gene-embedding NPZ (ordered symbols `genes` + float32 `emb` [G, 512]) and validates it structurally: 2-D, 512 columns, one row per symbol, all symbols unique, all values finite. It then walks every object in `training_set ∪ cross_slide_test_set`, reads each slide's `genes.tsv` symbols, and emits three artifacts into `work/direct/`:

| Artifact | Contents | Downstream consumer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gene_space_all.npz` | `genes`, `gene_emb`, per-object `objects`/`platform`/`split` arrays, boolean `panel_mask` [objects × G], `um_per_px = 55/224` | Stage 2, release export |
| `gene_space_xen.npz` | Gene subset measured on Xenium **training** slides only | Xenium-constrained export |
| `gene_emb_scgpt.npz` | `genes` + `emb`, verbatim from the input table | Stage 2 expression head |

The Xenium subset rule is a one-way door: symbols accumulate only from training-split slides with `platform == 0`, so held-out slides never widen the exported gene space — matching the documented rule that the gene list is the sorted union of *training-split* genes and held-out slides contribute none. Within Stage 2, each `LiveStore` maps its slide's `genes.tsv` columns onto the global gene space via a first-occurrence-wins rule (duplicated symbols within a slide are silently collapsed to the first column), producing `head_idx` — the contract that targets written into the loss use a consistent global gene ordering.

Identity on this axis is a hash: `gene_hash()` computes the SHA-256 of the JSON-serialized ordered gene list, and `check_checkpoint()` rejects any Stage-2 initialization whose stored `gene_head_sha256` differs from the current run's genes — reordering or re-subsetting the gene space invalidates every existing checkpoint.

Sources: [prepare.py](train/prepare.py#L21-L43), [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L52-L66), [training_contract.py](morph2mol/training_contract.py#L39-L40), [docs/training.md](docs/training.md#L47-L56)

## Runtime Enforcement at Training Entry

Both training stages run the same three-step verification sequence before building any tensors: derive the contract from disk, resolve the physical sample directories, and compare the resolved membership against the contract with exact set equality. `check_members()` distinguishes the two stages by key — Stage 1 checks against `training_set`, Stage 2 against `stage2_global_training` — and its error message enumerates the *missing* and *extra* samples, which makes split-file drift immediately diagnosable. Stage 1 resolves slides by walking `training_set/{xenium,cosmx}/*/*` on disk and requires a 512-dimensional scGPT embedding file per slide whose row count equals the slide's `expression.npz` row count; Stage 2 iterates the contract's own ID list through `object_directory()` and then re-checks membership as a guard against resolution drift.

| Stage | Check | Enforcement site | Failure signal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stage 1 | Embedding file exists, 2-D, width 512 | `target_path()` | `Missing scGPT embeddings` / `expected 512-dimensional` |
| Stage 1 | Embedding rows == expression rows | `target_path()` | `not aligned with expression rows` |
| Stage 1 | Resolved slides == `training_set`, no duplicates | `check_members()` | missing/extra sample lists |
| Stage 1 | ≥ 1 full optimizer batch; positive budget | `stage1_steps()` | `No full optimizer batch` |
| Stage 1 | Supervised cells == dataset size, exactly once per epoch | epoch-end all-reduce | `did not cover every usable cell exactly once` |
| Stage 2 | Resolved stores == `stage2_global_training` | `check_members()` | missing/extra sample lists |
| Stage 2 | Stage-1 ckpt: completed 3 epochs, scGPT target | inline in `main()` | `Initialize ... with a completed ... Stage-1 checkpoint` |
| Stage 2 | `gene_space_all` genes == `gene_emb_scgpt` genes | array equality | `gene embeddings and output gene order differ` |

The Stage-1 usable-cell rule deserves note: during cache building, cells whose embedding rows have zero magnitude are dropped, and every downstream budget — `stage1_steps()`, the coverage check, `data_identity` — is computed against the *filtered* count. A silent embedding-quality problem therefore surfaces as a smaller-than-expected corpus rather than a NaN deep in training. The final Stage-1 safety net is exact per-epoch coverage: after each epoch, ranks all-reduce their supervised counts and the run aborts if the total is not exactly one pass over the usable dataset.

Sources: [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L19-L41), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L44-L63), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L162-L163), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L206-L209), [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L113-L137), [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L154-L156), [training_contract.py](morph2mol/training_contract.py#L52-L58)

## Checkpoint Binding: The Identity Chain

Checkpoints are not just weights — they are notarized snapshots of the contract state under which they were produced. Stage 1's `saved_state()` embeds the full `run_contract`, an `init_hash` (a 16-hex digest over all trainable adapter and tower tensors at initialization), the DDP `world_size`, the `data_identity` dict, the coverage cursor, and per-rank RNG states. Stage 2 then chains three verifications against a Stage-1 checkpoint: `check_checkpoint()` compares the embedded `run_contract` with the freshly derived contract; `load_lora_checked(enc, ck['lora'], complete=True)` requires the LoRA key set to be *exactly* all parameters ending in `.A`/`.B` with matching shapes; and `checkpoint_identity()` hashes the Stage-1 file itself into `stage1_identity['sha256']`, which Stage 2 stores in its own checkpoints and later resume checks compare byte-for-byte.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant S2 as Stage 2 main()
    participant TC as training_contract
    participant FS as Filesystem
    S2->>FS: dataset_contract(dataset)
    FS-->>S2: contract (IDs + manifest_sha256)
    S2->>TC: check_members(contract, "stage2", store objects)
    S2->>FS: torch.load(stage1 checkpoint)
    S2->>TC: check_checkpoint(ck, contract)
    TC->>TC: ck.run_contract == contract ?
    S2->>TC: load_lora_checked(enc, ck.lora, complete=True)
    TC->>TC: all .A/.B keys present, shapes match
    S2->>TC: checkpoint_identity(stage1 file)
    Note over S2: sha256 stored as stage1_identity for resume checks
```

The resume layer extends the same discipline to *recipe* reproducibility: `check_stage1_resume()` and `check_stage2_resume()` compare every key in fixed recipe lists (`STAGE1_RECIPE`, `STAGE2_RECIPE` — learning rates, LoRA geometry, epochs, seeds, coverage parameters) between the checkpoint's stored args and the current invocation, alongside contract equality, world-size equality, data identity, and cursor consistency. A resume is only accepted when the corpus, the data order, the initialization, and the hyperparameters are all provably unchanged.

| Identity artifact | Computed from | Bound by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `manifest_sha256` | Raw bytes of `MANIFEST.csv` | Inside `run_contract`, compared in `check_checkpoint()` |
| `run_contract` | Six split sets + resolved root + manifest hash | Written into every Stage-1 checkpoint |
| `data_identity` | Cell count, object order, cache metadata hash | Stage-1 resume equality |
| `init_hash` | Initial adapter + tower tensor bytes | Stage-1 resume equality |
| `gene_head_sha256` | `gene_hash(ordered gene list)` | Stage-2 init and resume |
| `stage1_identity.sha256` | Bytes of the Stage-1 checkpoint file | Stage-2 run and resume |
| Cache `signature` | File stamps / array digests | Stale-cache rejection (see below) |

Sources: [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L145-L176), [training_contract.py](morph2mol/training_contract.py#L43-L78), [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L144-L164), [training_resume.py](morph2mol/training_resume.py#L99-L153)

## Consistency Signatures for Derived Arrays

Training never re-reads raw PNGs for repeated runs; instead it caches derived arrays (Stage-1 crop paths, masks, embedding targets; Stage-2 mask and target matrices) under signatures computed from the sources. `file_stamp()` captures a source file's resolved path, size, and nanosecond mtime; `array_stamp()` SHA-256s an index array's bytes; `cached_arrays()` publishes arrays atomically under a write lock and stores the signature in `metadata.json` *last*. A cache whose stored signature differs from the freshly computed one is rejected outright — the contract layer refuses to silently reuse arrays derived from changed inputs rather than rebuilding them. The full mechanics of resume cursors and cache sharing belong to [Resume, Caching, and Reproducibility](16-resume-caching-and-reproducibility); from the contract perspective, the important point is that every cached artifact carries a verifiable provenance signature, and Stage-1's `stage1_data_identity()` folds those cache signatures into the checkpoint's identity chain.

Sources: [training_cache.py](morph2mol/training_cache.py#L10-L49), [training_resume.py](morph2mol/training_resume.py#L85-L96), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L44-L63)

## Common Failure Modes

Because every check fails fast with an explicit message, most contract violations are diagnosable from the error text alone. The table below maps the most frequent operator mistakes to their enforcement sites:

| Symptom (error message) | Root cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Duplicate samples: {path}` | A sample listed twice in a split file | De-duplicate the split file; duplicates are never merged |
| `Invalid Stage1/Stage2/test split` | One of the four set invariants broken | Re-derive `stage2_global_training` / reference lists from the other splits |
| `{key} must match Stage-2 training and exclude all test objects` | `retrieval_references` or `gate_fit_references` drifted from `stage2_global_training` | Regenerate both reference lists to equal the Stage-2 set |
| `{sample}: ambiguous corpus objects` | Sample name reused across platforms/tissues, or present in multiple split roots | Enforce globally unique sample names in the corpus |
| `Checkpoint training split differs from the current corpus` | Corpus or `MANIFEST.csv` changed since the checkpoint was written | Re-derive and confirm the split sets; retrain or restore the original corpus |
| `Checkpoint gene-head order differs from this run` | Gene space reordered or re-subsetted after the checkpoint | Regenerate `gene_emb_scgpt.npz`/gene table in the original order |
| `Stale training cache: {root}` | Source files changed under an existing cache directory | Point at a fresh cache directory; never edit sources in place mid-run |
| `Stage-1 data order/cache identity changed` | Object order or cached-array content differs on resume | Resume with identical corpus state and cache contents |

Sources: [training_contract.py](morph2mol/training_contract.py#L7-L65), [tissue.py](morph2mol/tissue.py#L11-L19), [training_cache.py](morph2mol/training_cache.py#L20-L37), [training_resume.py](morph2mol/training_resume.py#L106-L128)

## Where to Go Next

The contract layer is the entry gate to the rest of the training pipeline. To see what happens after these checks pass — the symmetric contrastive alignment itself — continue to [Stage 1 Contrastive Alignment](14-stage-1-contrastive-alignment); for the spatial decoder and negative-binomial training that consumes the Stage-2 set, see [Stage 2 Expression Training](15-stage-2-expression-training). The signature mechanics summarized above are expanded in [Resume, Caching, and Reproducibility](16-resume-caching-and-reproducibility), and the downstream consumers of the reference split files are covered in [Reference Bank Construction](10-reference-bank-construction) and [Model Export and Release Packaging](17-model-export-and-release-packaging).

# Stage 1 Contrastive Alignment



Stage 1 is the first trainable phase of the Morph2Mol-25M pipeline: it teaches a frozen UNI2-h vision encoder — augmented with low-rank LoRA adapters — to place each cell's morphology in the same 128-dimensional space as that cell's precomputed scGPT RNA embedding. The stage runs a fixed three-epoch recipe with a symmetric InfoNCE objective at temperature 0.07, produces `checkpoints/alignment/stage1_final.pt`, and hands its adapted encoder weights to Stage 2 expression training. This page explains the data construction, the objective, the gradient-caching optimization strategy, the exactly-once coverage guarantee, and the resume machinery that make the stage reproducible. It assumes familiarity with the corpus layout described in [Training Data Contracts](13-training-data-contracts) and with the two towers' backends: the [Image Encoder and LoRA Adapters](6-image-encoder-and-lora-adapters) and the [scGPT RNA Embedding Backend](9-scgpt-rna-embedding-backend).

Sources: [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L1), [recipe.py](morph2mol/recipe.py#L11-L19), [docs/training.md](docs/training.md#L58-L76)

## Position in the Training Pipeline

Stage 1 consumes two inputs produced by earlier steps. The first is the prepared corpus — `training_set/{xenium,cosmx}/...` directories with `expression.npz`, `patch_cell_boundaries.npz`, and `manifest.csv.gz` per sample, validated against split files. The second is the per-sample scGPT embedding file: `train/embed_scgpt.py` runs the frozen whole-human scGPT model over every cell in `expression.npz` row order and writes `<sample>.npy` — 512-dimensional, L2-normalized, float16 cell features. Stage 1 never sees raw expression; it aligns morphology to these targets. Its output checkpoint is later consumed by Stage 2 (via `--stage1`) and by release export, as covered in [Stage 2 Expression Training](15-stage-2-expression-training) and [Model Export and Release Packaging](17-model-export-and-release-packaging).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Prepared corpus<br/>(expression + boundaries + manifest)"] --> S1["Stage 1<br/>Contrastive Alignment"]
    B["train/embed_scgpt.py<br/><sample>.npy 512-d targets"] --> S1
    C["Local UNI2-h weights<br/>(--uni2h)"] --> S1
    S1 -->|"stage1_final.pt<br/>(LoRA + towers)"| D["Stage 2<br/>Expression Training"]
    S1 --> E["Release Export"]
```

Sources: [docs/training.md](docs/training.md#L36-L84), [embed_scgpt.py](train/embed_scgpt.py#L85-L90), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L214-L219)

## The Alignment Architecture

The stage trains three movable parts against a frozen backbone. The **image pathway** loads UNI2-h (ViT-H/14, 24 blocks, 1536-dim features, register tokens, SwiGLU MLP) strictly from a local state dict, freezes all parameters, then injects LoRA into the `qkv` and `proj` projections of the last 12 blocks with rank 16, alpha 32, and dropout 0.05. Features from the 256 patch tokens are reshaped into a 16×16 grid and pooled with the cell's mask weights (the "cmask pool") into a single 1536-dim vector, so the representation describes exactly the cell polygon rather than the whole crop. The **image tower** (`HeTower`) then maps this through LayerNorm → Linear(1536→512) → GELU → Linear(512→128) followed by L2 normalization. The **RNA tower** (`RNATower`) standardizes the 512-dim scGPT embedding with fixed running buffers (μ, σ) and applies the mirrored MLP Linear(512→512) → GELU → Linear(512→128) → L2 normalize. Both towers project into a shared 128-dim unit sphere where contrastive similarity is computed.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Frozen["Frozen backbone + trainable adapters"]
        IMG["Cell crop 224×224"] --> UNI["UNI2-h ViT-H/14<br/>(frozen, 24 blocks)"]
        UNI --> LORA["LoRA on qkv/proj<br/>last 12 blocks"]
    end
    LORA --> POOL["cmask pool<br/>16×16 mask-weighted → 1536-d"]
    POOL --> HE["HeTower<br/>LN → 512 → GELU → 128 → L2"]
    RNA["scGPT embedding 512-d"] --> STD["(x − μ)/σ buffers"]
    STD --> RT["RNATower<br/>512 → GELU → 128 → L2"]
    HE --> LOSS["Symmetric InfoNCE<br/>τ = 0.07"]
    RT --> LOSS
```

| Component | Parameterization | Trainable | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| UNI2-h backbone | ViT-H/14, 1536-d, 24 blocks | No | Visual feature extraction |
| LoRA adapters | 12 blocks, r=16, α=32, dropout 0.05 | Yes (lr 1.5e-4) | Task-adapt attention layers |
| HeTower | LN(1536) → 512 → GELU → 128 → L2 | Yes (lr 1e-3) | Image projection head |
| RNATower | (x−μ)/σ → 512 → GELU → 128 → L2 | Yes (lr 1e-3) | RNA projection head |

Sources: [encoder.py](morph2mol/encoder.py#L9-L40), [contrastive.py](morph2mol/training/contrastive.py#L14-L22), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L139-L144), [recipe.py](morph2mol/recipe.py#L11-L19)

## Building the Training Tensors

Before any GPU work, the stage assembles three logically concatenated arrays — crop paths, 16×16 mask weights, and RNA targets — one entry per usable cell. Validation precedes construction: `dataset_contract` reads the split files and enforces the invariants (in-slide test ⊆ training, training ∩ cross-slide = ∅, stage-2 set = training − in-slide test), then `training_slides` scans `training_set/{xenium,cosmx}` in sorted order, requires a matching `<sample>.npy` embedding file with 512 columns whose row count equals the `expression.npz` row count, and asserts the discovered sample set is exactly the approved `training_set` split via `check_members`. The contract — including a SHA-256 of `MANIFEST.csv` — is stored in every checkpoint written by the run.

Per-sample caching follows in `build_data`. For each slide, `load_slide_npz` reads `patch_cell_boundaries.rasterizes each cell polygon into a 16×16 float32 weight map by area-pooling the rasterized polygon over each 14-pixel token (any cell with fewer than 3 vertices or a vanishing mask falls back to its central token), while `manifest.csv.gz` supplies each expression row's crop path.
