Embedding rows are gathered by expression row index, cast to float16, and **cells whose target vector is all-zero are dropped** — a cell with an empty scGPT embedding cannot supervise contrastive learning. The three arrays are written under `work_dir/cache/stage1/<sample>` through `cached_arrays`, which takes an exclusive file lock, keys the cache on a signature of source-file stamps (resolved path, size, mtime) plus fixed seed/schema constants, publishes `metadata.json` last, and later memory-maps the completed arrays. `JoinedArrays` then presents all slides as one read-only logical concatenation so statistics and indexing span the corpus without materializing it.

Sources: [training_contract.py](morph2morph/training_contract.py#L14-L36), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L19-L63), [contrastive.py](morph2mol/training/contrastive.py#L50-L64), [training_cache.py](morph2mol/training_cache.py#L10-L73)

> [!TIP]
> The cache signature uses file *stamps* (path + size + mtime), not content hashes — regenerating an embedding `.npy` in place invalidates the cache correctly, but editing a file while preserving mtime would not. When in doubt, delete `work_dir/cache/stage1` rather than trusting a stale cache; `cached_arrays` deliberately refuses mismatched signatures instead of silently rebuilding.

## The Objective: Symmetric InfoNCE at τ = 0.07

The loss is the CLIP-style symmetric cross-entropy. Similarity logits are `zi @ zg.T / TEMP` with `TEMP = 0.07`, labels are the identity permutation, and the loss averages the image-to-RNA and RNA-to-image directions: `0.5 * (CE(logits, lab) + CE(logits.t(), lab))`. With an effective batch of 2,048 cells per rank, each cell discriminates itself against 2,047 in-batch negatives — this is why the stage aggregates to such a large batch before stepping.

Normalization of the RNA targets happens once, before training: `rna_stats` streams the concatenated float16 embedding array in 200,000-row chunks, accumulating sums and sums-of-squares in float64 to produce per-dimension μ and σ (with variance floored at zero and σ clamped by 1e-6). These become non-trainable buffers inside `RNATower`, so a resumed run reconstructs identical normalization from data alone. On the image side, `he_embed` chains normalization by ImageNet MEAN/STD, the LoRA-adapted encoder, mask-weighted pooling, and the `HeTower` — the single function invoked identically in training and (later, for bank construction) inference, which keeps the two feature spaces consistent.

Sources: [contrastive.py](morph2mol/training/contrastive.py#L11-L48), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L142-L144)

## Augmentation and Batching

Every `__getitem__` passes through two wrappers. `CLIPDS` loads the crop PNG, converts to RGB, resizes bilinearly to 224×224, and returns the CHW uint8 image, its float32 mask, and the float32 RNA target. `D4Wrap` then samples a uniform orientation from the eight-element dihedral group — one of four right-angle rotations, optionally combined with a horizontal flip — and applies the *same* transform to the crop and its mask, so mask pooling stays geometrically consistent with the image. Determinism is anchored by a fixed seed: `torch.manual_seed(1)` at startup and a dedicated `torch.Generator(manual_seed(1))` feeding the DataLoader, which is what later makes mid-epoch resume bit-reproducible.

The sampler is a custom `ResumeTailSampler` extending `DistributedSampler`. Because the global cell count rarely divides evenly by `world_size`, distributed sharding pads some ranks; the sampler emits `(index, valid)` pairs where `valid = slot*num_replicas + rank < len(dataset)`, and `TailDataset` appends that flag to each sample. Supervision — the loss mask, the seen-cell counters, and the epoch-end assertion — operates strictly on `valid` rows, so padding slots are never trained on and **every usable cell contributes exactly once per epoch**. At each epoch boundary the ranks all-reduce their per-rank `seen` counts and the run raises `ValueError` unless the sum equals `len(dataset)` exactly; a hard coverage check, not a heuristic.

Sources: [contrastive.py](morph2mol/training/contrastive.py#L24-L33), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L66-L82), [clip_coverage.py](morph2mol/clip_coverage.py#L6-L31), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L178-L211)

## Gradient-Cached Optimization at Effective Batch 2,048

The central engineering constraint: the InfoNCE matrix needs all 2,048 embeddings in memory to form logits, but backpropagating through 2,048 concurrent UNI2-h forward passes would not fit. `gradcache_step_ddp` solves this with the classic gradient-cache decomposition, executed once per accumulation window (the DataLoader yields `accumulation = 2048 // chunk` micro-batches, chunk defaulting to 256):

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Chunk forward passes<br/>no_grad + bf16 autocast"] --> B["Concatenate Zi, Zg;<br/>detach → leaf tensors with grad"]
    B --> C["Masked InfoNCE on leaves;<br/>scale by world·n/total"]
    C --> D["loss.backward →<br/>cached grads gi, gg"]
    D --> E["Re-run each chunk with grad;<br/>torch.autograd.backward(zi_c, zg_c, gi, gg)"]
    E --> F["One grad all-reduce after last chunk<br/>÷ world; clip 1.0; AdamW step"]
```

Three details deserve attention. First, DDP ranks can hold different numbers of *valid* cells (the tail problem), so a rank with few supervised cells would otherwise dominate the gradient; the loss is rescaled by `world * n / total` (with `total` all-reduced) so the step direction equals the gradient of the global masked mean regardless of rank imbalance. A rank with zero valid cells computes a zero-grad placeholder `(zi.sum()+zg.sum())*0` to stay gradient-flow-connected. Second, parameter-gradient synchronization is deliberately deferred: **one all-reduce after the final chunk** rather than per-chunk DDP hooks, cutting communication volume by the accumulation factor. Third, optimization uses AdamW with two parameter groups — LoRA adapters at lr 1.5e-4 and both towers at lr 1e-3, shared weight decay 0.01 — with linear warmup over the first 150 steps (`min(1, (step+1)/150)` applied to each group's stored `base_lr`), and global gradient-norm clipping at 1.0 before every step.

Sources: [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L85-L117), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L152-L161), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L193-L197)

> [!TIP]
> The recompute phase re-runs each chunk *with* autocast and casts outputs to `.float()` before `torch.autograd.backward`, so cached gradients computed against float32 leaf copies are injected into bf16-computed graphs through the float cast boundary. If you adapt this pattern, keep that explicit cast — backward through mismatched dtypes silently produces wrong scales otherwise.

## Fixed Recipe and Step Budget

Stage settings live in `recipe.py` and are **immutable at runtime**: `stage1_settings` raises `TypeError` if any caller attempts to override a recipe key, accepting only runtime arguments (paths, workers, chunk, checkpoint frequency, resume). The total optimizer step count is computed from data shape, not configured: `stage1_steps(cells, epochs=3, world, chunk, accumulation)` sets `per_epoch = ceil(cells / (world·chunk·accumulation))` and returns `3 × per_epoch`, guaranteeing the loop trains at least one full optimizer batch per epoch and terminates after exactly three epochs regardless of corpus size. The recipe key set is also mirrored into `STAGE1_RECIPE` for resume validation, so a checkpoint can never be continued under silently changed hyperparameters.

| Recipe key | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `epochs` | 3 | Fixed three-epoch schedule |
| `loss` / `target` | `infonce` / `scgpt` | Symmetric InfoNCE against scGPT embeddings |
| `eff_batch` | 2048 | Cells per optimizer step per rank |
| `lr_lora` / `lr_tower` | 1.5e-4 / 1e-3 | AdamW learning rates |
| `wd` / `warmup` | 0.01 / 150 | Weight decay, warmup steps |
| `nblocks`, `r`, `alpha`, `dropout` | 12, 16, 32, 0.05 | LoRA placement and shape |
| `d4_aug` / `retain_tail` / `no_validation` | True / True / True | Dihedral augmentation, tail retention, no val split |
| `seed` | 1 | Global RNG seed |

Sources: [recipe.py](morph2mol/recipe.py#L11-L19), [training_contract.py](morph2mol/training_contract.py#L52-L58), [training_resume.py](morph2morph/training_resume.py#L15-L18), [docs/training.md](docs/training.md#L66-L76)

## Checkpoints, Resume, and Reproducibility

Every `save_every` steps (default 500) and at the final step, rank 0 writes `checkpoints/alignment/stage1_step{N}.pt` — and at completion `stage1_final.pt` — through `atomic_torch_save`, which writes to a PID-suffixed temp file and `os.replace`s it into place. The payload is comprehensive: trainable LoRA tensors, both tower state dicts, optimizer state, the frozen recipe args, `init_hash`, current `step`, `world_size`, the dataset contract, a revision tag, the data identity, a serialized coverage cursor, per-rank RNG states, and the DataLoader generator state.

Reproducibility rests on three independent identity anchors, all re-verified on resume. The **initialization hash** is a SHA-256 over every trainable parameter and tower tensor at startup, so resume refuses to continue a run whose random init differs (a different seed or library version would change the optimization trajectory). The **data identity** combines the cell count, the ordered sample list, and a SHA-256 over per-sample cache metadata records, detecting any change in concatenation order or cache contents. The **coverage cursor** (`Stage1Cursor`, a frozen dataclass) derives the full schedule arithmetically from `(cells, world, chunk, accumulation, epochs, step)`: steps-per-epoch, current epoch, `skip_batches`, and `skip_slots = min(skip_batches·chunk, samples_per_rank)`. On resume, `sampler.set_start(skip_slots)` truncates the epoch permutation from the front — `islice` skips already-consumed slots in C *without calling `__getitem__`*, so no already-trained image is ever decoded again — while `supervised_in_epoch` seeds the seen-counter with cells already covered, keeping the exactly-once epoch assertion honest across restarts. Resume additionally enforces the original DDP world size, the complete `STAGE1_RECIPE` key match, cursor self-consistency against the recomputed schedule, and identical total step budget; weights are restored with strict LoRA key-set and shape checks.

| Checkpoint field | Verified on resume |
| --- | --- |
| `lora`, `he_tower`, `scf_tower`, `opt` | Restored; LoRA keys/shape-checked, towers strict-loaded |
| `init_hash` | Must equal recomputed init digest |
| `data_identity` | Must equal recomputed cells/order/cache hash |
| `run_contract` | Must equal current `dataset_contract` |
| `args` (recipe keys) | All `STAGE1_RECIPE` keys must match |
| `world_size`, step budget, `coverage_cursor` | Original world size; cursor consistent with recomputed schedule |
| `rng_per_rank`, `loader_generator_state` | Restored per rank; generator state reloaded |

Sources: [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L145-L176), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L200-L219), [training_resume.py](morph2mol/training_resume.py#L25-L135), [training_resume.py](morph2mol/training_resume.py#L156-L187), [clip_coverage.py](morph2mol/clip_coverage.py#L18-L23)

## Running Stage 1

The entry point `train/train_phase1.py` parses shared arguments via `train._entry.arguments(1)` and dispatches to `morph2mol.training.stage1.main`. Multi-GPU runs use `torchrun`; the process group is NCCL with a four-hour timeout, per-rank CUDA devices, and the global seed applied on every rank. The CLI enforces `--chunk` to be a positive divisor of the fixed 2,048 effective batch and validates worker/checkpoint-frequency ranges.

```bash
torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=3 train/train_phase1.py \
  --dataset /data/corpus --work-dir /runs/morph2mol \
  --uni2h /models/uni2h --cell-embeddings /runs/scgpt_cells
```

| Argument | Default | Constraint / purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dataset` | required | Prepared corpus root with `splits/` and `MANIFEST.csv` |
| `--work-dir` | required | Receives `checkpoints/alignment/` and `cache/stage1/` |
| `--uni2h` | required | Directory containing UNI2-h `pytorch_model.bin` |
| `--cell-embeddings` | required | Directory of row-aligned `<sample>.npy` scGPT embeddings |
| `--chunk` | 256 | Encoder micro-batch; must divide 2,048 |
| `--workers` | 8 | DataLoader workers (≥ 0) |
| `--save-every` | 500 | Checkpoint interval in steps (≥ 1) |
| `--resume` | `''` | Path to a Stage-1 checkpoint to continue |

Sources: [train_phase1.py](train/train_phase1.py#L9-L12), [_entry.py](train/_entry.py#L6-L27), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L120-L133), [docs/training.md](docs/training.md#L60-L76)

## What Stage 1 Does *Not* Do

Precision about scope avoids misconfiguration. Stage 1 performs no expression prediction — the negative-binomial head, spatial decoder, and neighborhood sampling all belong to Stage 2, where D4 augmentation is also disabled and learning rates drop by an order of magnitude. It runs no validation split (the contract reserves `inslide_test_set` and `cross_slide_test_set` for evaluation, and the recipe fixes `no_validation=True`), builds no retrieval bank, and never touches the gate/fusion machinery. Its single deliverable is the alignment checkpoint; everything downstream — reference bank encoding, gated fusion weights, release packaging — consumes its LoRA and tower weights through later stages.

Sources: [recipe.py](morph2mol/recipe.py#L22-L33), [training_contract.py](morph2mol/training_contract.py#L14-L28), [docs/training.md](docs/training.md#L78-L97)

## Where to Go Next

With the alignment checkpoint in hand, continue through the training pipeline in order: [Stage 2 Expression Training](15-stage-2-expression-training) explains how the aligned encoder and `stage1_final.pt` seed the spatial expression model; [Resume, Caching, and Reproducibility](16-resume-caching-and-reproducibility) generalizes the cursor/RNG mechanics introduced here; and [Model Export and Release Packaging](17-model-export-and-release-packaging) shows how Stage-1 weights travel into a distributed release. For the inference-side consumption of the same `he_embed` pathway, see [Reference Bank Construction](10-reference-bank-construction).


# Stage 2 Expression Training



Stage 2 is where Morph2Mol learns to *predict expression from morphology*. It takes the contrastively aligned image encoder from Stage 1, attaches a spatial decoder and a negative-binomial expression head, and fits them against per-cell RNA counts under a fixed three-epoch recipe that guarantees every usable target cell contributes to the loss exactly once per epoch. This page dissects the stage's entry contract, its immutable recipe, the per-slide data store, the trainable parameter surface, the full-coverage spatial sampler, the composite loss, and the checkpoint/resume integrity machinery that binds it all together.

## Pipeline Position and Entry Contract

The stage is launched through a deliberately thin wrapper: `train/train_phase2.py` resolves the shared CLI arguments via `arguments(2)` and immediately delegates to `morph2mol.training.stage2.main`, so all orchestration logic lives in the training package rather than the entry script. The CLI requires `--dataset`, `--work-dir`, `--uni2h`, and — unique to stage 2 — `--stage1`, the path to the completed Stage-1 checkpoint, with `--workers` (default 8), `--save-every` (default 5000, ten times Stage 1's cadence), and `--resume` as the only runtime knobs.
Sources: [train_phase2.py](train/train_phase2.py#L1-L17), [_entry.py](train/_entry.py#L5-L28), [docs/training.md](docs/training.md#L96-L103)

Before any tensor is touched, the run is bound to a **dataset contract**. `dataset_contract` reads the four split files and enforces the set algebra `stage2_global_training == training_set \ inslide_test_set`, disjointness from the cross-slide test set, and that both `retrieval_references` and `gate_fit_references` equal the Stage-2 set exactly — plus a SHA-256 of `MANIFEST.csv` recorded into the contract for later checkpoint binding. When slides are actually loaded, `check_members` rejects the run unless the materialized sample list matches the approved `stage2_global_training` set with no missing or extra members.
Sources: [training_contract.py](morph2mol/training_contract.py#L16-L41), [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L113-L137)

The stage writes exactly one artifact family: `checkpoints/expression/stage2_last.pt` inside the work directory, atomically replaced on every save. That single rolling checkpoint is simultaneously the resume cursor and, after the final step, the input to release export.
Sources: [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L111-L224), [docs/training.md](docs/training.md#L114-L115)

## The Fixed Stage-2 Recipe

Every hyperparameter of the stage is frozen in `stage2_settings`, and the constructor enforces immutability structurally: supplying any key that collides with a recipe field raises `TypeError`, so callers may only pass runtime arguments (`tag`, `lora_ckpt`, `workers`, `save_every`, `resume`). This recipe is re-validated twice downstream — `check_stage2_settings` compares exported checkpoints against it field-by-field, and `STAGE2_RECIPE` (a 25-key subset covering model geometry, optimizer rates, sampling, and loss weights) is diffed against any resume checkpoint to reject recipe drift.
Sources: [recipe.py](morph2mol/recipe.py#L26-L40), [training_resume.py](morph2mol/training_resume.py#L12-L17)

| Setting | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `epochs` | 3 | Fixed training duration, shared with Stage 1 |
| `sampling` | `full_coverage` | Every target cell owns exactly one block per epoch |
| `target_cells` / `context_cells` | 128 / 64 | Supervised block size; bounded attention halo |
| `max_dist` | 137.0 µm | Spatial attention radius and halo selection radius |
| `d_model` / `n_layers` | 256 / 6 | SE(2) decoder width and layer count |
| `nblocks` / `lora_r` / `lora_alpha` / `lora_dropout` | 12 / 16 / 32 / 0.05 | LoRA on the last 12 encoder blocks, matching Stage 1 |
| `freeze_frac` | 0.2 | Recorded frozen-adapter fraction (see freezing below) |
| `lr_lora` / `lr_se2` | 3e-5 / 1e-4 | Two AdamW parameter groups |
| `grad_ckpt` | `True` | Encoder gradient checkpointing enabled |
| `d4` | 0 | Augmentation disabled during expression training |
| `lam_aux` / `lam_mse` | 1.0 / 1.0 | Equal weight on NB likelihood and log1p MSE |
| `gene_emb` / `free_head` | `scgpt` / `True` | Head rows initialized from scGPT gene embeddings |
| `seed` | 1 | Governs partitions, block shuffles, and RNG capture |

Sources: [recipe.py](morph2mol/recipe.py#L4-L40), [training_resume.py](morph2mol/training_resume.py#L12-L17), [docs/training.md](docs/training.md#L104-L113)

## Per-Slide Data Store: LiveStore

`LiveStore` materializes, for each slide, the four arrays the training loop needs — crop paths, 16×16 token masks, micron positions, and expression targets — in a single pass. Polygon masks come from a precomputed `cmask.npz` under the work directory's `features/` tree when available (renormalized so weights sum to one), falling back to `cells_of` reconstruction otherwise; positions stored in pixels are converted to microns using the slide's `um_per_pixel_source`, which is what makes the 137 µm attention radius physically meaningful across platforms. Both masks and targets are wrapped in an optional content-addressed cache whose signatures stamp the source files (`patch_cell_boundaries.npz`, `expression.npz`, `genes.tsv`), so a changed corpus invalidates stale arrays automatically.
Sources: [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L29-L70)

Gene mapping is the subtle part: each slide's `genes.tsv` symbols are matched — first occurrence only — against the model gene space stored in `direct/gene_space_all.npz` (the sorted union of training-split genes), yielding `head_idx`, the permutation from slide columns to head rows. Targets `y` are then gathered as `X[expr_rows][:, matched_cols]` and held in float16, and the loss later slices per-gene dispersion by the same `head_idx`, so predictions and likelihoods always operate on measured genes in a globally consistent order.
Sources: [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L52-L66), [head.py](morph2mol/head.py#L40-L42)

Cell geometry enters the model as **area covariates** rather than raw shapes: `cell_areas` computes each cell's shoelace polygon area in µm² (degenerate polygons fall back to the slide median instead of zero), and the store derives `area_abs = log(area+1)` and `area_rel = area_abs − log(median+1)`. The relative term is what the head uses as a multiplicative exposure correction, decoupling per-cell size from tissue-wide scale. Crop decoding in `load` is strictly deterministic — RGB, bilinear resize to 224×224, no augmentation — consistent with the recipe's `d4=0`.
Sources: [head.py](morph2mol/head.py#L9-L20), [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L67-L77)

## Model Assembly and the Trainable Surface

`ExpressionModel` is a four-stage pipeline: a LoRA-adapted UNI2-h encoder, a 1536→256 linear projection, a six-layer SE(2) spatial transformer, and the negative-binomial `DirectHead`. Only the encoder pass runs under bf16 autocast (`C.AMP_DTYPE`); features are cast back to float32 before the projection, keeping the spatial decoder and head in full precision. The SE(2) decoder is architecture-fixed: three pre- and three post-attention `SE2Layer(256, 64, 8)` blocks over a Gaussian distance basis scaled to 137 µm, with pairwise cell distances in microns as the only geometric signal.
Sources: [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L80-L91), [contrastive.py](morph2mol/training/contrastive.py#L9), [se2.py](morph2mol/se2.py#L7-L22)

Before reading the diagram, note the prerequisite: LoRA adapters `A`/`B` are low-rank side-branches injected into the last 12 transformer blocks' `qkv` and `proj` modules; Stage 2 re-injects them with identical geometry and loads Stage 1's weights into them.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    IMG["224×224 RGB crops + 16×16 mask W<br/>(targets + context halo)"] --> ENC
    subgraph ENC["UNI2-h ViT + LoRA (last 12 blocks)"]
        FROZEN["blocks 0-2 of adapted tail: A/B frozen"]
        TRAIN["blocks 3-11: A/B trainable @ lr 3e-5"]
    end
    ENC -->|"pooled_feat, bf16 autocast,<br/>mask-weighted token pooling"| POOL["1536-d pooled feature → float32"]
    POOL --> INP["Linear 1536 → 256<br/>lr 1e-4"]
    INP --> SE2["SpatialTransformer: 6 SE(2) layers,<br/>Gaussian basis @ 137 µm, lr 1e-4"]
    SE2 --> HEAD["DirectHead MLP 258 → 1024 → 1536, lr 1e-4"]
    AREA["area_abs, area_rel covariates"] --> HEAD
    GEMB["scGPT gene embeddings: frozen buffer E,<br/>learnable copy W"] --> HEAD
    HEAD --> MU["µ = (softplus(zWᵀ+b)+1e-4) · e^(e^γ·area_rel)"]
```

Sources: [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L80-L104), [head.py](morph2mol/head.py#L23-L38), [se2.py](morph2mol/se2.py#L7-L22)

The trainable surface is shaped in three moves. First, only parameters ending in `.A`/`.B` — the LoRA tensors — are marked trainable on the encoder; everything else stays frozen. Second, `freeze_first_lora` freezes the first three of the last twelve adapted blocks (the `freeze_frac` recipe slot), so low-level morphology features from Stage 1 are preserved while higher blocks adapt to the expression objective. Third, the optimizer receives two AdamW groups: LoRA at 3e-5 and everything else (`inp`, `se2`, `head`, including the learnable gene matrix `W`, bias `b`, area exponent `log_gamma`, and per-gene dispersion `log_theta`) at 1e-4, both with zero weight decay. The stage also refuses a malformed starting point: the Stage-1 checkpoint must target `scgpt`, span exactly 3 epochs, and be fully stepped, and `load_lora_checked(complete=True)` demands the entire LoRA key set with shape-verified tensors.
Sources: [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L142-L157), [training_contract.py](morph2mol/training_contract.py#L72-L78), [docs/training.md](docs/training.md#L111-L112)

| Component | Initialization | Trainable | LR group |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Encoder body + towers | Pretrained UNI2-h | Frozen | — |
| LoRA A/B, adapted blocks 0–2 | Stage-1 checkpoint | Frozen | — |
| LoRA A/B, adapted blocks 3–11 | Stage-1 checkpoint | Yes | 3e-5 |
| `inp` projection | Random linear | Yes | 1e-4 |
| `se2` decoder | Random | Yes | 1e-4 |
| `head.W` gene rows | scGPT embeddings (via `E` buffer) | Yes | 1e-4 |
| `head.b`, `log_gamma`, `log_theta` | Zeros | Yes | 1e-4 |

Sources: [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L150-L169), [head.py](morph2mol/head.py#L23-L38)

## Full-Coverage Spatial Sampling

Stage 2's central guarantee — *every usable target cell contributes loss exactly once per epoch* — is implemented by `CoveragePlan` and `FullCoverageDataset` rather than by a sampler over shuffled cells. For each epoch, `partition_cells` derives a deterministic RNG from `(seed, crc32(slide_id), epoch)`, rotates the slide's cell positions by up to ±45°, jitters the grid origin, and bins cells into a grid whose side length is derived from the slide's span and the 128-target budget; any oversized grid cell is recursively median-split along its longest axis into blocks of at most 128 targets. An ownership assertion then verifies that every cell appears in exactly one block, and blocks are shuffled for step order with a separate per-epoch RNG. Across the three epochs the rotation angle, origin jitter, and shuffle all change, so no cell is repeatedly stuck in the same neighborhood configuration.
Sources: [full_coverage.py](morph2mol/full_coverage.py#L14-L44), [full_coverage.py](morph2mol/full_coverage.py#L61-L91), [docs/training.md](docs/training.md#L114-L115)

The following flowchart shows one epoch's construction; the KD-tree prerequisite is that each slide's micron positions are indexed once and reused for halo queries across all its blocks.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Seed = seed + crc32(slide) + epoch·1000003"] --> B["Rotate positions ±45°,<br/>jitter grid origin"]
    B --> C["Grid binning:<br/>side ≈ √(span·128·2/N)"]
    C --> D["Recursive median-split →<br/>blocks of ≤128 targets"]
    D --> E{"Every cell owned<br/>exactly once?"}
    E -->|no| F["ValueError:<br/>partition invalid"]
    E -->|yes| G["Shuffle block order<br/>(seed + epoch·7919)"]
    G --> H["Per block: cKD-tree halo,<br/>≤64 non-target cells within 137 µm"]
    H --> I["Item = targets ⊕ context,<br/>loss mask on first len(targets) slots"]
```

Sources: [full_coverage.py](morph2mol/full_coverage.py#L14-L58), [full_coverage.py](morph2mol/full_coverage.py#L118-L134)

`CoveragePlan.locate` maps a global step number to `(epoch, slide, targets)` via binary search over epoch boundaries and a rank-strided slot decode, which is how the training loop can resume at an arbitrary step and reconstruct the exact data position. Steps per rank are `ceil(blocks_per_epoch / world)`, and the plan additionally exposes `supervised_before(step, rank)` — an exact recomputation of how many targets a rank has already consumed — which becomes the ground truth against which resume checkpoints are audited. Everything the partition depends on is fingerprinted under `REVISION = 'full_coverage_halo_v1'` and cached per slide-epoch, so a partition scheme change invalidates old caches rather than silently changing training data.
Sources: [full_coverage.py](morph2mol/full_coverage.py#L93-L115), [full_coverage.py](morph2mol/full_coverage.py#L8), [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L138-L141)

## Loss and Distributed Optimization

Each training item is one spatial block: up to 128 targets plus up to 64 context cells, batch size 1 at the DataLoader level with a pass-through collate. The forward pass predicts `µ` for all cells in the block, but `supervised_sums` masks to owned targets only — context cells participate in SE(2) attention yet never touch the loss, satisfying the docstring contract "Context labels do not enter either loss". The composite objective sums two masked means with equal weight: the per-gene negative-binomial likelihood `nb_nll(y, µ, log_theta[hi])` with dispersion clamped to [1e-4, 1e4], and a log1p-domain MSE that stabilizes optimization on heavy-tailed counts.
Sources: [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L174-L197), [full_coverage.py](morph2mol/full_coverage.py#L136-L145), [head.py](morph2mol/head.py#L40-L42)

The DDP loss normalization is worth reading closely. Each block's `(nll + mse)` is a *mean over its own targets*, so blocks with different target counts would otherwise contribute unequally per optimizer step. The loop counteracts this by all-reducing the block's target count across ranks and scaling the loss by `world / total.clamp_min(1)`, making the per-target gradient contribution uniform across the entire distributed batch regardless of partition geometry. Gradients are then globally clipped to norm 1.0 over trainable parameters only, and DDP is constructed with `gradient_as_bucket_view=True` and `broadcast_buffers=False` — the latter avoiding needless buffer synchronization since the head's `E` buffer is constant.
Sources: [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L190-L201), [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L167-L173)

> [!TIP]
> The `world / total.clamp_min(1)` scaling is what turns "every cell counts once" from a sampling promise into a gradient-level invariant: without it, a rank holding several 40-cell tail blocks would down-weight those targets relative to ranks holding full 128-cell blocks, and the epoch coverage audit below would still pass while gradients were subtly biased.

Coverage is not just promised — it is *audited at runtime*. `supervised` accumulates per-rank target counts during the loop, and whenever `step` lands on an epoch boundary (`coverage.step_ends`), the all-reduced count must equal `epoch × coverage.cells` exactly or training aborts with `Target-cell coverage differs from the epoch budget`. This converts any silent partition, sharding, or skip-logic bug into an immediate, loud failure instead of a subtly undertrained model.
Sources: [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L202-L210)

> [!TIP]
> When debugging a crash at an epoch boundary, the mismatch size in `seen.item()` vs `epoch * coverage.cells` localizes the fault: a deficit that is a multiple of `world` points to rank-sharding drift, while a deficit matching one slide's cell count points to a stale or invalidated coverage cache for that slide.

## Checkpointing, Resume, and Integrity

Every `save_every` steps (default 5000) and at the final step, rank 0 writes `stage2_last.pt` via `atomic_torch_save`, which saves to a PID-suffixed temporary file and `os.replace`s it into place — a concurrent reader never observes a torn checkpoint. The payload is deliberately complete: trainable LoRA tensors (keyed by parameter name), the three non-encoder modules, optimizer state, the full frozen `args` namespace, the step cursor, world size, the dataset contract, the gene-order hash, the Stage-1 checkpoint's SHA-256 identity, the coverage revision, per-rank supervised counts, and per-rank RNG states for Python, NumPy, CPU-torch, and CUDA.
Sources: [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L211-L224), [training_resume.py](morph2mol/training_resume.py#L137-L144)

Resume (`--resume stage2_last.pt`) runs a gauntlet of checks before a single weight is restored, all aimed at the same goal: guaranteeing that a resumed run is bit-for-bit the continuation of the original:

| Check | Failure condition |
| --- | --- |
| `check_stage2_resume` completeness | Missing `rng_per_rank`, `coverage_revision`, or `supervised_cells_per_rank` |
| Contract + gene-order binding | Different corpus splits or `gene_head_sha256` mismatch |
| Stage-1 lineage | `stage1_identity.sha256` differs from the currently supplied `--stage1` file |
| World size | Resume under a different DDP world size |
| Recipe drift | Any of the 25 `STAGE2_RECIPE` keys differs from the live `stage2_settings` |
| Epoch budget | Checkpoint `step` outside `[0, total_steps]` |
| Coverage audit | `coverage_revision` changed or per-rank counts ≠ recomputed `supervised_before(step, r)` |
| Trainable-set equality | Resume LoRA keys ≠ current `requires_grad` parameter names (freezing changed) |

Sources: [training_resume.py](morph2mol/training_resume.py#L96-L110), [training_resume.py](morph2mol/training_resume.py#L12-L17), [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L158-L166)

After the checks pass, restoration order matters for reproducibility: LoRA weights and `inp`/`se2`/`head` state dicts load strictly, the optimizer state restores AdamW moments and step counters, the dataset starts at `start=step`, and only then does `restore_main_rng` rewind every rank's RNG streams from the checkpoint — ensuring that halo queries, any downstream sampling, and future checkpoint RNG captures continue on the original trajectory. If the loaded step already equals `total_steps`, the stage exits cleanly with "Three training epochs are already complete", making reruns idempotent.
Sources: [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L158-L186), [training_resume.py](morph2mol/training_resume.py#L112-L135)

## Running Stage 2

The canonical invocation matches the released Morph2Mol-25M recipe on three GPUs; a single-GPU run needs only `python train/train_phase2.py` with the same flags and no `torchrun`:

```bash
torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=3 train/train_phase2.py \
  --dataset /data/corpus --work-dir /runs/morph2mol --uni2h /models/uni2h \
  --stage1 /runs/morph2mol/checkpoints/alignment/stage1_final.pt
```

Sources: [docs/training.md](docs/training.md#L96-L103), [_entry.py](train/_entry.py#L5-L28)

Runtime behavior is observable through three log families emitted by rank 0: `[data]` reports each slide's cell count and measured-gene count as stores build; `[coverage]` prints the per-epoch target budget and total steps per rank, then audits each epoch boundary; and `[train]` emits loss and elapsed seconds every 200 steps. Progress beyond step 4000 with default settings indicates the rolling checkpoint at `checkpoints/expression/stage2_last.pt` is being refreshed roughly every epoch for a typical corpus.
Sources: [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L136-L141), [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L202-L210), [_entry.py](train/_entry.py#L14-L17)

## Next Steps

Stage 2's output feeds directly into release packaging, and its recovery machinery deserves its own deep dive. Continue with [Resume, Caching, and Reproducibility](16-resume-caching-and-reproducibility) for the shared cursor/RNG/cache architecture across both stages, or jump to [Model Export and Release Packaging](17-model-export-and-release-packaging) to see how `stage2_last.pt` is distilled into the deployable release alongside `gene_space_all.npz` and the scGPT gene table. For the upstream alignment objective that produced the `--stage1` input, see [Stage 1 Contrastive Alignment](14-stage-1-contrastive-alignment), and for the split algebra consumed by `dataset_contract`, see [Training Data Contracts](13-training-data-contracts).

# Resume, Caching, and Reproducibility



Morph2Mol's training pipeline is built for long-running jobs on shared GPU allocations, where preemption, hardware failure, and multi-process contention are normal events rather than exceptions. The system therefore treats **determinism as a first-class architectural constraint**: every checkpoint carries enough identity, cursor, and RNG state to reconstruct the exact training position, while every expensive derived artifact (scGPT embeddings, cell crops, coverage partitions, dense expression targets) is persisted behind content-derived signatures that make stale reuse impossible. This page explains the three cooperating mechanisms — checkpoint/resume, signature-gated disk caches, and identity hashing — as one integrated design.

Sources: [training.md](docs/training.md#L9-L11), [training_resume.py](morph2mol/training_resume.py#L1-L18)

## Design Principles: Four Pillars of Deterministic Training

The architecture rests on four pillars that interact at every checkpoint boundary. The **frozen recipe** (`recipe.py`) hard-codes all hyperparameters with `SEED = 1` and rejects any runtime attempt to override them — only paths, workers, chunk size, save frequency, and resume targets may vary. The **cursor** encodes position within the fixed epoch budget. The **cache signatures** bind disk artifacts to their inputs via file stamps and array hashes. The **identity hashes** (manifest, gene list, data identity, stage-1 checkpoint bytes, initialization tensors) let a resumed process prove that its corpus, gene order, and weight initialization are bit-identical to the original run.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Recipe["Pillar 1: Frozen Recipe"]
        R1["stage1_settings()<br/>SEED=1, EPOCHS=3"]
        R2["stage2_settings()<br/>128 targets, 64 context"]
    end
    subgraph Cursor["Pillar 2: Position Cursor"]
        C1["Stage1Cursor<br/>step → epoch/skip slots"]
        C2["coverage.supervised_before()<br/>per-rank counts"]
    end
    subgraph Cache["Pillar 3: Signature Caches"]
        K1["cached_arrays()<br/>flock + metadata-last"]
        K2["file_stamp / array_stamp"]
    end
    subgraph Identity["Pillar 4: Identity Hashes"]
        I1["manifest_sha256<br/>gene_hash"]
        I2["init_hash<br/>stage1_identity"]
        I3["data_identity<br/>coverage_revision"]
    end
    Recipe -->|"check_recipe()"| Check{"Resume Gate"}
    Cursor -->|"consistency check"| Check
    Cache -->|"cache_sha256"| Check
    Identity -->|"equality checks"| Check
    Check -->|all pass| Restore["Restore weights,<br/>optimizer, RNG, position"]
    Check -->|any fail| Reject["ValueError:<br/>refuse to resume"]
```

Any mismatch at the gate aborts the resume with a descriptive `ValueError` — the code never silently adapts to a changed environment. This "verify-then-restore" pattern is applied identically in both training stages, differing only in which checks apply.

Sources: [recipe.py](morph2mol/recipe.py#L4-L19), [recipe.py](morph2mol/recipe.py#L22-L39), [training_resume.py](morph2mol/training_resume.py#L99-L128)

## Checkpoint Anatomy and Atomic Publication

Checkpoints are complete snapshots: resuming never requires re-deriving anything from logs or file listings. Stage 1 saves LoRA adapters, both projection towers, the optimizer state, full `args`, the run contract, the data identity, a coverage cursor record, per-rank RNG states, and the DataLoader generator state. Stage 2 additionally saves the decoder input projection, SE(2) transformer, expression head, gene-list hash, stage-1 checkpoint hash, the coverage plan revision, and gathered per-rank supervised-cell counts.

| Payload key | Stage 1 | Stage 2 | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lora` | ✓ | ✓ (trainable only) | Image adapter weights |
| `he_tower` / `scf_tower` | ✓ | — | Contrastive projection heads |
| `inp` / `se2` / `head` | — | ✓ | Decoder + expression head |
| `opt` | ✓ | ✓ (required) | Exact optimizer momenta |
| `run_contract` | ✓ | ✓ | Split sets + `manifest_sha256` |
| `data_identity` | ✓ | — | Slide order + cache SHA |
| `stage1_identity` | — | ✓ | SHA-256 of the stage-1 `.pt` file |
| `coverage_cursor` / `coverage_revision` + `supervised_cells_per_rank` | ✓ cursor record | ✓ revision + counts | Position + plan consistency |
| `rng_per_rank` | ✓ | ✓ | Per-rank RNG states |
| `loader_generator_state` | ✓ | — | Sampler permutation state |
| `init_hash` | ✓ | — | Initialization fingerprint |

All writes go through `atomic_torch_save`, which serializes to a PID-suffixed temporary file and publishes via `os.replace` — readers can never observe a half-written checkpoint even after a crash mid-save. Stage 2 writes a single rolling `stage2_last.pt` (guarded by a distributed barrier so rank 0 never snapshots while peers are mid-step), whereas Stage 1 keeps a timestamped series `stage1_step{N}.pt` plus a terminal `stage1_final.pt`.

Sources: [training_resume.py](morph2mol/training_resume.py#L179-L188), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L171-L176), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L200-L219), [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L211-L226)

> [!TIP]
> The stage-2 save collects `supervised` counts from every rank via `dist.all_gather_object` *before* rank 0 writes, then barriers afterward — this ordering guarantees the saved `supervised_cells_per_rank` vector is mutually consistent with the saved `step`, which is exactly what `check_stage2_resume` later recomputes and compares.

## Stage-1 Resume: The Cursor Model

Stage 1 uses a compact cursor algebra. `Stage1Cursor` is a frozen dataclass holding `(cells, world, chunk, accumulation, epochs, step)` and *derives* everything else: epoch boundaries, batches to skip, sampler slots to skip, and the cumulative supervised-cell count per rank. Because the recipe fixes three epochs and the effective batch of 2,048 cells per rank, the entire trajectory is a pure function of these six integers — position recovery requires no history.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["torch.load(resume)"] --> B["check_stage1_resume()"]
    B --> B1["policy: retain_tail +<br/>no_validation + fixed epochs"]
    B --> B2["structural keys present<br/>(data_identity, cursors, RNG)"]
    B --> B3["check_checkpoint: run_contract<br/>== current dataset_contract"]
    B --> B4["check_recipe: 15 recipe keys<br/>bit-identical"]
    B --> B5["world_size == current world"]
    B --> B6["init_hash matches<br/>current model init"]
    B --> B7["data_identity + total_steps<br/>match recomputation"]
    B1 & B2 & B3 & B4 & B5 & B6 & B7 --> C["cursor = Stage1Cursor(...)"]
    C --> D["restore_stage1_weights()<br/>LoRA checked, towers strict,<br/>optimizer state"]
    D --> E["generator.set_state(<br/>loader_generator_state)"]
    E --> F["Epoch loop: sampler.set_start(cursor.skip_slots)<br/>mask padding via TailDataset"]
    F --> G["restore_main_rng() before<br/>first post-resume step"]
```

The elegant part is skip semantics in the sampler. `ResumeTailSampler` reproduces the identical seed+epoch permutation of `DistributedSampler` and uses `islice` to discard already-processed slots **in C, before any `Dataset.__getitem__` call** — so a resume near the end of an epoch does not decode thousands of JPEG crops just to throw them away. Because DDP pads uneven ranks, each yielded item carries a `valid` flag that masks sampler padding out of the supervision count, and the loader-generator state plus per-rank RNG restore make the post-resume stream byte-identical to the original run.

Sources: [training_resume.py](morph2mol/training_resume.py#L25-L82), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L164-L187), [clip_coverage.py](morph2mol/clip_coverage.py#L6-L31)

## Stage-2 Resume: Coverage-Plan Recomputation

Stage 2 cannot use a lightweight cursor because its per-step supervision load varies with the spatial block sizes. Instead, resume validation *replays the entire coverage plan*: the constructor builds `CoveragePlan` for all epochs deterministically (each object seeded by `zlib.crc32(obj)`, each epoch offset by `epoch * 1000003`, shuffle by `seed + epoch * 7919`), then `check_stage2_resume` recomputes `coverage.supervised_before(step, rank)` for every rank and demands equality with the checkpoint's `supervised_cells_per_rank`. It also pins the plan revision string (`full_coverage_halo_v1`) so a future change to partitioning or halo logic invalidates old checkpoints rather than silently misaligning them.

Two additional gates protect the stage boundary. The stage-1 checkpoint must be a *completed* run (`step == args.steps`, scGPT target, three epochs), and its raw file bytes are hashed by `checkpoint_identity` into `stage1_identity` — so even a functionally identical but byte-different re-export of stage 1 is rejected. On the resume path itself, the trainable-parameter set must match exactly, decoder components load with `strict=True`, the optimizer restores, and `FullCoverageDataset` is constructed with `start=step` so iteration resumes at the exact global step. A checkpoint that has already reached `total_steps` triggers a clean early exit instead of a wasted relaunch.

Sources: [training_resume.py](morph2mol/training_resume.py#L138-L153), [full_coverage.py](morph2mol/full_coverage.py#L55-L105), [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L144-L185), [training_contract.py](morph2mol/training_contract.py#L43-L49)

## The Cache Layer: Signature-Gated Disk Arrays

The cache system answers one question: *can these arrays be trusted without reading them?* `cached_arrays(directory, signature, build)` implements a write-once, read-many protocol. All participants serialize on an exclusive `fcntl` lock; the first writer builds arrays into `.tmp.npy` files, `os.replace`s each into place, and publishes `metadata.json` **last** — making metadata publication the atomic commit point. Any later reader either finds valid metadata (and mmaps the arrays read-only with `mmap_mode='c'` to prevent accidental mutation) or finds none and rebuilds. Crucially, if metadata exists but its signature differs from the current inputs, the call **raises** — a stale cache is an error, not a silent fallback.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["cached_arrays(dir, signature, build)"] --> B["acquire exclusive flock<br/>(root/write.lock)"]
    B --> C{"metadata.json exists?"}
    C -->|No| D["build(root) writes<br/>name.tmp.npy files"]
    C -->|Yes| E{"meta.signature ==<br/>signature?"}
    E -->|No| F["raise ValueError:<br/>'Stale training cache'"]
    E -->|Yes| G["np.load(..., mmap_mode='c')<br/>all listed arrays"]
    D --> H["os.replace each tmp → .npy<br/>then metadata.tmp.json → metadata.json"]
    H --> G
```

Signatures come from two stamp functions with different cost/precision trade-offs. `file_stamp` is O(1) — resolved path, size, and `st_mtime_ns` — suitable for large immutable inputs like NPZ archives and model weights. `array_stamp` hashes the full contiguous bytes of a small array, suitable for index vectors like expression-row selections where a same-sized same-mtime rewrite must still invalidate. The pipeline uses both together: stage-1 crop caching stamps the embedding file, cell boundaries, and manifest; stage-2 `LiveStore` stamps boundaries and mask files plus an `array_stamp` of the row selection, and `sparse_targets` materializes the dense float16 expression matrix chunk-wise into a memmap whose signature additionally includes stamps of the row and column indices.

| Cache site | Contents | Signature inputs | Cost avoided on re-run |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cache/stage1/{obj}` | Cell paths, masks, float16 scGPT targets | `file_stamp` × 3 (embeddings, boundaries, manifest) | Crop decode + embedding gather |
| `cache/stage2/{obj}/masks` | Normalized boundary masks | `file_stamp` × 2 + `array_stamp(rows)` | NPZ mask re-normalization |
| `cache/stage2/{obj}/targets` | Dense float16 expression matrix `Y` | file stamps + `array_stamp` rows/cols | Sparse-to-dense projection |
| `cache/coverage/{obj}/epoch{N}` | Partition `order` + `ptr` arrays | revision, `array_stamp(pos)`, object seed, epoch, target budget | KD-grid partition per epoch |
| `scgpt_cells/{obj}.npy` | 512-d cell embeddings (pre-training) | existence check only | Full scGPT forward pass |

Note the two cache generations have different rigor: `embed_scgpt.py` uses simple skip-if-exists with atomic `os.replace` publication, seeded deterministically per object via `zlib.crc32(name)` (explicitly because Python's `str` hash is salted per process), while the in-training caches add full signature validation. This division is deliberate — embedding generation is idempotent and content-addressed by output row alignment, which stage 1 re-verifies anyway through `target_path` shape/row checks.

Sources: [training_cache.py](morph2mol/training_cache.py#L10-L49), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L44-L63), [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L42-L66), [full_coverage.py](morph2mol/full_coverage.py#L64-L76), [embed_scgpt.py](train/embed_scgpt.py#L61-L125)

> [!TIP]
> Stage-2 resume correctness depends on the coverage cache being *regenerable*: if you delete `cache/coverage/`, `CoveragePlan` recomputes partitions from the same seed equations, and `supervised_before` still matches the checkpoint. Never reuse a work-dir across corpora though — the `cached_arrays` signature will correctly refuse, and so will `run_contract`.

## Reproducibility Mechanics: RNG and Identity Chains

Reproducibility here means *bit-level continuation*, achieved through a layered chain of hashes and RNG captures. At process start, both stages seed Python, NumPy, and all CUDA generators from the fixed recipe seed, and stage 1 creates a dedicated `torch.Generator(manual_seed=1)` that drives sampler shuffling independently of global RNG. At every checkpoint, `capture_rng_per_rank` snapshots `random`, NumPy, and torch CPU/CUDA states per rank, using `dist.all_gather_object` in DDP so all ranks' states are stored together; `restore_main_rng` reinstalls the exact per-rank state after resume, validating world-size equality first.

The identity chain then closes every loophole:

| Hash | Computed over | Detects |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `manifest_sha256` | `MANIFEST.csv` bytes | Corpus content changes |
| Split-set checks | `splits/*.txt` membership rules | Split rearrangement, duplicate IDs |
| `gene_hash` | JSON-serialized gene list | Gene-head reordering |
| `data_identity.cache_sha256` | Per-slide metadata + path-array lengths | Data order or completed-cache changes |
| `init_hash` | Sorted trainable tensors + tower state dicts | Different initialization (e.g., changed weights file) |
| `stage1_identity.sha256` | Stage-1 checkpoint file bytes | Any byte-level stage-1 difference |
| `coverage_revision` / `resume_revision` | Literal version strings | Algorithm-version drift between runs |

Because `check_checkpoint` compares the entire `run_contract` dict (which embeds the resolved dataset path and all split ID sets), and `check_recipe` compares every recipe-relevant CLI argument, the resume gate collectively proves: same corpus, same splits, same genes, same data order, same initialization, same world size, same hyperparameters — before a single tensor is loaded.

Sources: [training_resume.py](morph2mol/training_resume.py#L156-L176), [training_contract.py](morph2mol/training_contract.py#L7-L49), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L130-L163), [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L124-L138)

## Failure Semantics: What Refuses to Resume

The design philosophy is fail-loud: every resume-invalidating condition raises immediately with the offending key. The table below maps each failure condition to its check site and error, which doubles as a troubleshooting guide.

| Condition | Detected by | Error surfaced |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Corpus/split membership changed | `check_checkpoint` via `run_contract` | `Checkpoint training split differs from the current corpus` |
| Any of 15 (or 23) recipe args changed | `check_recipe` | `Resume training recipe differs: {key}` |
| DDP world size differs | explicit comparison | `Stage-1 resume requires the original DDP world size` / `RNG checkpoint world size differs` |
| UNI2-h weights file differs → new init | `init_hash` comparison | `Stage-1 initialization differs from the saved run` |
| Data order or per-slide cache changed | `data_identity` inequality | `Stage-1 data order/cache identity changed` |
| Effective cells or epoch budget changed | cursor `total_steps` recomputation | `Stage-1 effective cell count or total epoch budget changed` |
| Gene-head order differs (stage 2) | `gene_head_sha256` | `Checkpoint gene-head order differs from this run` |
| Coverage plan logic changed | `coverage_revision != REVISION` | `Resume coverage plan/count differs from the checkpoint` |
| Cache directory reused with new inputs | `cached_arrays` signature check | `Stale training cache; use a fresh cache directory` |
| Missing scGPT embeddings at resume | `target_path` | `Missing scGPT embeddings: {path}` |
| Stage-1 checkpoint not a completed run | `step != args.steps` gate | `Initialize expression training with a completed three-epoch scGPT Stage-1 checkpoint` |

Each epoch additionally runs a **coverage audit**: stage 1 all-reduces the per-rank supervised count and demands it equal `len(dataset)` exactly once per cell; stage 2 demands `seen == epoch * coverage.cells` at each epoch boundary. These invariants turn silent data-loading bugs (duplicated or dropped cells) into immediate failures rather than subtly biased models.

Sources: [training_resume.py](morph2mol/training_resume.py#L106-L153), [training_cache.py](morph2mol/training_cache.py#L20-L37), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L206-L211), [stage2.py](morph2mol/training/stage2.py#L202-L208), [stage1.py](morph2mol/training/stage1.py#L19-L28)

## Practical Resume Workflow

Operationally, both entry points expose identical resume flags. `--save-every` defaults to 500 steps for stage 1 and 5,000 for stage 2, and `--resume <path>` points at any prior checkpoint from the *same stage*. The documented contract: resume restores "weights, optimizer state, and data position; use the same world size and corpus when resuming."

| Flag | Stage 1 default | Stage 2 default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--save-every` | 500 steps | 5000 steps | Trigger also fires at final step |
| `--resume` | empty | empty | Path to same-stage checkpoint |
| `--chunk` | 256 (must divide 2048) | n/a | Changing it changes `accumulation` → recipe check fails |
| `--workers` | 8 | 8 | Loader parallelism only; does not affect determinism |

A typical interruption/recovery sequence looks like:

```bash
# After preemption — resume stage 1 from the latest periodic snapshot:
torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=3 train/train_phase1.py \
  --dataset /data/corpus --work-dir /runs/morph2mol \
  --uni2h /models/uni2h --cell-embeddings /runs/scgpt_cells \
  --resume /runs/morph2mol/checkpoints/alignment/stage1_step1500.pt

# Resume stage 2 from its rolling snapshot (same world size, same work-dir):
torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=3 train/train_phase2.py \
  --dataset /data/corpus --work-dir /runs/morph2mol --uni2h /models/uni2h \
  --stage1 /runs/morph2mol/checkpoints/alignment/stage1_final.pt \
  --resume /runs/morph2mol/checkpoints/expression/stage2_last.pt
```

Three practical rules follow from the verification design. First, **never edit the work-dir contents between interruption and resume** — the cache signatures and data identity will detect and reject any drift. Second, the checkpoint filename encodes the step, but the cursor inside is authoritative; stage 2's rolling file means you always resume from the newest state, while stage 1's numbered files let you pick an earlier point deliberately. Third, caches make interactive-scale re-runs cheap by design — deleting `checkpoints/` while keeping `cache/` reconstructs training from scratch in minutes rather than hours, since all crop decoding, mask normalization, target materialization, and per-epoch partitioning skip the expensive build paths.

Sources: [_entry.py](train/_entry.py#L16-L27), [training.md](docs/training.md#L58-L97), [training_cache.py](morph2mol/training_cache.py#L20-L37)

## Where This Fits in the Pipeline

Resume and caching are the reliability substrate beneath both training stages, but each stage has its own semantic story: the data contracts verified here are introduced in [Training Data Contracts](13-training-data-contracts), the stage-1 objective and gradient caching appear in [Stage 1 Contrastive Alignment](14-stage-1-contrastive-alignment), and the stage-2 coverage plan's spatial semantics are detailed in [Stage 2 Expression Training](15-stage-2-expression-training). When training completes, the same checkpoints flow into [Model Export and Release Packaging](17-model-export-and-release-packaging), where `check_stage2_settings` re-validates the recipe against the Morph2Mol-25M release profile before anything ships.


# Model Export and Release Packaging



This page documents how Morph2Mol turns training checkpoints into a portable, self-contained release directory that inference machines can consume without access to the training corpus. The export process is **verification-first**: before a single byte is written, checkpoints are checked against the frozen 25M recipe, stage lineage, and gene ordering; after everything is written, the assembled directory is re-opened and validated exactly as a downstream consumer would. We cover the release directory anatomy, the `export_release.py` pipeline, the hash-based integrity contract, the `release.json` manifest, and the two-phase packaging workflow used when a reference bank and fusion gate are involved.

## Why a Self-Contained Release Directory

The release layer is designed around a strict portability principle: *"Portable release paths and identities. No training corpus is required at inference"* ([release.py](morph2mol/release.py#L1)). Everything a prediction machine needs — the frozen vision tower, LoRA adapters, decoder weights, gene vocabulary, retrieval bank, and fusion gate — lives inside one directory, addressed exclusively by **relative paths** recorded in `release.json`. Checkpoints written during export contain only inference tensors: the docstring of `export_weights` states it saves *"inference tensors without optimizer state or training-machine paths"* ([export_release.py](train/export_release.py#L11-L12)).

The schema field in the manifest guards against version drift. A release is only accepted if its schema is `morph2mol-release-v1` or the legacy alias `voice25m-release-v1`; anything else raises `Unsupported release.json schema` ([release.py](morph2mol/release.py#L11-L12)). The legacy alias mirrors the `Voice25M = Morph2Mol` compatibility shim in the inference model ([model.py](predict/model.py#L71-L72)), so older analysis scripts keep working against new releases.

Sources: [release.py](morph2mol/release.py#L1-L12), [export_release.py](train/export_release.py#L11-L12), [model.py](predict/model.py#L71-L72)

## Release Directory Anatomy

A complete release, as documented in the weights README and produced by the exporter, contains the following layout:

```text
morph2mol/
  release.json          # manifest: relative paths + sha256 pins
  stage1.pt             # stripped Stage-1 LoRA adapters
  stage2.pt             # Stage-2 LoRA + inp + se2 + head tensors
  gene_space.npz        # ordered gene symbol vocabulary
  xenium_genes.tsv      # optional Xenium panel subset
  beta.json             # per-gene/per-stratum fusion weights
  beta.meta.json        # gate fitting metadata (hashes, K, tau)
  beta/                 # per organ/width weight files + manifest
  uni2h/                # frozen UNI2-h vision tower (e.g. pytorch_model.bin)
  bank/                 # reference bank: model.json, summaries/...
```

The layout is documented verbatim in the weights README ([README.md](weights/README.md#L7-L27)), and each entry below maps to the exact statement in the exporter that writes it.

| Artifact | Role | Written by | Integrity anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
| `release.json` | Manifest: relative paths + sha256 map | `main()` | schema check + `sha256` block |
| `stage1.pt` | `{'lora': ...}` only — no optimizer state | `export_weights` | `stage1_identity.sha256` inside `stage2.pt` |
| `stage2.pt` | `lora`, `inp`, `se2`, `head` + frozen recipe args | `export_weights` | recipe freeze + `gene_head_sha256` |
| `gene_space.npz` | Ordered gene symbols for the expression head | byte-for-byte copy | `gene_head_sha256` |
| `uni2h/` | Frozen vision tower directory | `copytree` | loaded by name at inference |
| `bank/` | Cluster retrieval summaries + `model.json` | `copytree(symlinks=False)` | `model.json` identity fields |
| `beta.json` / `beta.meta.json` | Gate weights + fitting provenance | `copy2` (sibling pair) | 5-of-7 cross-checks in `Release` |
| `xenium_genes.tsv` | One gene symbol per line, no header | generated from npz | gene-order semantics |

Sources: [README.md](weights/README.md#L7-L27), [export_release.py](train/export_release.py#L27-L62)

## The Export Pipeline

`train/export_release.py` is a standalone script with a deliberately small CLI: `--uni2h`, `--stage1`, `--stage2`, `--space`, `--out` are required; `--bank`, `--beta`, and `--xenium-space` are optional ([export_release.py](train/export_release.py#L36-L40)). The full flow is:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["python train/export_release.py ..."] --> B{"--out directory empty?"}
    B -- "no" --> X1["ValueError: Export directory must be empty"]
    B -- "yes" --> C["export_weights(stage1, stage2, space, out)"]
    C --> C1["Load both checkpoints on CPU"]
    C1 --> C2{"Stage-2 args match Morph2Mol-25M recipe?"}
    C2 -- "no" --> X2["ValueError from check_stage2_settings"]
    C2 -- "yes" --> C3{"stage1_identity.sha256 == sha(stage1 file)?"}
    C3 -- "no" --> X3["ValueError: initializer differ"]
    C3 -- "yes" --> C4{"gene_head_sha256 == gene_hash(space genes)?"}
    C4 -- "no" --> X4["ValueError: gene order differs"]
    C4 -- "yes" --> W["Write stage1.pt, stage2.pt, gene_space.npz"]
    W --> D["copytree uni2h/"]
    D --> E{"bank xor gate supplied?"}
    E -- "only one" --> X5["ValueError: Supply both --bank and --beta"]
    E -- "both" --> F["copy bank/, beta.json, beta.meta.json"]
    E -- "neither" --> G["skip retrieval artifacts"]
    F --> H["optional: xenium-space to xenium_genes.tsv"]
    G --> H
    H --> I["Write release.json with sha256 map"]
    I --> J["Release(out, retrieval=bool(bank))"]
    J --> K["print resolved release path"]
```

The single most important step is `export_weights` ([export_release.py](train/export_release.py#L11-L33)). It performs three validations before writing anything. First, `check_stage2_settings(second['args'])` compares every training hyperparameter recorded in the Stage-2 checkpoint against the frozen `stage2_settings()` recipe — any mismatch on any key aborts with the exact offending key ([recipe.py](morph2mol/recipe.py#L36-L40)). Second, the Stage-2 checkpoint's embedded `stage1_identity['sha256']` must equal the streaming SHA-256 of the supplied Stage-1 checkpoint file, proving the expression model was initialized from *this* alignment checkpoint ([export_release.py](train/export_release.py#L21-L22)). Third, `gene_head_sha256` must equal `gene_hash()` of the gene symbols loaded from the gene-space file, pinning head-column order to vocabulary order ([export_release.py](train/export_release.py#L23-L25)).

Only then are the artifacts written. The exported `stage1.pt` is reduced to just `{'lora': first['lora']}`. The exported `stage2.pt` keeps `['lora','inp','se2','head']` and adds `args=vars(stage2_settings())` (re-serialized from the frozen recipe, not from the checkpoint), `step`, `gene_head_sha256`, and — critically — a **recomputed** `stage1_identity={'sha256': sha(out/'stage1.pt')}` pointing at the *exported* Stage-1 file rather than the original training checkpoint ([export_release.py](train/export_release.py#L27-L32)).

> [!TIP]
> The `stage1_identity` inside the exported `stage2.pt` is hashed against the *exported* `stage1.pt`, not the original training checkpoint. Since the export strips `stage1.pt` down to LoRA tensors only, its bytes (and therefore its hash) differ from the training file — the exporter recomputes the hash after writing so downstream validation in `predict/model.py` will pass against the release-local file.

After writing, `main()` copies the UNI2-h tower, enforces bank/gate pairing (`bool(a.bank) != bool(a.gate)` is rejected), copies the bank with `symlinks=False` so the release contains real bytes rather than dangling links, and requires the gate's `beta.meta.json` to sit next to `beta.json` via `with_suffix('.meta.json')` ([export_release.py](train/export_release.py#L49-L55)). Finally the manifest is assembled with a `sha256` map over `stage1`, `stage2`, `gene_space`, and the directory is handed to `Release(out, retrieval=...)` for a full cold-start validation before the script prints the path ([export_release.py](train/export_release.py#L61-L65)).

Sources: [export_release.py](train/export_release.py#L11-L68), [recipe.py](morph2mol/recipe.py#L36-L40), [README.md](weights/README.md#L33-L46)

## The Integrity Contract: Hashes and Cross-Artifact Identity

Three hashing primitives underpin the entire release contract:

| Primitive | Location | Definition | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sha(path)` | `morph2mol/retrieval.py` | Streaming SHA-256 in 8 MiB blocks | File-level pins in `release.json`, checkpoint identity |
| `gene_hash(genes)` | `morph2mol/training_contract.py` | SHA-256 of `json.dumps(list(genes))` | Order-sensitive gene-vocabulary identity |
| `fingerprint(value)` | `morph2mol/bank_io.py` | SHA-256 of `json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True)` | Bank cache fingerprint (`cache_fingerprint`) |

Sources: [retrieval.py](morph2mol/retrieval.py#L16-L21), [training_contract.py](morph2mortraining_contract.py#L39-L40), [bank_io.py](morph2mol/bank_io.py#L30-L31)

Note that `gene_hash` serializes the *ordered list* — it is not a set hash, so a permuted gene vocabulary produces a different digest and is rejected. This is what makes the head-column ordering contract enforceable at export time *and* at inference time.

The `Release` class is the contract's enforcer. Given a directory, it loads `release.json`, resolves each declared path, and fails fast with `FileNotFoundError` naming the missing artifact ([release.py](morph2mol/release.py#L13-L20)). It then recomputes the three file hashes and compares them to the manifest's `sha256` block; a mismatch aborts with `Release checksum mismatch: <key>` ([release.py](morph2mol/release.py#L21-L26)).

For releases with retrieval enabled, seven cross-artifact identity checks run as a single conjunction — if *any* fails, the entire release is rejected with `Model checkpoints, genes, reference bank and fusion weights do not match`:

| # | Field in bank / gate metadata | Must equal | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `bank['checkpoint_sha256']` | `hashes['stage1']` | Bank features were encoded with this Stage-1 model |
| 2 | `bank['gene_space_sha256']` | `hashes['gene_space']` | Bank panels index this exact vocabulary |
| 3 | `gate_meta['checkpoint_sha256']` | `hashes['stage1']` | Gate was fitted against this Stage-1 model |
| 4 | `gate_meta['stage2_checkpoint_sha256']` | `hashes['stage2']` | Gate calibration used this expression model |
| 5 | `gate_meta['gene_space_sha256']` | `hashes['gene_space']` | Gate gene indices match this vocabulary |
| 6 | `gate_meta['cache_fingerprint']` | `bank['cache_fingerprint']` | Gate calibration used the same bank cache |
| 7 | `gate_meta['gate_sha256']` | `sha(gate file)` | The gate file itself is unmodified since fitting |

Sources: [release.py](morph2mol/release.py#L27-L39), [fit_beta.py](train/fit_beta.py#L91-L99)

Two protocol checks follow: if the gate metadata records a `spatial_context` protocol, it is validated against the current prediction protocol ([release.py](morph2mol/release.py#L40-L42)), and the retrieval settings must agree — `gate_meta['K']` and `gate_meta['tau']` must equal the bank's `retrieval_K` and `tau` (both fixed at 50 and 0.03 in the builder) or the release is rejected ([release.py](morph2mol/release.py#L43-L45), [bank_builder.py](morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L93-L100)).

> [!TIP]
> These checks mean a release is not a bag of files but a **hash-connected identity graph**: mutating any one artifact breaks at least two independent edges. This is also why the exporter refuses to write into a non-empty directory — partial or stale files could otherwise satisfy some checks while masking an inconsistent combination.

The identity relationships can be read as a graph over artifacts:

```mermaid
graph LR
    S1["stage1.pt"] -- "sha256" --> RJ["release.json sha256 map"]
    S2["stage2.pt"] -- "sha256" --> RJ
    GS["gene_space.npz"] -- "sha256" --> RJ
    S2 -- "stage1_identity.sha256" --> S1
    S2 -- "gene_head_sha256" --> GS
    BK["bank/model.json"] -- "checkpoint_sha256" --> S1
    BK -- "gene_space_sha256" --> GS
    BM["beta.meta.json"] -- "checkpoint_sha256" --> S1
    BM -- "stage2_checkpoint_sha256" --> S2
    BM -- "gene_space_sha256" --> GS
    BM -- "cache_fingerprint" --> BK
    BM -- "gate_sha256" --> BJ["beta.json"]
```

Sources: [release.py](morph2mol/release.py#L7-L46), [bank_builder.py](morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L93-L100)

## The release.json Manifest

The manifest is intentionally minimal — a schema tag plus relative paths, optionally a `sha256` block written by the exporter. The example configuration shows the full field set ([release.example.json](configs/release.example.json#L1-L10)):

| Field | Purpose | Written by exporter |
|---|---|---|
| `schema` | Always `morph2mol-release-v1` for new exports | yes (hard-coded) |
| `uni2h` | Relative path to vision tower directory | yes (always) |
| `stage1` / `stage2` / `gene_space` | Core model artifacts | yes (always), sha256-pinned |
| `xenium_genes` | Optional Xenium panel TSV | only with `--xenium-space` |
| `bank` / `gate` | Retrieval artifacts | only when both `--bank` and `--beta` are given |
| `sha256` | Map of file → digest for `stage1`, `stage2`, `gene_space` | yes (always) |

Only the four core fields plus (conditionally) `bank` and `gate` are *required* to exist at load time; `Release` resolves them and rejects missing artifacts ([release.py](morph2mol/release.py#L14-L20)). Because all values are relative to the release root, the directory can be moved or renamed without breaking anything.

Sources: [configs/release.example.json](configs/release.example.json#L1-L10), [release.py](morph2mol/release.py#L13-L20), [export_release.py](train/export_release.py#L46-L47)

## Two-Phase Packaging Workflow

The exporter supports an **intermediate release mode**: run it *without* `--bank`/`--beta` to produce a minimal release (tower + checkpoints + gene space + manifest) that downstream preparation tools consume. The weights README makes this explicit: *"Omit both `--bank` and `--beta` when exporting the intermediate checkpoints used by reference preparation during model training"* ([README.md](weights/README.md#L46)). Both consumers open it with retrieval disabled:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["train/export_release.py<br/>(no --bank/--beta)"] --> B["intermediate release<br/>Release(retrieval=False)"]
    B --> C["train/prepare_bank.py<br/>encode reference slides"]
    C --> D["morph2mol/bank_builder.py<br/>cluster + summarize bank"]
    B --> E["train/fit_beta.py<br/>fit fusion gate on references"]
    D --> F["bank/ + model.json"]
    E --> G["beta.json + beta.meta.json"]
    A2["train/export_release.py<br/>(full, final)"] --> H["complete release"]
    F --> A2
    G --> A2
```

`train/prepare_bank.py` documents this in its own CLI help — `--release` is *"Direct release from export_release.py (bank/gate not needed)"* ([prepare_bank.py](train/prepare_bank.py#L12)) — and constructs `Release(a.release, retrieval=False)` ([prepare_bank.py](train/prepare_bank.py#L26)). It stamps every per-object `feature_meta.json` with the Stage-1 hash and feature protocol, and the bank builder later elevates those identities into `model.json`'s top-level `checkpoint_sha256` / `gene_space_sha256` — the very fields check #1 and #2 verify against ([bank_builder.py](morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L88-L99)). `train/fit_beta.py` likewise opens the intermediate release without retrieval and records the full identity tuple (`checkpoint_sha256`, `stage2_checkpoint_sha256`, `gene_space_sha256`, `cache_fingerprint`, `gate_sha256`) into `beta.meta.json`, which becomes the other half of the final release's integrity web ([fit_beta.py](train/fit_beta.py#L28-L32), [fit_beta.py](train/fit_beta.py#L91-L99)).

This phased design means the expensive bank-building and gate-fitting runs happen against a *hash-pinned* model snapshot: if any checkpoint changes mid-pipeline, the intermediate release's hashes change, and the final full export fails loudly rather than silently mixing artifacts from different training runs.

Sources: [README.md](weights/README.md#L46), [prepare_bank.py](train/prepare_bank.py#L12-L26), [fit_beta.py](train/fit_beta.py#L28-L32), [bank_builder.py](morph2mol/bank_builder.py#L88-L99)

## Consuming a Release at Inference

The released model class re-validates the same invariants at construction time, independent of the CLI: it compares `stage2`'s embedded `stage1_identity['sha256']` against `release.hashes['stage1']`, re-checks `gene_head_sha256` against the loaded gene space, and re-applies the recipe freeze before building the encoder ([model.py](predict/model.py#L21-L29)). This defense-in-depth means even a hand-edited `release.json` that passed file-hash checks would still be caught if the internal checkpoint identities disagree.

One subtlety worth knowing when reading exported tensors: Stage-2 saves *only the trainable LoRA subset*, while frozen adapters still come from Stage-1 — the constructor loads Stage-1 LoRA with `complete=True` first, then overlays the Stage-2 subset ([model.py](predict/model.py#L33-L46)). The training-side loader enforces the same subset discipline via `load_lora_checked` ([training_contract.py](morph2mol/training_contract.py#L68-L78)). A practical consequence: `stage1.pt` in a release is never optional, even though Stage-2 alone defines final behavior.

For the downstream side of this contract — how releases are verified after download or transfer, and how the CLI consumes `--release` — see [Release Integrity Verification](21-release-integrity-verification) and [Inference CLI Reference](3-inference-cli-reference). The bank and gate artifacts themselves are covered in [Reference Bank Construction](10-reference-bank-construction) and [Gated Fusion Weights](12-gated-fusion-weights).

Sources: [model.py](predict/model.py#L21-L48), [training_contract.py](morph2mol/training_contract.py#L68-L78)

## Packaging Checklist

To package a newly trained model, run the exporter as documented ([README.md](weights/README.md#L33-L46)):

```bash
python train/export_release.py \
  --uni2h /models/uni2h \
  --stage1 /runs/morph2mol/checkpoints/alignment/stage1_final.pt \
  --stage2 /runs/morph2mol/checkpoints/expression/stage2_last.pt \
  --space /runs/morph2mol/direct/gene_space_all.npz \
  --xenium-space /runs/morph2mol/direct/gene_space_xen.npz \
  --bank /runs/bank --beta /runs/beta.json \
  --out /models/morph2mol
```

| Failure you might see | Root cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Export directory must be empty` | Non-empty `--out` | Point at a fresh directory |
| `Checkpoint does not use the Morph2Mol-25M setting: key=...` | Checkpoint trained with non-recipe hyperparameters | Retrain or use the correct checkpoint |
| `Expression checkpoint and alignment initializer differ` | Stage-2 wasn't initialized from this Stage-1 file | Supply the matching Stage-1 |
| `Expression checkpoint and exported gene order differ` | `--space` doesn't match the checkpoint's head | Export with the training-time gene space |
| `Supply both --bank and --beta` | Only one of the pair given | Pass both, or neither |
| `Missing release artifact <key>` / `Release checksum mismatch` | Release directory altered after export | Re-export; never edit a release in place |
| `...bank and fusion weights do not match` | One of the 7 cross-checks failed | Rebuild bank/gate against this exact model |

Note the licensing constraint: the UNI2-h tower must be obtained under approved access and redistribution must follow its terms ([README.md](weights/README.md#L3-L3), [README.md](weights/README.md#L46-L46)).

Sources: [README.md](weights/README.md#L3-L46), [export_release.py](train/export_release.py#L44-L55)

With packaging covered, natural continuations are:

- **Verify a shipped release end-to-end**: [Release Integrity Verification](21-release-integrity-verification)
